name: Hadhrat Sarwar-e-Aalam Muhammad RasoolAllah ﷺ
biography:
The blessed birth of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ took place on Monday, 12th Rabi-ul-Awwal (according to some traditions, 9th Rabi-ul-Awwal), in 571 AD, the year of the Elephant. He was born in Makkah to Hadhrat Abdullah and Hadhrat Aminah, and his birth marked the arrival of the beloved Messenger of Allah Ta’ala and the leader of both worlds. For the first few days, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ was fed by his blessed mother, after which he was nursed by Thuwaybah and then by Haleemah Sa’diyah RadhiAllahu Anha. It was the custom of the noble families of Quraysh to send their children to the countryside for a short period, and Haleemah Sa’diyah RadhiAllahu Anha was honoured with caring for the young Muhammad ﷺ. Her household was greatly blessed after his arrival. At around two years of age, a remarkable incident took place when two angels came to Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, opened his blessed chest and washed his heart. At the age of six, his beloved mother passed away, and he was then cared for by his grandfather Abdul Muttalib. Two years later, his grandfather also passed away, and his uncle Abu Taalib took responsibility for him. As Allah’s Messenger ﷺ grew older, his noble character became increasingly known. By the age of twenty-five, the people of Makkah called him Al-Ameen, meaning “the trustworthy”. Hadhrat Khadeejah-tul-Kubraa RadhiAllahu Anha heard of his honesty and employed him to take a caravan to Syria. After witnessing his exceptional character, she proposed marriage to him, and Allah’s Messenger ﷺ accepted. At the age of forty, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ began experiencing true and beautiful dreams and would often spend time in the Cave of Hira. Then Hadhrat Jibreel Alayhis Salaam came with the first revelation and commanded him, “Read!” This marked the beginning of Wahi and his mission as the final Messenger of Allah Ta’ala. Hadhrat Khadeejah RadhiAllahu Anha comforted Allah’s Messenger ﷺ when he returned home, reassuring him that Allah Ta’ala would never abandon a person of such noble character. In the early days, he ﷺ invited people to Islam privately. Hadhrat Khadeejah RadhiAllahu Anha was the first woman to accept Islam, while Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique RadhiAllahu Anhu was the first adult male. Hadhrat Ali RadhiAllahu Anhu was the first male child to accept Islam. After three years, Allah Ta’ala commanded His Messenger ﷺ to openly invite people towards Islam. The Quraysh responded with increasing hostility, mocking and harming Allah’s Messenger ﷺ and persecuting the early Muslims. Despite the suffering, he ﷺ remained patient and continued calling people towards Islam. As the persecution increased, some Muslims migrated to Abyssinia. Later, the Muslims were subjected to a three-year boycott. Ten years after the first revelation, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ suffered the loss of his beloved wife Hadhrat Khadeejah RadhiAllahu Anha and his uncle Abu Taalib. Due to the immense sadness caused by their deaths, that year became known as Aam-ul-Huzn, the Year of Sadness. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ then travelled to Taif with Hadhrat Zayd bin Haarith RadhiAllahu Anhu to invite its people towards Islam. They rejected his message and treated him harshly, but he ﷺ continued to show patience. Around this time came the miraculous journey of Mi’raaj. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ was taken from Makkah to Masjid Al-Aqsa on Buraaq, where he led the Prophets Alayhimus Salaam in

Salaah. He was then taken through the heavens and granted an extraordinary station of nearness to Allah Ta’ala. During this journey, the five daily prayers were made obligatory upon the Ummah. When the people of Makkah mocked Allah’s Messenger ﷺ after hearing about Mi’raaj, Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique RadhiAllahu Anhu immediately believed him without hesitation. From this, he became known as As-Siddique. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ continued inviting the tribes of Arabia towards Islam, and eventually people from Yathrib, later known as Madeenah, accepted Islam and pledged to support him ﷺ. The Muslims were instructed to migrate, and eventually Allah’s Messenger ﷺ also made Hijrah with Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique RadhiAllahu Anhu. The Quraysh had planned to kill Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, but Allah Ta’ala protected him. He ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu took refuge in the Cave of Thawr for three days. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu became concerned for their safety, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ reassured him: “Laa tahzan, innallaha ma’anaa” — “Do not fear; indeed Allah is with us.” They eventually reached Madeenah, where Allah’s Messenger ﷺ was welcomed with immense happiness. He ﷺ stayed initially at Quba and then entered Madeenah, where Masjid-un-Nabawi was established and the Muslim community began to flourish. In the second year after Hijrah, the Qiblah was changed towards the Ka’bah, fasting in Ramadhaan became obligatory, and permission for Jihad was given. The Muslims subsequently faced several major battles, including Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, Khaybar, the conquest of Makkah and Hunayn. Islam continued to spread throughout Arabia. In the tenth year after Hijrah, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ performed his Farewell Hajj. During his Khutbahs, he emphasised the rights of Muslims, the protection of their lives and wealth, the rights of women, and holding firmly to the Book of Allah Ta’ala. On the Day of Arafah, Allah Ta’ala revealed that the Deen had been perfected and His favour upon the believers had been completed. During his final illness, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ suffered from severe fever and weakness. When he was unable to lead the Salaah himself, he instructed Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique RadhiAllahu Anhu to lead the Muslims. Eventually, on Monday, 12th Rabi-ul-Awwal, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ passed away from this world, with his blessed head resting in the lap of Hadhrat A’ishah Siddiqah RadhiAllahu Anha. The passing of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ was the greatest loss suffered by the Ummah. His mission, however, had been completed, the Deen had been conveyed, and his Companions RadhiAllahu Anhum carried his message forward and spread Islam throughout the world. Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raaji’oon.

name: Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique RadhiAllahu Anhu
biography:
Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique RadhiAllahu Anhu was born one year and eight months after the Year of the Elephants. Traced back seven generations, his lineage meets that of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ. He was eighteen years old when he began keeping the company of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ.

Hadhrat Ibn Abbaas RadhiAllahu Anhu states that the verse from Surah Al-Ahqaaf, “Hattaa idhaa balagha ashuddahu wa balagha arba’eena”, was revealed to extol the excellence of Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique RadhiAllahu Anhu. When he was twenty years old, he travelled with Allah’s Messenger ﷺ to Syria on business. During the journey, they rested beneath a jujube tree near the residence of a Darwesh from the People of the Book. The monk asked who was sitting beneath the tree. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu identified him as Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib ﷺ, the monk declared that he was a Prophet and that nobody had sat in the shade of that tree since Eesa Alayhis Salaam. From that day, the monk’s words remained engraved upon the heart of Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu developed immense love for Allah’s Messenger ﷺ and kept his company as much as possible. When Allah’s Messenger ﷺ reached the age of forty, Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu was thirty-eight years old and embraced Islam. Before the Prophethood of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ was announced, Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu had a dream in which a great, radiant light descended upon the Ka’bah, spread throughout Makkah, and eventually entered his house. A Jewish priest dismissed the dream, but years later, during a journey, another monk interpreted it by saying that Allah Subhana Wa Ta’ala would send a Prophet and that Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu would be his close companion during his lifetime and later become his Khaleefah. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu has the great honour of being the person who embraced Islam without taking even a moment to consider his decision. He accepted the message immediately when it was presented to him by Allah’s Nabi ﷺ. He was also the first adult male to embrace Islam. Through his invitation, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, Sa’ad bin Abi Waqqaas, Uthmaan bin Affaan, Zubayr bin Al-Awwaam and Talhah bin Ubaydullah RadhiAllahu Anhum embraced Islam. After accepting Islam, Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu was never separated from Allah’s Nabi ﷺ and accompanied him on every journey and expedition unless otherwise instructed. His presence was greatly beneficial to the Muslims and the spread of Islam. During the early days of Islam, when the poorer Muslims were severely persecuted by the disbelievers of Makkah, he purchased the freedom of many Muslim slaves, including Hadhrat Bilaal and Hadhrat Aamir bin Fuhayrah RadhiAllahu Anhuma. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu spent his wealth generously in the path of Allah. On the day he embraced Islam, he possessed forty thousand dinars, which he spent on Allah’s Messenger ﷺ. At the time of his Hijrah from Makkah to Madeenah, he had five thousand dinars and spent the entire amount on Islam and the Muslims. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ greatly praised Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu. He stated that he had not benefited from anyone’s possessions more than those of Abu Bakr and that Abu Bakr’s favours to him would be repaid by Allah Subhana Wa Ta’ala. He also stated that Abu Bakr was more virtuous in this Dunya and the Hereafter, that he would be the first of his Ummah to enter Jannah, and that if he were to take a Khaleel other than Allah, it would be Abu Bakr. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ further described him as the most compassionate person towards his Ummah and praised what was in his heart. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu was also the companion of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ in the cave during the Hijrah. When the command for Hijrah came, Jibreel Alayhis Salaam informed

Allah’s Messenger ﷺ that Abu Bakr would be his companion. The Qur’an also refers to him as the second of the two who were in the cave. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu was the first Khaleefah after Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, a Mubashshir bil Jannah, and Afdhal-ul-Bashar ba’d al-Anbiyaa — the best of mankind after the Prophets. Hadhrat Ali RadhiAllahu Anhu stated, “The one who brought the truth was Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, and the one who testified to it was Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu.” When Allah’s Messenger ﷺ was approaching his passing, he instructed Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu to lead the Muslims in Salaah. He led the people in prayer for five days during the lifetime of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ. This was an indication to the Muslims of his suitability for Khilaafah. After the passing of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, everyone agreed upon the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu. Hadhrat Umar RadhiAllahu Anhu was the first to make Bay’ah, followed by Abu Ubaydah RadhiAllahu Anhu and then the remaining Companions who were present. Hadhrat Ali and Hadhrat Zubayr RadhiAllahu Anhuma also acknowledged his superiority, mentioning that he was the Companion of the Cave and that Allah’s Messenger ﷺ had appointed him to lead the people in Salaah during his lifetime. In his first address as Khaleefah, Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu said that he had been made their leader despite not considering himself better than them. He instructed the people to assist him when he did good and correct him when he made mistakes. He also emphasised that truthfulness was a trust and falsehood was treachery. He later stated that he had never desired leadership and felt that an unbearable weight had been placed upon his shoulders. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu was extremely firm in following the Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ. When the expedition of Usaamah bin Zayd RadhiAllahu Anhu, which had been commissioned by Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, was suggested to be postponed because of the difficulties facing the Muslims, Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu refused, saying that he would rather die than stop something initiated by Allah’s Messenger ﷺ. The army was therefore dispatched. Similarly, when some tribes refused to pay Zakaah while continuing to perform Salaah, Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu firmly ordered that they be fought if they did not retract their position. Hadhrat Umar RadhiAllahu Anhu initially advised leniency, but after hearing Abu Bakr’s firm response, he realised that Allah Subhana Wa Ta’ala had opened his heart to the truth. During his Khilaafah, the fitnah of Musaylimah the Liar, who had claimed Prophethood in Yamamah, was also crushed. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu dispatched Hadhrat Khalid RadhiAllahu Anhu against his army. After many days of fighting, Musaylimah was killed by Wahshi RadhiAllahu Anhu. Another great achievement of Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu was the collection of the Qur’an into one place. Following the Battle against Musaylimah, many reciters and Huffaaz of the Qur’an were martyred. Hadhrat Umar RadhiAllahu Anhu feared that portions of the Qur’an could be lost and advised that it be collected. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu appointed Zayd bin Thaabit RadhiAllahu Anhu, one of the original scribes of revelation, to undertake this task. The Qur’an was collected from the leather pieces, palm leaves and other materials upon which it had been written, and the completed collection was kept with Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu before later passing to Hadhrat Umar RadhiAllahu Anhu.

Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu remained Khaleefah for two years and seven months. Following the passing of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, he became increasingly weak due to his extreme sadness at the separation. On the 7th of Jumad al-Aakhir 13 Hijri, after taking a bath in cold water, he developed a fever which worsened. Near the time of his passing, he asked Hadhrat A’ishah Siddeeqah RadhiAllahu Anha about the clothing in which Allah’s Messenger ﷺ had been shrouded. Upon learning that the Prophet ﷺ had been shrouded in three white pieces of cloth, he instructed that he too be shrouded in his own clothes, even though they were old and worn. During his final illness, Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu advised Hadhrat Salmaan Farsi RadhiAllahu Anhu to take from the Dunya only what was necessary and to remember the importance of fulfilling one’s pact with Allah. When the Companions asked him to appoint a successor, he appointed Hadhrat Umar RadhiAllahu Anhu, stating that he would tell Allah Subhana Wa Ta’ala that he had appointed the best person alive from His creation. Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu passed away between Maghrib and Isha on the 22nd of Jumad al-Aakhir 13 Hijri, at the age of sixty-three. He was buried next to Allah’s Messenger ﷺ in the Hujrah of Hadhrat A’ishah RadhiAllahu Anha. In accordance with his instruction, his wife Asmaa bint Umays RadhiAllahu Anha washed him, while Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu poured the water. Hadhrat Umar RadhiAllahu Anhu led the Janazah Salaah with four Takbeers. His blessed head was placed in line with the shoulders of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, and Hadhrat Umar, Hadhrat Uthmaan, Hadhrat Talhah and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan RadhiAllahu Anhum lowered him into his blessed grave. —

name: Hadhrat Salmaan Farsi RadhiAllahu Anhu
biography:
Hadhrat Salmaan Farsi RadhiAllahu Anhu was born into a wealthy Zoroastrian family in Persia but spent much of his life sincerely searching for the truth. He first followed the religion of Moosa Alayhis Salaam and later Christianity, serving various Christian priests and enduring great hardship with patience and steadfastness. Eventually, he came to Madeenah and accepted Islam, entering the blessed companionship of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, who later secured his freedom. Hadhrat Salmaan RadhiAllahu Anhu participated in many battles and played an important role in the Battle of the Trench. When the Muhajireen and Ansar disputed over which group he belonged to, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ declared that Salmaan was from the Ahl-ul-Bayt, among the companions of the Suffah, and among those for whom Jannah eagerly awaits. During the Khilafah of Hadhrat Umar RadhiAllahu Anhu, he was appointed governor of Madaa’in. Despite receiving an allowance from the Bayt-ul-Maal, he gave it in charity and lived an extremely simple life. He had little interest in worldly possessions and would even carry people’s goods himself, refusing to let his position as governor create pride or distance between him and ordinary people. He strongly warned against accumulating wealth unnecessarily and emphasised that wealth spent according to Allah’s Hukm would benefit a person on the Day of Qiyamah, whereas wealth not used correctly would become a burden. His humility was also evident when someone

insulted him. Rather than becoming angry, he feared that the person’s criticism might actually describe his shortcomings. Near the end of his life, he wept because he feared that his few worldly possessions might prevent him from meeting Allah’s Messenger ﷺ in the Hereafter. His possessions consisted only of basic everyday items. Before his passing, he instructed his wife to perfume the area around him, saying that visitors from a realm beyond men and jinn were about to arrive. He then passed away peacefully in Madaa’in on 10 Rajab 33 Hijri. The account also mentions the karamaat of Hadhrat Ali RadhiAllahu Anhu, who is reported to have travelled from Madeenah to Madaa’in in one night to perform his ghusl before returning. A narration in Jaami’ Tirmidhi further highlights Hadhrat Salmaan’s wisdom: he taught Hadhrat Abu Dardaa’ RadhiAllahu Anhu that one’s Nafs, Lord, guests and family all have rights that must be fulfilled, and Allah’s Messenger ﷺ affirmed that Salmaan had spoken correctly.

name: Hadhrat Qasim Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu
biography: Hadhrat Imam Qaasim bin Muhammad RadhiAllahu Anhu had a spiritual nisbat with Hadhrat Salmaan Farsi RadhiAllahu Anhu. He was raised in the household of his paternal aunt, Hadhrat A’isha Siddeeqah RadhiAllahu Anha, and through the companionship of Imam Zayn-ul-’Aabideen RadhiAllahu Anhu, he also acquired nisbat with Hadhrat Ali RadhiAllahu Anhu. His family connection to the Ahl-ul-Bayt was also significant. During the conquest of Persia, Hadhrat Ali RadhiAllahu Anhu received three daughters of the Persian king, all of whom accepted Islam. One married Imam Hussain RadhiAllahu Anhu and became the mother of Imam Zayn-ul-’Aabideen; another married Hadhrat Abdullah bin Umar RadhiAllahu Anhu and became the mother of Hadhrat Saalim; and the third married Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abi Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu and became the mother of Hadhrat Qaasim RadhiAllahu Anhu. Hadhrat Imam Qaasim RadhiAllahu Anhu was a unique and outstanding personality of his time and was regarded as a great light among the Taabi’een and Fuqahaa. Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa’eed RadhiAllahu Anhu said that he had never seen anyone in his time whom he considered better than Qaasim bin Muhammad. Hadhrat Umar bin Abdul Azeez Rahmatullah Alayhi also held him in such high regard that he said if he had the choice of selecting a Khalifah, he would choose Imam Qaasim. During his final days, the Imam instructed his companions to bury him in the same clothes he wore for prayer, consisting of his Qamees and Izaar. When his son questioned whether two pieces of cloth were too many, he reminded him that Hadhrat Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu was also shrouded in three pieces and explained that the living have greater need for new clothing than the deceased. Hadhrat Imam Qaasim RadhiAllahu Anhu passed away at the age of seventy-two in Qudayd, a place between Makkah and Madeenah. Historians differ regarding the exact year of his passing, with some recording 106 Hijri and others 108 Hijri.

name: Hadhrat Imam Ja’far Sadiq Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Imam Ja’far Saadiq RadhiAllahu Anhu was the son of Imam Muhammad Baagir RadhiAllahu Anhu and the grandson of Imam Zayn-ul-’Aabideen RadhiAllahu Anhu. His maternal grandfather was Imam Qaasim bin Muhammad bin Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu, through whom he acquired inner knowledge, as well as from his father. He said, “Waldati Abu Bakr marratayn,” meaning that he had been born twice to Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu: physically through his maternal grandfather, Qaasim bin Muhammad bin Abu Bakr RadhiAllahu Anhu, and spiritually through the inner knowledge he acquired from that lineage. He was given the title Saadiq because of his truthfulness. He was born in Madeenah Munawwarah in 80 Hijri and belonged to the auspicious Ahl-e-Bayt. His lineage was Imam Ja’far Saadiq bin Imam Muhammad Baagir bin Zayn-ul-’Aabideen bin Imam Hussain bin Ali al-Murtadhaa RadhiAllahu Anhum. Among his students were Imam Abu Haneefah Rahmatullah Alayhi, Yahya bin Sa’eed Ansari Rahmatullah Alayhi, Ibn Jareeh, Imam Maalik Rahmatullah Alayhi, Muhammad bin Ishaaq, Moosa bin Ja’far and Sufyaan Yameenah. Muslim scholars were agreed upon the auspicious Imamat of Imam Ja’far Saadiq RadhiAllahu Anhu. Umar in al-Magdoom described him as possessing the qualities worthy of the family of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, with excellent inner and outward conduct, knowledge, dignity, beauty, piety and chastity. He lived for some years in Madeenah Munawwarah, where people benefited greatly from his presence, and later went to Iraq, where he resided for a considerable period. Hadhrat Da’ood Tai Rahmatullah Alayhi once asked the Imam for advice, saying that his heart had become black. The Imam reminded him that the matter was not based upon lineage, but upon the actions through which Allah Ta’ala is pleased with a person. Hearing this, Hadhrat Da’ood Tai Rahmatullah Alayhi wept considerably. When Hadhrat Sufyan Thawri Rahmatullah Alayhi asked the Imam for advice, he said that a liar could never be good-natured, an envier could never achieve peace of mind, and an ill-mannered person could never be a true leader. He further advised that one who wants to be an ‘Aabid should remain safe from Haraam, and one who wants to be a Muslim should be content with whatever Allah Ta’ala has written and destined. He advised against sitting in the company of habitual sinners, as their company would affect a person and lead them towards sin, and said that advice should be taken from those who spend their lives in obedience to Allah Ta’ala. The Imam stated that a person who does not control their tongue lives in regret. He also said that as a person develops love and longing for Allah Ta’ala, they begin to distance themselves from creation. He explained that some sins can bring a person closer to Allah Ta’ala when they cause genuine regret and repentance, while some acts of worship can take a person away from Allah Ta’ala when they make a person arrogant about their deeds. On one occasion, a man lost a purse containing one thousand dinars and accused the Imam, who he did not recognise, of stealing it. The Imam asked how many dinars were in the purse, took the man to his house and gave him one thousand dinars. When the man returned home, he found his purse there. He returned to the Imam, apologised and offered to return the money, but the Imam told him to keep it, saying that they never take back what they have given away.

The man later discovered that he had been speaking to Imam Ja’far Saadiq RadhiAllahu Anhu and was overcome with embarrassment and regret. The Khaleefah Mansoor once intended to have the Imam assassinated. He instructed that the Imam should be killed when he removed his topi. However, when Imam Ja’far Saadiq RadhiAllahu Anhu was brought before him, Mansoor stood up in awe and then became unconscious. He remained unconscious for twenty-one days. When he regained consciousness, he explained that he had seen the Imam accompanied by a huge dragon-like creature with its mouth wide open, and he feared that it would eat him if he caused the Imam any harm. The Imam’s humility was such that, while accompanied by those who served him, he once suggested that they should all ask the person among them who had been pardoned to intercede for the rest of them. When his companions said that he did not need their intercession because he was an intercessor for creation, he replied that he was ashamed of his actions, especially when thinking about presenting them before his Lord. On another occasion, the Imam saw people gathered around a dead cow while an old lady wept beside it. She explained that the cow had died and asked how she would manage without it. The Imam asked whether she would like Allah Ta’ala to bring the cow back to life. When she agreed, he kicked the cow and it immediately came back to life. The Imam then disappeared into the crowd so that nobody would recognise him. Imam Ja’far Saadiq RadhiAllahu Anhu was unmatched in his knowledge of Tafseer during his time. Imam Abu Haneefah Rahmatullah Alayhi stated that among the people of knowledge, he had not seen anyone more knowledgeable in matters of Fiqh than Imam Ja’far bin Muhammad. Imam Maalik Rahmatullah Alayhi observed that the Imam’s complexion would turn pale whenever Allah’s Messenger ﷺ was mentioned in his presence. He would not relate Ahadeeth unless he was in a state of wudhu. Whenever Imam Maalik Rahmatullah Alayhi saw him, he found him engaged in one of three things: Salaah, sitting in silence, or reciting the Qur’an. He described the Imam as a scholar of Shariah and exceptionally compassionate by nature. Imam Ja’far Saadiq RadhiAllahu Anhu passed away at the age of sixty-eight in Madeenah Munawwarah on 15 Rajab 148 Hijri. He was buried in Jannat-ul-Baqi by the blessed graves of other members of the Household of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ.

name: Hadhrat Bayazeed Bistaami Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was born in the year 136 Hijri. The grandfather of the Shaykh had converted to Islam from Zoroastrianism. The spiritual upbringing of the Shaykh was by Hadhrat Imam Ja’far Saadiq radhiallahu anhu, but since the Shaykh was born after Hadhrat Imam had passed away, the Shaykh never actually saw Hadhrat Imam radhiallahu anhu during his lifetime. The Shaykh’s grandparents were from Bistaam, and his mother used to say, “If I ate anything doubtful during my pregnancy, I felt sick and would not feel better until I had vomited.” The Shaykh was still a child when he started going to school and learning to read. One day he came across the phrase, ‘Be grateful to Allah and be grateful to your parents.’ The Shaykh spoke to

his mother, saying, “How can I fulfil the rights of Shukr in relation to both?” His mother replied, “I shall not hold you to my rights, and put you in Allah’s protection.” It was after this that the Shaykh left Bistaam for the wilderness of Syria, where he spent thirty years occupied in devotions and mujahidaat. When the Shaykh stood for Salaah, a loud rattling noise from the Shaykh’s chest bones could be easily heard by anyone near him. Once a person asked the Shaykh, “Who is your Shaykh?” He replied, “An old woman.” The person asked how that could be and the Shaykh related, “When I was living in the wilderness, I once saw an old lady carrying some heavy items. She sought my help and asked me to carry her load for her. I pointed at a lion which came running and carried the woman’s load. I asked her how she would explain to the people of the city that her load was being carried by a lion. She replied, “I will tell the people that I met an oppressor.” I asked, “How is that?” She replied, “Tell me, does this lion have a choice as to whether or not it should carry my burden?” I replied, “It does not have a choice.” She then said, “So if you inflict a burden upon creation that Allah has not ordained for it, then tell me, are you an oppressor or not? My case is also supported by the fact that you wish the people of the city to know that this lion is obedient to you and that you possess karamaat.” It has been related that the Shaykh travelled on foot to the house of Allah in Makkah, prostrating after every footstep and thus taking twelve years to get there. The Shaykh stated, “This Court cannot be likened to the courts of the kings of this Dunya.” The Shaykh did not go to Madeenah Munawwara that year, saying, “It would be against Adab. Insha’allah, next time I will come with the intention of Ziyarat.” On this journey, people began following him in huge numbers. The Shaykh was desperate to avoid attention and wanted the people to leave him alone. He tried his best to get away from them but couldn’t, so after one prayer, he recited a verse, “Inni anallah laa ilaha illa ana fa’budoon.” When the people heard this they began saying, “This man is mad,” and left him alone. On one journey, the Shaykh had loaded his luggage along with that of his mureeds on one camel. Someone saw this and said, “Look how this poor camel has been overloaded.” The Shaykh replied, “Look carefully.” When the person looked closely, he saw that the luggage was floating one hand span above the camel, which could therefore not feel any weight. When he saw this, he said, “Subhanallah! What is this?” The Shaykh replied, “If I keep my state hidden from you, you curse me, and when I make things known to you, you do not have the strength to cope with it.” The Shaykh stated, “Once I spoke to Allah subhana wa ta’ala in a dream. I said, ‘O Allah! How can I reach You?’ Allah subhana wa ta’ala said, ‘By leaving your Nafs.’” The Shaykh also stated, “All that I have achieved in life is due to the fadhal of Allah; I have achieved nothing from my own efforts or worship.” On another occasion, he said, “One day I received Ilham and heard a voice saying, ‘O Baayazeed! Offer something better than the worship that you do at the moment, and bring Me that which you cannot find in My Court.’ I asked, ‘O Allah! What is there that is not in Your Court?’ I had the reply in Ilham: ‘Helplessness, humility, dependence and defeat.’” The Shaykh’s Taqwah was such that on his way back from Makkah Mukarramah, he stopped at Hamdaan and bought a Safflower tree sapling. When the Shaykh arrived in Bistaam, he noticed that a few insects had come with the sapling and said, “I have exiled these insects from their homeland.” He then took the insects back to Hamdaan before returning to Bistaam.

Once, the Shaykh was in the Jami’ah Masjid when he pierced his staff into the earth. He did this at a spot that was close to where another Shaykh had similarly fixed his staff. The Shaykh’s staff then fell over, and in doing so knocked over the staff of the other Shaykh, who had to bend down to pick it up. The Shaykh felt very bad about this and followed the man out of the Masjid after the prayer and said, “Please forgive me for the discomfort that I have caused you.” The Shaykh used to say, “Your mother’s pleasure is a very great thing indeed. Through serving her, a person can acquire what he can never get through devotional worship and mujahidaat.” The Shaykh explained this, saying, “One night, my mother asked me for drinking water. There was no water at home so I had to go to a spring that was some distance away. When I returned a while later, I found my mother sleeping. I did not wish to disturb her so I stood by her side all night long, holding the water container in the severe cold, in case she should wake up and ask for water. When my mother finally woke up, she saw me and noticed that the water vessel had stuck to my hand because of the cold; she then prayed for me.” The Shaykh’s next-door neighbour was a fire-worshipper, and once he went away on a journey. He left his wife and young child at home. When the darkness of the night fell, the child would cry loudly because of the dark. The Shaykh therefore put a lantern on the wall so that their house would get some light and the child could play and remain happy. When the neighbour returned from his journey, his wife told him about this. The neighbour was so impressed and moved by the good conduct of the Shaykh that he embraced Islam as a result. The state of the Shaykh’s absorption was such that everyday he would ask the name of a mureed that had been in his company for twenty years. One day, the mureed asked, “Hadhrat I have been in your service for twenty years. Why do you still ask my name?” The Shaykh replied, “The fact is that since His Name has come into my heart, I have forgotten all others.” Once, some people praised a person that they considered to be saint. The Shaykh decided that he too would go and meet this person for blessing. When the Shaykh got there, he noticed the man spit in the direction of the Qibla. The Shaykh returned without meeting him, saying, “If he was a man of Tareeqah, he would never have been so disrespectful.” The Shaykh used to say, “If you see a person levitating in the air or displaying what looks like a miracle, do not be impressed with it unless he is steadfast upon the Shari’ah of Allah and the Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.” Once, on his travels, the Shaykh prayed behind an Imam at a Mosque. The Imam noticed that the Shaykh was staying around for a while, so he asked, “Tell me, what arrangements have you made regarding eating?” The Shaykh said, “Be patient while I repeat my prayer, after which I shall answer you.” After praying, the Shaykh said, “Salaah is not valid behind a person who does not recognise the Provider of his Rizq (sustenance).” Once a person asked the Shaykh, “Please tell me about the state of your Mujaahidah.” The Shaykh replied, “If I were to tell you about something significant, you will not be able to comprehend it, nor do you have the strength to understand it. For this reason I shall tell you about one of the minor mujahidas of my life. Once my Nafs did not obey me, so I kept it thirsty by depriving it of drinking water for one whole year.” Once a person came to the Shaykh seeking advice and said, “Please give me advice through which I can be pardoned.” The Shaykh replied, “There are two things that will be enough for you. Firstly, remember that Allah is always aware of your situation, and that no matter what you

do, He sees it. Secondly, you should know that your Lord is in no way dependant on your actions.” One day someone requested the Shaykh to give him a piece of cloth from his Qamees as a blessing. The Shaykh replied, “Even if you were to wear my clothes, they would not benefit you unless you made your actions like mine.” The Shaykh also stated, “True men are those whose hearts are only for Allah subhana wa ta’ala.” The Shaykh passed away at Bistaam on the 15th of Sha’baan, 261 Hijri. Later someone saw the Shaykh in a dream and asked him what happened to him after he died. The Shaykh replied, “Allah subhana wa ta’ala asked me, ‘Old man! What have you brought for Me?’ I replied, ‘O Allah! You know well that when a Faqeer goes into the Court of a king, the king does not say, ‘What have you brought for me?’ Instead, he asks, ‘What would you like?’”

name: Hadhrat Abul Hassan Khurqaani Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The nisbat of the Shaykh was with Hadhrat Sultaan-ul-‘Aarifeen Baayazeed Bistaami rahmatullah alayhi, and this nisbat was established through the Owaysi method (a direct spiritual link, with no physical association). This is because the Shaykh was born some time after Baayazeed Bistaami rahmatullah alayhi had passed away. The Shaykh was a guiding light and an ideal example for the people of Tareeqah and Haqeeqah. The Shaykh had a great status in Ma’rifat (spiritual insight) and in his knowledge of Tawheed, and he is one of those saints that possessed great vision and Mushaahidah (witnessing of the unseen). The Shaykh was to be found more often than not in a state of absorption. Long before his birth, Shaykh Baayazeed rahmatullah alayhi used to visit the graves of the martyrs at Dahistan every year. On the way, he used to come to a halt near Khurqaan, where he would stand and breathe as if he were trying to smell something. His Mureeds would say, “Hadhrat, we cannot smell any fragrance. What do you sense?” Shaykh Baayazeed rahmatullah alayhi would reply, “I smell the fragrance of a great man who will emerge from this land of thieves. His name will be Ali and his family name Abul Hasan. He will exceed me in three areas, namely, he will have a heavy responsibility in respect of his wife and children, he will plough the land and he will be a planter of trees.” After Hadhrat Khwajah Abul Hasan rahmatullah alayhi first set out on the Path, for twelve consecutive years he would pray the Isha prayer in congregation and would then go to the blessed shrine of Sultaan-ul-‘Aarifeen Baayazeed rahmatullah alayhi, where he would put his attention on that blessed Rooh and would stand and wait all night in anticipation of an opening for blessings. He would pray, “O Allah! Grant Abul Hasan a little of what you have given to your beloved Baayazeed.” And then he would pray the Fajr prayer in congregation, with the same wudhu’ of the previous night’s Isha. On one occasion, seven days passed without a meal being served at the Shaykh’s Khanqah. After the seventh day of hunger, a man appeared at the Khanqah bringing with him some flour and a goat, and he called out, “I have brought this food for the Sufis.” The Shaykh addressed those that were present, saying, “Whosoever is a Sufi, let him take the food; I myself do not

have the courage to make the claim of being a Sufi.” In the end the man had to return with the food he had brought. Once a person came to Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi and said, “Grant me the Khurqah (robe of initiation).” The Shaykh said, “First, tell me, if a woman was to dress in the clothes of a man, would it make her a man?” The man replied, “No, she wouldn’t become a man.” The Shaykh then replied, “Then what is the benefit of wearing the Khurqah? If you are not a suitable person to whom the Khurqah can be given, then what is the point of wearing it?” Once, a person came with the intention of visiting the Shaykh. He found his way to the Shaykh’s house. The Shaykh was out and his wife replied from the house. She was very harsh in the way she spoke, saying, “Go away! Why would you want to meet that liar and zindiq (atheist) anyway?” The man turned away, thinking, ‘What quality can there be in someone who is rejected by his own wife?’ As he was thinking this and walking away, he saw Hadhrat Shaykh coming towards him carrying a bundle of wood while mounted on a lion. The man was astonished by the sight before him and thought, ‘His wife has said one thing and what I see before me is another.’ Hadhrat Khwajah knew what was in his heart and spoke to him, saying, “So long as you continue to bear the burden that your wife puts upon you, the lion will continue to bear your burden.” It has been related that the Sultan of the time, Mahmood Ghaznawi, once came to visit the Shaykh, but the Shaykh did not show him the respect that the rulers of the age expected. Mahmood met the Shaykh and said, “Give me advice.” The Shaykh replied, “Take care regarding a few matters. Abstain from forbidden things, pray Salaah in congregation, and show kindness and affection towards the creation of Allah.” Mahmood said, “Please pray for me.” The Shaykh said, “O Mahmood! May your ending be praiseworthy.” After this, Mahmood presented the Shaykh with a purse of gold coins as a gift. The Shaykh in turn presented Mahmood a chapatti made from barley and told him to eat it. Mahmood tried eating it but found it very difficult to swallow. The Shaykh said, “Is my chapatti getting stuck in your throat?” Mahmood replied, “Yes, it is sticking in my throat.” The Shaykh replied, “In just the same way, your gold coins stick in my throat.” Before leaving, Mahmood said, “Please give me a sign to remember you by”, so the Shaykh gave him a Qamees. When the time came for the King to leave, the Shaykh got up and saw him out. The King asked, “When I came, you paid no attention and carried on as normal, but now that I am leaving, you are showing me much respect. Can I ask why this is the case?” The Shaykh replied, “That is because you came here with the arrogance of a King, but you are leaving with the humbleness of a Faqeer.” It has also been related that some time later, when King Mahmood laid siege to the city of Sawmnaat, he realised that he was fighting a losing the battle. He immediately went and, holding the Qamees that Hadhrat rahmatullah alayhi had given him as a gift, prayed to Allah, saying, “O Allah! Through the waseelah of this Qamees, Please grant me victory.” Thereafter Allah subhana wa ta’ala granted him victory. The same night, Mahmood saw Hadhrat rahmatullah alayhi in his dream, who addressed him, saying, “O Mahmood, you did not appreciate my robe. Had you prayed ‘O Allah! Convert all these kuffaar into Muslims!’ then indeed they would all have embraced Islam!” On one occasion, a Mureed of the Shaykh expressed his desire to travel to Lebanon to see the Qutb-e-Aalam (Pole of the World) of that time. The Shaykh gave him permission to do so. When the mureed arrived in Lebanon, he saw a huge gathering of people sitting before a Janazah, but

no prayer was taking place. The mureed asked someone, “Why are the people just sitting and not performing the Janazah prayer?” The person replied, “We are waiting for the Qutb-e-Aalam, for he leads all five of the daily prayers.” Some time later, everybody suddenly got up and formed rows. The mureed related, “I realised that the Imam must have arrived, and then the Janazah prayer took place. The Imam left immediately after the prayer and I did not catch a glimpse of his face, so I asked the people ‘Who was the person who led the prayer?’ They replied ‘That was the Qutb-e Aalam, and his name is Abul Hasan Khurqaani.’ As soon as I heard this, I began to cry in the realisation that despite being a mureed of the Shaykh, I was unaware of his great status and that he was the Qutb-e-Aalam of the age.” On one occasion, Shaykh Abu Sa’eed rahmatullah alayhi and many others came to meet the Shaykh. There was not enough food in the house, so the Shaykh told his wife to throw a cloth over the chapattis and keep taking them out one by one from underneath it. She did this and found that every time she pulled out a chapatti, it was not the last. The people of the gathering continued to eat and the chapattis continued to be served. When everyone had eaten, the Shaykh’s wife removed the cloth from the chapattis. The Shaykh said to his wife, “If you had not removed the cloth, the provision of chapattis from beneath it would not have stopped until the day of Qiyamah.” The Shaykh once stated, “A person does not become a Sufi by walking around with a prayer mat, by dressing in rags or by following customs. In fact, a Sufi is one who has destroyed his Nafs to such an extent that he does not feel his existence is significant.” He also stated, “Whatever one does for Allah’s sake is called ‘Ikhlaas’ (sincerity), and whatever one does for creation is ‘Riya’ (show).” Once he said, “I know not which is better,” and then followed this by saying, “That heart which is occupied in Allah’s remembrance.” On another occasion he said, “Keep your eyes moist with tears; this is because Allah subhana wa ta’ala befriends those who weep.” He also stated, “The successor to Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam is that person who followed and obeyed him, and not that person who displays his knowledge through extensive writing but does not act upon it in his life.” One of the Shaykh’s sayings was, “The most enlightened heart is that which has no room for the Dunya; and the best work is that which is not done with the fear of creation in mind; and the most lawful of ni’mats (favours) is that which you have attained through the most effort; and the best of friends is that person whose life is completely upon the Haq.” He also stated, “I have heard a voice from Allah saying to me, ‘O My servant! If you come to me with grief, I shall give you joy. If you come to me in a state of poverty and need, I shall grant you true wealth. And when you become completely helpless and dependant, I shall make the air and water obedient to your desire.’” Once he said, “There are three occasions when the angels have immense fear of the Awliya’allah; firstly, when they come to take his life; secondly, when they write down his actions; and thirdly when they come to him for questioning in the grave.” The Shaykh also stated, “There are some men of Allah who rest in the dark of their homes at night with blankets covering their faces, but at the same time they can clearly see the moon and the stars in the skies, and they can see the good actions and sins of the people and they can see the angels that bring provision to the people.”

When the time of the Shaykh’s death was near, he instructed his companions, saying, “Dig my grave thirty yards deep, for I do not wish to be buried at a higher place than my Shaykh Baayazeed rahmatullah alayhi.” This request was duly executed. The Shaykh passed away at Khurqaan in the year 426 Hijri, and that is where the blessed shrine of the Shaykh is situated.

name: Hadhrat Abul Qasim Gurgaani Rahmatullah Alayh
biography: The Shaykh’s blessed name was Ali bin Abdullah and his family name was Abul Qasim. His nisbat was with Hadhrat Shaykh Abul Hasan Khurqaani rahmatullah alayhi and he also had indirect nisbat, via three routes, with Hadhrat Junayd Baghdadi rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh was one of the greatest Awliya of his age and many karamat have been attributed to him. Hadhrat Daata Ganj Bakhsh Hajweri rahmatullah alayhi states, “I travelled to Toos in order to meet Hadhrat Abul Qasim rahmatullah alayhi, so that he could help me find the meaning of a waaqi’ah (event) that was very difficult for me to fathom. When I went into the company of the Shaykh, I found him alone in his Hujrah (study). He was looking at a pillar and explaining my waaqi’ah as if talking to it. I spoke and said, ‘Hadhrat, with whom are you conversing?’ The Shaykh replied, ‘O young man! At this moment in time Allah subhana wa ta’ala has made this pillar my companion; it has asked me a question and I am giving it an answer.’” Once, Hadhrat Shaykh Abu Sa’eed rahmatullah alayhi and Shaykh Abul Qasim rahmatullah alayhi were both sitting together on a platform in front of a gathering of Darweshes. One of the people present began to wonder what the status of these two men might be. He was just thinking this when Shaykh Sa’eed rahmatullah alayhi said, “If there is anyone who wishes to see two kings at the same time and at the same place, then let him come and look at this platform.” On hearing this, the Darwesh looked at them both and Allah removed all the veils from his sight; he beheld their status and he began to think in his heart that there was probably no saint on the earth with a greater status than them on that day. Shaykh Sa’eed put his attention on the Darwesh and said, “There is one small country where seventy thousand men just like Abu Sa’eed and Abul Qasim arrive every day, and seventy thousand others leave.” The Shaykh passed away on the 23rd of Safar 450 Hijri.

name: Hadhrat Abu Ali Faarmadi Toosi Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The blessed name of the Shaykh was Fadhal bin Muhammad bin Ali and the family name was Abu Ali. The Shaykh was from a village near Toos called Faarmad, and he had nisbat with Hadhrat Khwajah Abul Hasan Khurqaani rahmatullah alayhi and also with Shaykh Abul Qasim Gurgaani Toosi rahmatullah alayhi. In his earlier days, the Shaykh went to Nishapur to acquire formal religious knowledge. The Shaykh relates, “One day I heard that Shaykh Abu Sa’eed Abil Khayr had come to the town, so I went to see him. When I saw the Shaykh, I was overcome with love for him and after a short while I returned home. One day, I was sitting at home when all of a sudden I had a strong desire

to see Shaykh Abu Sa’eed rahmatullah alayhi again. Even though I was aware that Hadhrat Shaykh would not normally be out at this time, I nevertheless got up and walked outside. I had barely started walking in the street when I noticed the Shaykh going somewhere with his mureeds. I joined the group and walked along with them. Hadhrat Shaykh came to a gathering where Samaa’ (congregational invocation of Allah) was to start. During the Samaa’, the Shaykh fell into a powerful state of wajd (ecstasy) during which he tore his shirt into bits. When the Samaa’ ended, the Shaykh grabbed the torn-up sleeves and called out, ‘Where is Abu Ali Toosi?’ When I heard this, I thought he must be calling someone else with a similar name to mine, for the Shaykh did not know me. But when the Shaykh called out a third time, someone turned to me, saying, ‘The Shaykh is calling you.’ I got up and went to the Shaykh, who handed me the sleeves and said, ‘Take these and take good care of them.’ Thenceforth I kept them safely in my possession and reaped great benefits. They always emitted an extraordinary light. “After Shaykh Abu Sa’eed had left Nishapur, I went to Imam Abul Qasim Qushayri and told him my condition. The Imam told me to busy myself in my studies, but the light continued to increase. After spending three consecutive years acquiring knowledge, there came a day when I noticed a light coming from my pen and inkpot. I went to the Imam and related what I had experienced. The Imam said, ‘It is now time for you to halt your acquisition of outer knowledge and go to acquire the knowledge of Tareeqah.’ From that day I stayed at the Khanqah in the company of the Imam. One day the Imam was going to take a bath. I noticed this, so I filled up a couple of buckets of water and put them in the bathroom. When the Imam finished bathing, he asked, ‘Who put water in the bathroom?’ I stayed quiet out of fear that I had done something wrong. But when the Imam asked a third time, I stepped forward and confessed that it was me. Hadhrat Imam addressed me saying, ‘O Abu Ali! I have not gained in seventy years what you have obtained with just one bucket of water!’ I stayed in the company of the Imam, busy in mujahidah, until one day I was overcome by a state during which I lost all sense of myself. When I told the Imam about what had happened, he said, “O Abu Ali! This is beyond me.” I understood then that I was in need of a murshid who could take me beyond this stage. “I had heard of the excellence of Hadhrat Shaykh Abul Qasim Gurgaani, and so I went to the city of Toos in search of him. When I found the Shaykh, he was with his mureeds, sitting in muraqabah. As soon as I entered, the Shaykh raised his head from muraqabah and said, ‘O Abu Ali! What would you like? You have not yet reached any stage. You are in need of Tarbiyyah, after which you will achieve a great status.’ From then on, I sat on the company of the Shaykh and undertook a programme of mujahidaat and devotions. The Shaykh also gave me the hand of his daughter in marriage. “One day Abu Sa’eed Toosi was visiting, and he indicated that I ought to deliver speeches. Only a few days later, Shaykh Abul Qasim instructed me to start delivering sermons.” After this the Shaykh returned to Nishapur, where the effect of his talks became very evident. The Shaykh had a great number of followers and was accepted by the common people. People from far-off places used to come to the gatherings to listen to the Shaykh. He was also held in high esteem by many of the distinguished people of society, particularly the rulers of the time. The creation of Allah benefited greatly from the teachings of the Shaykh. The Shaykh passed away in the month of Rabi-uth-Thani in the year 477 Hijri at Toos, and that is where the blessed shrine of the Shaykh is located.

name: Hadhrat Yusuf Hamdani Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh’s nisbat was with Hadhrat Khwajah Abu Ali Faarmadi rahmatullah alayhi, but it has also been said that the Shaykh was indirectly a mureed of Shaykh Abul Hasan Khurqaani rahmatullah alayhi, and that he was given the Khurqah (robe of permission) by Shaykh Abdullah Chawpni rahmatullah alayhi and that he also sat in the company of Shaykh Hasan Samnaani rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh’s family name was Abu Yaqoob. From the age of 18, he benefited from travels to Baghdad, Isfahan, Iraq, Khurasaan, Samarqand and Bukhara, as well as other places. After acquiring much knowledge, the Shaykh began to benefit communities of Muslims by means of his sermons. He had exceptional knowledge regarding the rulings of Shari’ah and fatawa, and at the same time had one foot firmly planted in the field of spiritual knowledge. The great scholars and fuqaha of the time used to make a habit of acquiring the company of the Shaykh, and would join the huge gatherings that regularly took place. The Shaykh’s Khanqah was always full, and was more frequented by seekers of Allah than any other Khanqah of that age. Shaykh Abdul Qadir Jilani rahmatullah alayhi also acquired the company of Khwajah Yusuf Hamdaani rahmatullah alayhi. One day, Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi addressed Shaykh Abdul Qadir Jilani rahmatullah alayhi, who was still only a young man at the time, saying, “You should now begin to deliver sermons.” Abdul Qadir Jilani rahmatullah alayhi replied, “Hadhrat, I am an Ajami (non-Arab), so how can I speak in front of scholars and people who are masters of the language?” Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi said, “You are more than capable in all respects. Deliver sermons, for I see in you something that will one day raise your status to a very high level indeed.” One day, a woman came crying to the Shaykh and said, “My son has been abducted and taken away by enemies. Please pray that he returns safely.” The Shaykh replied, “Be patient; you will find your son at home.” When the woman returned to her house, she found that her son was already there. When asked how he had returned, he said, “I was being held captive when all of a sudden I saw a man appear before me, and in moments he rescued me and brought me here.” The woman went back to Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi and related the boy’s story. The Shaykh replied, “Why are you so amazed by Allah’s Hukm?” On one occasion, Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi was delivering a speech when two people from the audience called out saying, “Stop talking! You are an innovator.” The Shaykh turned to them and replied, “Be quiet!” At this, both men collapsed and died on the spot. A similar story is related about an occasion when the Shaykh was in Baghdad, where he used to deliver sermons. A scholar from the audience asked the Shaykh a for a legal ruling, to which the Shaykh replied, “Sit down; I smell kufr in your speech.” Some time later, it was discovered that this scholar had become a Christian and had died in that state. The madhab of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi was Hanafi. The Shaykh taught the Deen of Allah with steadfastness for over sixty years, and was widely regarded as one of the greatest men of the age. It was the Shaykh’s habit that he would not go out anywhere except on a Friday.

The Shaykh passed away on Monday the 22nd of Rabi-ul-Awwal in 535 Hijri at a place called Mauza’ Yami’een, when he was on a journey from Herat to Maru. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is at Maru.

name: Hadhrat Abdul Khaliq Ghajdwani Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
This Shaykh is the leader of the Naqshbandi Silsilah. He was a descendent of Imam Malik rahmatullah alayhi, and his mother was also descended from the kings of Rome. The Shaykh’s father, whose name was Abdul Jameel, was among the great scholars and Awliya of the age. His father had acquired the company of Khidhr alayhi salaam, and it was Khidhr alayhi salaam who had informed Imam Shaykh Abdul Jameel of the following: “You will have a son; name him Abdul Khaliq. I shall treat him as a son and give him nisbat from myself.” Due to the circumstances of the time, Imam Shaykh Abdul Jameel rahmatullah alayhi migrated from Roman territories to Mawralnahar, and took up residence at a place called Ghajdwan, near Bukhara. It was here that the blessed Shaykh Abdul Khaliq rahmatullah alayhi was born and spent his childhood. As he got older, he began to busy himself in acquiring knowledge in Bukhara. The Shaykh learned Tafseer from Hadhrat Badr-ud-din rahmatullah alayhi. One day when the Shaykh was reading up on the Tafseer of a verse, he came across advice to the effect that ‘You should call upon your Lord secretly and with tears. And He does not like those who transgress the limits.’ The Shaykh went to his respected teacher and asked, “What is the reality and method of this secrecy? I ask because if a dhaakir was to do dhikr aloud or to sway while doing dhikr, then anyone who saw him would know what he was doing. Yet if he does silent dhikr, then in accordance with the Hadeeth, Shaytaan will be aware of what he is doing because Shaytaan can circulate in a person in the same way as blood.” The teacher was astonished by this question and replied, “This relates to Ilm-e-Ludni (knowledge acquired by spiritual intuition). If Allah wills, you will learn this knowledge from the Ahl-ullah (the Folk of Allah).” After this incident, the Shaykh set out in search for a friend of Allah. While he was searching he met Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam. Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam said, “I am Khidhr, and I have taken you as a son.” Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam then taught the Shaykh Wuqoof-e-Adadi (to pause the dhikr on an odd number). In order to practise this, he told the Shaykh to go to a spring, immerse himself in the water and recite Laa ilaha illa llah Muhammad ur-Rasoolullah in his heart. The Shaykh carried out this instruction and busied himself in this practice, for Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam had informed him that doing so would open his heart up to the Israar (secrets). Indeed that was exactly what happened and much knowledge entered his heart. After some time, Hadhrat Khwajah Yusuf Hamdani rahmatullah alayhi visited Bukhara for a while. The Shaykh went to Hadhrat Yusuf Hamdani rahmatullah alayhi and gained the benefits of his company. This is why it has been stated that the Shaykh received Sabaq (training) from Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam and Sohbat (company) from Hadhrat Khwajah Yusuf Hamdani rahmatullah alayhi. Even though the dhikr taught by Hadhrat Khwajah Yusuf Hamdani rahmatullah was jahr (aloud), he did not forbid Hadhrat Abdul Khaliq rahmatullah alayhi from doing silent dhikr. In fact, he used to say, “Make sure you do dhikr in the manner that Hadhrat

Khidhr alayhi salaam has taught you.” Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah states that at the time he was twenty two years old. After some time, when Hadhrat Khwajah Yusuf rahmatullah alayhi left Bukhara and went to Khurasan, Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi busied himself in devotion and mujahidaat. Many people from Syria began to enter the Silsilah through the Shaykh and a Khanqah where the Shaykh could teach was established in that country. Regarding his meeting with Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam, the Shaykh relates, “I was busy at that time in searching for a man of Allah. One day, which happened to be a Friday, I was sitting at the gate of our garden when a weak and old looking man approached me from the street. I stood up for him and showed him full respect. The old man addressed me, saying, ‘O young man! I see in you the signs of sainthood. Have you made bay’ah yet?’ I replied, ‘I have been searching for a while.’ It was then that he said, ‘Young man! I am Khidhr and I have accepted you as a son.’ Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam taught me the Khafi dhikr that is known as Habs Nafs (Holding Breath).” The Shaykh would often weep profusely when in worship. Once some Mureeds of the Shaykh asked him, “Hadhrat, why is it that you cry so much, despite the fact that you are in a very good state?” The Shaykh replied, “I keep thinking of Allah’s independent decision. In this state, I feel that the time for my soul to depart is near, and I live in the continual fear that I may have done something unintentionally and without realising that may have been an action that Allah does not like.” Sometimes the Shaykh would look so worried and frightened that it looked as if he had just been sentenced to death. One day one of the people who served the Shaykh asked, “What is Faraaghat (disengagement/respite)?” The Shaykh replied “The Faraaghat of the heart is when there is no room for love of dunya in your heart. And Faraaghat is not distancing yourself from the daily duties that have to be carried out in this world.” The foundations of the Naqshbandi Tareeqah are based on the following instructions of the Shaykh: 1. Hosh dar dam – This means that not a single breath of a Saalik must be neglectful of Allah subhana wa ta’ala, just as Hadhrat Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi stated: “Do not even let one breath to go to waste.” 2. Nazr bar qadam – The Saalik should always guard his gaze. When he walks he should keep his focus on the ground in front of him and not look in various directions around him as he walks. 3. Safar dar watan – This means to leave bad habits and characteristics and adopt good qualities. 4. Khalwat dar anjuman – This means to be with the creation externally and to be with the Haq subhana wa ta’ala internally. Remember, this means to be busy in Allah’s dhikr at all times. 5. Baaz Gasht – This means that after doing the dhikr of Allah for a while, one should with great humility make du’a, saying, “O Allah! You are my goal and Your pleasure it is that I seek.” 6. Nigah Daasht – This means to block out odd thoughts and clear the mind from worldly thought at the time of doing dhikr.

7. Yaad Daasht – This means that a Saalik should always be attentive to Allah subhana wa ta’ala without needing any assistance, whether in the form of words or sound. In other words, he should be in a state of anticipation of Allah at all times. When a person is so engulfed in this state that he forgets his own existence, then that is what is called fanaa (annihilation). 8. Wuqoof-e-Zamaani – This means that the Saalik should always be aware of whether each breath is taken in remembrance or in neglect. 9. Wuqoof-e-Adadi – To take care to halt on an odd number during dhikr ‘Habs Nafs’. 10.Wuqoof-e-Qalbi – This means that the attention of the Saalik should always be on his heart. There was once a Majdhooba (enraptured) woman who used to walk the streets naked. People would ask her, “Why do you not wear any clothes?” She would reply, “From whom shall I do purdah? There are no men in this town.” One day she went to the shop of a Nan bread maker, climbed into in his clay oven and said, “Shut the lid over me. I wish to hide from a man who has come into this town.” A while later, some people tried to extract her from the Tandoor oven and she called out asking for her clothes. A set of clothes were brought for her and she came out of the oven unmarked by the fire. After she had dressed, the people asked her, “Which man has suddenly made you do purdah?” She replied, “Come with me and I will show you.” She led the people into the company of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh stood up in respect for her, and spoke to her for a few moments before parting. Once the Shaykh was with his companions on the journey for Hajj. During their journey, they ran out of water and became very thirsty. Eventually they arrived at a well, only to realise that it was dry. But no sooner had Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi approached the well and looked at it that it filled to the brim with water. All those who were present drank the water and performed wudhu. One person filled a vessel with water as a precaution, and as soon as he did this the water level went right back down into the depths of the well. When Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi found out about this, he said, “My friends did not put their trust in Allah, otherwise the water of this well would not have gone down till the day of Qiyamah.” Once the Shaykh gave some advice to his son Khwajah Awliya Kabeer rahmatullah alayhi, saying, “Make sure you fulfil the rights of Allah and his Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam and be aware of the rights of your parents. Never fail to recite the Qur’an while looking at it, regardless of whether you know it by heart or not. Keep away from ignorant Sufis and do not sit in the company of innovators. Never miss the congregational prayer. Never give up on the Mercy of Allah. Always remain between the states of fear and hope, sometimes fearing and sometimes hoping. Trust in Allah alone and do not expect any loyalty from creation. Singing (religious singing) is only good for one whose heart is alive and his Nafs is dead. Otherwise singing kills the heart. One who wishes to indulge should keep himself busy in prayer and fasting.” The Shaykh also said, “O Son, never ever be arrogant, for some day you will have to leave this world. Live your life in this world like a traveller. My son, remember this advice and act upon it, just as I listened to the advice of my Shaykh and acted upon it. If you do so, Allah will be your Protector in this world and the next. Insha’allah the person who follows all this advice will reach the true destination.”

Once, the Shaykh heard a Darwesh saying, “If I were given the choice between Heaven and Hell, I would take Hell because I have never fulfilled the desires of my Nafs. Paradise is a desire of the Nafs, whereas the Nafs hates the idea of going to Hell.” Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi said “What has man got to do with choice? It is the duty of the servant to go where he is sent and be pleased with where he has been kept. This is the true way for the slave of Allah to live.” Once the Shaykh was sat among his companions when a young man, wrapped in a shawl and with a prayer mat draped over his shoulders, came and sat down at one side. This young man then addressed the Shaykh, saying, “Can you explain to me the meaning of the Hadeeth of Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam ‘Fear the insight of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah’?” The Shaykh immediately replied, “The meaning is that you should break your zannaar (a religious waist-cord worn by polytheists) and bring it to me.” On hearing this, the man said, “A’audhubillah, how can I have a zannaar?” Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi nodded at one of his serving Mureeds, who got up and removed the piece of cloth that was covering the young man, and the zannaar that he was wearing came into view. On seeing this, the young man broke the cord and embraced Islam. Then the Shaykh addressed the people, saying, “Let us all break our zannaars and bring Iman into our lives, just as this new Muslim has done today. He has broken a physical and external thread, and we need to break a spiritual, internal thread so that we too can gain the forgiveness of Allah subhana wa ta’ala.” On hearing this, the people of the gathering were overcome and began to fall at the feet of the Shaykh in Tawbah (repentance). It has been related that at the time of the departure of the Shaykh from this Dunya, his sons and Mureeds were by his side. The Shaykh opened his eyes and said, “My friends, good news! Allah subhana wa ta’ala has given me the news that He is pleased with me.” The companions of the Shaykh began to cry and then the Shaykh said, “And there is good news for you too. Through Ilham (inspiration), Allah has informed me that every person who joins this Tareeqah and remains steadfast upon it till the Last Day will be blessed with His Mercy and forgiveness. Try your best to be steadfast and never separate from this Tareeqah.” A short while later a voice was heard reciting the verse: اَهُتَّيَأٰٓـَي ُةَّنِئَمْطُمْلٱ ۝ ِٓيعِجْرِإ ٰ ىَلِإ ِكِّبَر ًۭةَي ِاضَر ًۭةَّي ِضْرَّم O contented Nafs (soul)! Return unto thy Lord, pleased with Him and in His pleasure. (Surah al-Fajr, verse 27 to 28) After this, the soul of the Shaykh left this finite world. The Shaykh passed away on the 12th of Rabi-ul-Awwal 575 Hijri. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is situated at Ghajdwan. Sometime after the Shaykh had passed away, someone saw him in a dream, sitting on an enlightened throne below the ‘Arsh, surrounded by angels who were conveying to him salaam from Allah subhana wa ta’ala.

name: Hadhrat Khwaja Muhammad Aarif Reogari Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Hadhrat Khwajah Arif Reogari rahmatullah alayhi was the great Khalifah of Hadhrat Khwajah Abul Khaliq Ghajdwani rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh was honoured in that he spent the

whole of his life in the service of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi and benefited from that great company throughout his life. It would be impossible to define the amount of spiritual benefit that he received from his Shaykh during that time. It is well known that Hadhrat Khwajah Abdul Khaliq Ghajdwani rahmatullah alayhi had four major Khulafa. These were Khwajah Ahmad Siddique rahmatullah alayhi, Khwajah Auliya-e-Kabeer rahmatullah alayhi, Khwajah Sulayman Karmeeni and Khwajah Arif Reogari. The link to the Silsilah of Hadhrat Khwajah Baha’uddin Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi, however, goes back to Hadhrat Khwajah Arif Reogari rahmatullah alayhi. Hadhrat Arif Reogari rahmatullah alayhi was born at a place called Reogar which is approximately 18 miles from Bukhara. After Hadhrat Khwajah Abdul Khaliq Ghajdwani rahmatullah alayhi passed away, the Shaykh kept himself busy in guiding Allah’s creation. The Shaykh holds a great status in his knowledge, piety, Taqwah, devotion and worship. The level to which the Shaykh followed the Sunnah in his life was legendary. Every one of his actions used to be in accordance with the Sunnah. The Shaykh passed away in the month of Shawwal in the year 616 Hijri. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is at Reogar which is a small distance away from the city of Bukhara.

name: Hadhrat Mahmood Faghnawi Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was the most virtuous of the Khulafa of Hadhrat Khwajah Arif Reogari rahmatullah alayhi. Before passing away, Hadhrat Khwajah called for the Shaykh and gave him Khilafah and permission to undertake Da’wat-e-Khalq (inviting people to the Path). The Shaykh was born at a place near Bukhara called Mauza’ Anjeer Faghni. He later resided at Wahiknah from where he gave guidance and tarbiyyah to Allah’s creation. For the purpose of Da’wah, the Shaykh would teach the Jahr (loud) dhikr. He was the first Shaykh of this Silsilah to make loud dhikr; Hadhrat Khwajah Abdul Khaliq Ghajdwani and Hadhrat Khwajah Arif Reogari rahmatullah alayhum before him did not do loud dhikr. Some people began to complain and ask why the Shaykh had started loud dhikr since it was not the way of the Masha’ikh and opposed the way of the Silsilah. The Shaykh replied to these complaints, saying, “Hadhrat Khwajah, during his last days, instructed me to do loud dhikr. It seemed to me that Hadhrat Khwajah Arif rahmatullah alayhi told me to start loud dhikr in the manner that a person reminds someone to recite the kalimah aloud when they reach their last breath.” Hadhrat Khwajah Mahmood rahmatullah alayhi considered this to be permission for teaching loud dhikr. Hadhrat Khwajah Ramateeni rahmatullah alayhi, who was the Khaleefah of the Shaykh stated, “Once I did Ziyarah of Hadhrat Khidr alayhi salaam, and I asked him, ‘Which of the Masha’ikh of this day and age should one follow?’ He replied ‘Khwajah Mahmood.’” Hadhrat Ali Ramateeni rahmatullah alayhi also relates, “Once I was busy in dhikr with my companions, when suddenly we saw a white bird fly over us. It spoke, ‘O Ali! Remain busy in what you are doing.’ All the people in the gathering became unconscious on hearing the bird speak. When they regained consciousness, I informed them the bird was the Rooh of Hadhrat

Khwajah Mahmood Anjeer Faghnawi rahmatullah alayhi, for Allah gave him the power to take the form of any creature he desired.” Another event similar to this occurred in the life of the Shaykh. Khwajah Dahqan Qalbi rahmatullah alayhi, who was the first Khaleefah of Hadhrat Awliya Kabeer, was on his deathbed when he made du’a, saying, “O Allah! Send one of your friends to help me when I am dying, so that my end may be good and my Iman stay intact through his blessing.” His prayer was answered, for the Rooh of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi came to him when he was taking his last breaths, and he passed away in a good state. Hadhrat Khwajah Mahmood Anjeer Faghnawi rahmatullah alayhi passed away in the year 715 Hijri. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is in Anjeer Faghni.

name: Hadhrat Khwaja Azeezan Ali Ramateeni Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was one of the Khulafa of Hadhrat Khwajah Mahmood Faghnawi rahmatullah alayhi. When Hadhrat Mahmood’s last breaths were near, he appointed the Shaykh as his Khaleefah. The Shaykh was born at a place called Ramateen, and his title was ‘Azeezan’. The Shaykh lived for a while in Khwarizm, where he spent his time in worship and devotion. Many people became his followers during that time. It became a well-known fact that the Shaykh had acquired the company of Hadhrat Khidr alayhi salaam during this period. Once Hadhrat Samaasi rahmatullah alayhi, who was of similar age to the Shaykh, sent a message saying, “I have heard that Khidr alayhi salaam was responsible for your Tarbiyyah. Could you tell us more about this?” The Shaykh sent a reply, saying, “Khidr loves the Aashiqs of Allah subhana wa ta’ala.” Someone once asked him, “How do you define Iman?” The Shaykh replied, “Iman is breaking with creation and creating a tie with the Haq subhana wa ta’ala.” Once Shaykh Badr-ud-din rahmatullah alayhi asked the Shaykh, “When Allah mentions in the Qur’an, ‘O Ye who believe, remember Allah with abundant remembrance’, does ‘dhikran katheeran’ (abundant remembrance) refer to the dhikr of the tongue or the dhikr from the heart?” Hadhrat Shaykh replied, “For the Mubtidi (a beginner), it refers to dhikr of the tongue, and for the Muntahi (an accomplished dhaakir), it refers to dhikr of the heart. The Mubtidi has to try hard, with patience and endurance, whereas for the Muntahi, the dhikr reaches his heart and then all his organs, veins, arteries and joints begin to do the dhikr of Allah. It is at this point that a saalik becomes a possessor of dhikran katheeran; and a day’s effort by him is equivalent to a year’s effort by anybody else.” The Shaykh used to say, “Every night and day, Allah subhana wa ta’ala looks at the heart of the believer 360 times with the Gaze of Mercy. The heart has 360 doors that lead to the other parts of the body; these are the 360 veins and arteries. When the heart is affected by the dhikr and reaches the stage when it becomes worthy of the special gaze of Haq subhana wa ta’ala, then with that gaze, all the parts of the body are given provision through the heart, and all these parts of the body thereby become obedient; and when one is in obedience, a fayz (spiritual outpouring) in the form of light is formed, and this fayz reaches the heart. This is what is meant by Nadhr-e-Rahmat (the Gaze of Mercy).

The Shaykh also stated, “If any of the sons of Abdul Khaliq Ghajdwani rahmatullah alayhi were alive today, Mansoor Hallaj would have been saved from crucifixion.” He also said, “Behave in a very humble manner in front of the friends of Allah, so that they may pray for you.” On another occasion, the Shaykh stated, “Consider the person in whose company you forget Allah to be Shaytaan. In fact, he is worse than Shaytaan because Shaytaan only whispers thoughts into your mind, whereas man does the same but openly in conversation.” Once a person came into the service of the Shaykh and said, “Hadhrat, please do not forget about me.” The Shaykh replied, “Go to the bazaar, buy a bowl and bring it back to me as a gift.” He did as instructed, upon which the Shaykh said, “Now whenever I look at it I shall remember you.” Another of his sayings was “Greatest care should be taken at the time of eating and the time of talking.” The Shaykh related that “Once Hadhrat Khidr alayhi salaam came to Khwajah Abdul Khaliq Ghajdwani rahmatullah alayhi, who served him with two chapattis. When Hadhrat Khidr alayhi salaam excused himself from eating them, Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi said, ‘They are Halaal - do eat.’ Hadhrat Khidr alayhi salaam replied, ‘it is true that this food is Halal, but the person who made the dough was not in wudhu.’” The Shaykh also stated, “A Murshid should administer Tarbiyyat (education) to his mureeds in accordance with their potential and ability.” On another occasion he said, “When the servant remembers Allah subahana wa ta’ala, Allah rewards him with three things, namely Tawfeeq, the dhikr of Allah and the honour of acceptance before Allah subhana wa ta’ala.” The Shaykh published a magazine in which he wrote ten conditions for the Saalik. These were as follows: Purity, silence, solitude, fasting, dhikr, abstinence from sin, seeking the pleasure of Allah, company of the Pious, the night prayer (tahajjud) and eating halal food. The Shaykh had two sons. One was Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad and the other was Hadhrat Khwajah Ibraheem rahmatullah alayhima. When the Shaykh was in his last days, he called for his son Hadhrat Khwajah Ibraheem rahmatullah alayhi and appointed him as his successor. Some people began to think that it was not right that the Shaykh had appointed his younger son as the Khaleefah, while the elder son also lived in the vicinity. The Shaykh noticed this and said, “Khwajah Muhammad will soon come to meet me.” It came to pass that the Shaykh’s elder son indeed passed away only nineteen days after the Shaykh himself. Hadhrat Khwajah Azeezan rahmatullah alayhi passed away on Monday the 28th of Dhil Qa’da in the year 721 Hijri, and he was one hundred and thirty years old at the time. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is in Khwarizm.

name: Hadhrat Muhammad Baba Samaasi Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was one of the Khulafa of Hadhrat Ali Azeezan Ramateeni rahmatullah alayhi. He was born at a place called Samaasi which is a few miles from Ramateen. When Hadhrat Azeezan rahmatullah alayhi was in his last days, he called all his companions and appointed Hadhrat Baba rahmatullah alayhi as his Khaleefah, and instructed the rest of his mureeds to follow him and come into his service.

The state of the Shaykh’s absorption and selflessness was such that when chopping trees in his garden, he would often become lost within himself before he managed to complete the task of cutting the branch. Whenever the Shaykh passed by the area of Kawshak Hindwan, he used to say, “I smell the fragrance of a true man of Allah from this earth.” And when the Shaykh went there on one occasion, he said, “It seems to me that the birth of that man has now taken place.” On the day he made this pronouncement, Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi was only three days old. The grandfather of Hadhrat Baha’uddin Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi took him to Hadhrat Baba Samaasi rahmatullah alayhi, and when the Shaykh saw the child he said, “This is our son, and I accept him as my son.” Then the Shaykh turned to his companions and said, “The fragrance that I used to refer to came from this man.” Then he addressed his distinguished Khaleefah Hadhrat Sayyid Ameer Kalaal rahmatullah alayhi and said, “Under no circumstances must the Tarbiyyah of this son of mine be deficient in any way; if it should be so, I shall never forgive you.” Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi states, “Once after a meal, Hadhrat Baba rahmatullah alayhi gave me a Naan and said, ‘Keep this with you.’ Then we set off on a journey.
