While we were travelling, I began wondering why I had been given the Naan bread, upon which Hadhrat Baba rahmatullah alayhi addressed me, saying, ‘Keep control over your Baatin (inner self).’ We then reached the house where Hadhrat Baba rahmatullah alayhi wanted to stay. When the host saw that his guest was Hadhrat Baba Samaasi rahmatullah alayhi, he was overcome with joy. But he then proceeded anxiously to come in and out of our presence. Hadhrat Baba rahmatullah alayhi spoke to him, saying, ‘tell me truthfully: why you are so worried?’ He replied, ‘Hadhrat, I have milk for you in my house, but despite all my efforts I have not been able to obtain any chapati.’ Hadhrat Baba rahmatullah alayhi turned to me and said, ‘Bring out that Naan’, and added, ‘O my son! Do you see now how that Naan has come into use?’” Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi rahmatullah alayhi also relates: “One day the Shaykh saw me making du’a and he addressed me, saying, ‘O my son, when you supplicate, you should do it in such a manner that you call upon Allah saying, ‘O Allah! I am a very weak servant of Yours! With Your blessings and Mercy, please make me steadfast upon that which pleases You.’ Then he added, ‘Know that Allah’s pleasure is present when a person is not afflicted by any difficulty. And if, for some reason, hardships and difficulties do befall the friend of Allah, then from His infinite wisdom, He gives His friend the strength to cope with them.” The Shaykh passed away on the 10th of Jumad-al-Aakhir 755 Hijri. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is in Qasbah Samaasi.

name: Hadhrat Syed Ameer Kalaal Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was the most prominent of the Khulafa of Hadhrat Muhammad Baba Samaasi rahmatullah alayhi. He was a Sayyid by lineage and was trained as a potter. His mother used to say, “When Ameer Kalaal was in my womb, I got a pain in my belly whenever I ate something doubtful, a pain which wouldn’t go away until I vomited. I realised that this was happening because of the baby, and so I took great care thereafter in what I ate.”

In his youth, the Shaykh’s favourite pastime was wrestling. One day, the Shaykh was engaged in a wrestling match when Khwajah Baba rahmatullah alayhi happened to pass by. Hadhrat Baba Samaasi rahmatullah alayhi stopped in his tracks and began to watch. Some of the mureeds who were with Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi began to think that there must be some significant reason why their Shaykh had stopped to watch a wrestling bout in this way. Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi then spoke to his mureeds, saying, “I see a man from whom a huge amount of people will reach the stages of perfection. I am standing here so that I may hunt him.” Moments later, the gaze of Hadhrat Ameer rahmatullah alayhi fell upon Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi, and this one glance sparked immense love for Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi in the Shaykh’s heart. So the Shaykh left in the middle of the bout, and began to follow behind Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi. Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi then showed great affection for the Shaykh, took him to his Hujrah (study) and on that same day the Shaykh was initiated into the Tareeqah Aaliyah. From that day forth, the Shaykh lost his love for wrestling and spent thirty years in the service of Hadhrat Baba rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh used to travel twice a week from his home in Saukhaar to Samaas to acquire the company of his Shaykh. The Shaykh would say, “No matter how small a sin may seem, never ever consider it to be minor, because doing so will cause many people to enter the Hellfire.” An illustration of how cautious he was is that once, when on a journey, he and his mureeds washed their clothes and then wanted to put them out to dry. The Shaykh instructed his companions, saying, “Do not put them out to dry on thorn bushes, as I do not wish to harm the roots of the bushes with my clothes. And do not put them out to dry on the trees, for it is possible that it could harm the branches. And do not lay them out on the land, as this could harm the grass.” The mureeds asked, “How else can we dry them?” The Shaykh replied, “Let them rest on your backs, and then turn your backs towards the Sun.” The Shaykh stated, “The Path to Allah truly opens only after a person has adopted Taqwa.” He also used to say, “True Darweshes are always busy praying for the believers; when they begin to think of themselves, they are veiled from creation.” The king of that time wanted to make a gift of wealth and possessions to the Shaykh. The Shaykh asked him, “Why do you want to do this?” His reply was, “I wish to be close to you.” The Shaykh then said, “If you want the Darweshes of Allah to have room in their hearts for you, then make a habit of Taqwa and apply justice fairly, for these are the things that will make you closer to Allah subhana wa ta’ala.” One day, the Shaykh was travelling with his mureeds when their path was suddenly obstructed by a lion. Without any fear whatsoever, the Shaykh approached the lion, held it by its neck and led it off the path. The Shaykh’s companions were stunned by what they had seen, and noticing this, the Shaykh said, “Allah’s creatures have fear and respect for people who themselves have immense fear of Allah, both internally and externally.” The Shaykh used to say, “By Allah! Even if a person were to become crooked due to the abundance of his worship, or his body thin from excessive devotion, he could never please Allah if his earnings were not pure and lawful.” The Shaykh would also say, “No act of worship is better than kindness. When you make the dhikr of Allah, you should do so with all other desires and thoughts put aside. The dhikr of Allah purifies the tongue and the Salaah purifies the body. Repentance is not expressed in words alone; in fact, repentance is when you feel severe regret in your heart for your sins, and then

refrain from those sins in the future. You should weep so much that you can feel the effect of Tawbah inside you.” He also said, “Remove any worry about livelihood from your heart, and make room in it for worry about the Hereafter and how to live this life as an obedient servant.” He also advised the following: “Never consider your actions to be pure. Always weigh them with the scales of the Shari’ah. If they are within the bounds of Shari’ah, then one should accept them; otherwise they should be rejected.” He further commented that “One should safeguard the Shari’ah with every single action and respect the boundaries that Allah subhana wa ta’ala has ordained.” Another of his sayings is as follows: “Nothing improves a person more than good manners and a charitable nature. In order to gain the knowledge of Allah, however, it is essential for a person to have the right belief and to stay clear from falsehood and innovation.” He also said, “Do not keep the company of worldly people, for their company will keep you away from Allah.” It has been related that three days before he passed away, the Shaykh went into Muraqabah. After three days of Muraqabah, he raised his head, praised Allah subhana wa ta’ala and then said, “I was very worried about my fate and that of my companions until I heard a voice inside me, saying, ‘O Kalaal! We have showered our Mercy upon you and your companions, and even upon those on whom a fly settled while they served you; and We have forgiven their sins.’” The Shaykh passed away on the same day after the Morning Prayer on the 8th of Jumad-ul-Awwal 772 Hijri. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is situated in the district of Saukhaar.

name: Hadhrat Syed Baha’uddin Naqshband Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was born on the 4th of Muharram 708 Hijri at a place called Qasr-i-Arifan near the city of Bukhara, and he was a saint from birth. Karamats and visions were part of the Shaykh’s life from his childhood. One day, soon after the Shaykh had learned to talk, he spoke to his mother regarding some cattle that were in front of them, telling her that one of the cows had a calf in her belly of such and such a colour, and with such and such markings on its body. When the cow gave birth, its calf was just as the Shaykh had described, and all the marks on its body were exactly where he had said they were. Physically, the Shaykh acquired the knowledge of Tareeqah from Hadhrat Ameer Kalal rahmatullah alayhi, but in reality the Shaykh was a spiritual student of Hadhrat Khwajah Abd-ul-Khaliq Ghajdwani rahmatullah alayhi, for the Shaykh attained guidance from his Rooh. Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Baba Samasi rahmatullah alayhi related the excellence of the Shaykh before he was even born, saying, “The time is approaching when a great person will be born in these lands. I can smell his fragrance. The world will be illuminated by his presence and multitudes of people will attain fayz from him.” This is why the Shaykh was taken to Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Baba rahmatullah alayhi three days after his birth, who immediately accepted him as a son and addressed his honourable Khaleefah Hadhrat Ameer Kalal rahmatullah alayhi, saying, “I place this child in your care, and I shall never forgive you if there is any deficiency in the spiritual upbringing of this child.”

The Shaykh states, “One day I was sat all alone, when all of a sudden I heard a voice saying, ‘O Baha’uddin, do you not think that the time has come for you to turn your face away from the world and for you to devote yourself to Me?’” On hearing this voice, the Shaykh was overcome with anxiety. He stood up and went out into the darkness of the night. On reaching a wide stream, the Shaykh washed his clothes, performed ghusl and prayed two rakats of prayer. In later days, the Shaykh would say “So much time has passed, yet I still live with the desire to experience a prayer like that again.” The Shaykh relates, “In my youth I would live in a state of unrest, wandering the streets at night, visiting the various shrines in and around Bukhara. One night, I saw a lamp that was full of oil but its light was flickering, sometimes bright and at other times so dim as if it would disappear altogether. I noticed that with a little adjustment, the lamp could become very bright. When I reached the shrine of Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Wasi’ rahmatullah alayhi, I was instructed to go to the shrine of Hadhrat Khwajah Mahmood Anjeer Faghnawi rahmatullah alayhi. When I got there, two men approached me. They tied two swords to my back and made me sit on a horse. They then turned the horse around to face in the direction of the shrine of Khwajah Mazd Afan. When I reached that shrine, I sat down facing the Qibla, and all of a sudden the wall before me parted, and I saw a very big throne in front of me. Then I saw that a saintly person had sat on the throne, and that in front of him was a green curtain and gathered around him was a group of saints. Someone began to call out the names of these saints saying, ‘This is Khwajah Abdul Khaliq rahmatullah alayhi (and it was he who was sat on the throne), this is Khwajah Ahmad Siddique rahmatullah alayhi, this is Khwajah Awliya Kalal rahmatullah alayhi, this is Khwajah Arif Reogari rahmatullah alayhi, Khwajah Mahmood Faghnawi rahmatullah alayhi, Khwajah Ali Ramatini’ and when it came to Khwajah Muhammad Baba Samasi rahmatullah alayhi, the voice said, ‘And this is your Shaykh.’ I then requested that I be allowed to convey salaam to Hadhrat Khwajah Abdul Khaliq rahmatullah alayhi. The curtain before him was drawn to the side, and Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi returned my greeting and then taught me Sulook from beginning to end. He then addressed me, saying, ‘Be steadfast upon the Shari’ah under all circumstances, and act upon the blessed Sunnah with devotion. Stay well clear of innovations and refrain from a life in which you only fulfil the minimum requirements of worship and no more. Always make the Ahadeeth of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam your guide.’ “Later I went into the company of Hadhrat Ameer Kalal rahmatullah alayhi, who taught me dhikr Nafi Athbaat Khafi (rejecting everything but Allah through silent repetition of La ilaha illa’llah), which I continued to perform with steadfastness for a long while; and in accordance with the instruction of Hadhrat Khwajah Abdul Khaliq Ghajdwani rahmatullah alayhi, I would not do Jahr (loud) dhikr. When the companions of Hadhrat Khwajah Ameer Kalal rahmatullah alayhi used to do loud dhikr, I would often get up and leave. The other mureeds of the Shaykh did not like this, but their doubts were finally put to rest when one day Hadhrat Khwajah Ameer rahmatullah alayhi said, ‘O People! You think ill of Baha’uddin, but do you not know that a very special favour of Allah is upon him?’ Later, Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah spoke to me saying, ‘O Baha’uddin, I have completed your spiritual upbringing in the manner that I had been instructed by Hadhrat Baba Samasi rahmatullah alayhi.’ After that, Hadhrat Shaykh granted me khilafah. “Once I had a dream that I would attain something from a Turkish Shaykh, so I was always on the look out for that Shaykh. Finally, one day I met this Shaykh in one of the bazaars of

Bukhara. I recognised him and discovered that his name was Khalil. Later a messenger came to me saying that I had been called to meet this Darwesh called Khalil. I went to see him straight away and wanted to tell him about my dream, but he said to me, ‘I know what is in your heart; there is no need to tell me.’ I loved this person and I had some amazing experiences in his company. A few days later, he disappeared. I learned later that he was the King of Mawralnahar, and he called me to his kingdom and offered me a job. I served the king for six years and during that time saw many remarkable things.” Regarding this, the king used to say, “The person who serves others for the sake of Allah alone has a great status among creation.” The Shaykh relates another event thus: “During the time that I was in the service of Hadhrat Ameer Kalal rahmatullah alayhi, I once saw Hadhrat Khidr alayhi salaam. He was riding, wearing a kulla and had a big stick in his hand. He spoke to me, saying, ‘Have you seen my horse?’ and then he hit me with his stick. I did not say anything in reply. Then he blocked my path a few times, and I said to him, ‘I know full well that you are Khidhr alayhi salaam.’ He followed me and said, ‘Stop!’ but I did not listen and carried on walking. When I arrived in the company of Hadhrat Ameer Kalal rahmatullah alayhi, the Shaykh took one look at me and said, ‘You met with Hadhrat Khidr alayhi salaam and yet you didn’t pay him any attention?’ I replied, ‘Hadhrat, all my attention at the time was on you.’ Hadhrat Khwajah Ameer rahmatullah alayhi then explained, “The spiritual well-spring of the Khwajigan is linked to four sources; the first is Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam, the second is Junayd al-Baghdadi rahmatullah alayhi, the third is Hadhrat Bayazid Bistami rahmatullah alayhi from the chain of authority that reached him from Hadhrat Ali radhiallahu anhu, and the fourth is the chain of authority that reached him from Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique radhiallahu anhu.’” The Shaykh used to say, “A person should not shut his eyes intentionally during Wuqoof-e-Qalbi (stopping the worldly thoughts of the heart) as that is nothing but Itlaai’ Khalq (observing one’s own being).” The Shaykh also stated, “Once, on seeing a person sitting with his neck bent down and head bowed, Ameer-ul-Mu’mineen Hadhrat Umar radhiallahu anhu said, ‘When a person is not alone and is amongst other people, he should do dhikr in such a manner that no one notices that he is in Allah’s remembrance.’ The Shaykh used to say, “Dhikr is the removal of neglect. When someone is no longer neglectful, then he can be called a dhaakir.” The Shaykh further explained, “It is a saying of the saints that if a person is neglectful for even the time it takes to blink, he will never be able to comprehend how much he has lost in that one moment.” The Shaykh also stated, “Whoever remains busy in Allah’s dhikr in the morning and evening can never be among the ghafil (neglectful). He is indeed a dhaakir.” The Shaykh related: “I was granted a vision of the Maqam of Shaykh Junayd, Shaykh Shibli, Shaykh Mansoor Hallaj and Hadhrat Bayazid Bistami rahmatullah alayhum, and I saw that whatever stage they reached, I too reached. During this spiritual journey, we arrived at the gates of one majestic station which I realised was that of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. When Hadhrat Bayazid Bistami rahmatullah alayhi reached this station, he had a desire to view the Maqam, and due to this, the hand of refusal hit his forehead. My response was very different; I placed my head in utmost respect and reverence at the gate of the station, with no desire to behold it.”

In a similar vein, the Shaykh stated, “One should seek steadfastness and should never desire miracles. Allah subhana wa ta’ala seeks steadfastness from his servants, whereas your Nafs seeks miracles.” He also said, “If a friend of Allah walks in a garden and hears the trees speaking to him and sees spirits coming to visit him, he should never set store by these things and should always adopt a humble manner, continually striving to perfect his way of life.” The Shaykh also stated, “My Tareeqah is to follow the Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam in the manner explained to us by his blessed Sahaba radhiallahu anhum”; and he said, “In my Silsilah, a little is worth a lot, but devotion and obedience is a condition of this reward.” He also stated, “Our Tareeqah is one of Suhbat (company). Fame comes from solitude and in fame there is destruction.” The Shaykh gave the following advice about the friends of Allah: “When you go to visit a friend of Allah, you should examine yourself and analyse your state; if you see that your Deen has improved through this company, then make it incumbent upon yourself to make this company regular.” The Shaykh further stated, “True self-analysis is when a saalik continually assesses his own actions; he should regret his shortcomings, thank Allah for his progress and always work tirelessly to improve.” He also said, “There is no friend of Allah on this Earth who is not under the special gaze of Allah subhana wa ta’ala. When you sit in the company of the friend of Allah, the fayz (overflow of spiritual blessings) that you receive is in fact a reflection of that special gaze.” Another point he made was that “The friends of Allah are endowed with the knowledge of many secrets concerning the wonders of creation, but those with this knowledge do not disclose it, whereas those who have no idea talk a lot and pretend they know everything.” The Shaykh stated, “If a mureed has any doubt regarding one of his Shaykh’s actions, he should be patient for it may well be that the reason for the action will become very clear later.” He also said, “One should always try one’s best to strive hard in Allah’s Path.” The Shaykh states, “Once, Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam and his Sahaba each put one piece of bread in a clay oven to bake. All the pieces of bread got baked except for the bread of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. This was because the Prophet’s blessed hand had touched it, and therefore the fire could not burn it.” The Shaykh continued, “Through attaining perfection in following the Sunnah, I too was once in a similar situation; I too once placed a piece of bread in a clay oven along with some of my companions, and all their pieces got baked whereas mine was left untouched by the fire.” Once a person came to the Shaykh and asked him to display a miracle. The Shaykh replied, “Despite committing so many sins, I still walk on the land and the earth does not devour me. Tell me, what can be a bigger miracle than this?” Once the Shaykh enquired from Hadhrat Khwajah Ala’uddin Attar rahmatullah alayhi whether or not the time for Zuhr Salaah had begun, and was informed that it hadn’t. The Shaykh then said, “Look up at the sky.” When they looked up at the sky, they noticed that the veils of the heavens had been drawn aside and that the angels in the heavens were performing the fardh prayer. The Shaykh then said, “And you were telling me that it was not yet time.” Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi had the opportunity to see the blessed House of Allah and performed the Hajj. On the day of sacrifice, when all the pilgrims were making Qurbani, the Shaykh said, “I too shall make a sacrifice: there is a boy - I sacrifice him in Your Path.” Later the people discovered that on that very day of Eid, the Shaykh’s son had passed away in Bukhara.

Once, Ameer Burhan-ud-din brought some pieces of bread and began to bake them in a clay oven, when all of a sudden it began to rain heavily. At this Hadhrat Khwajah said, “Tell the rain not to come near us while we are here.” The Ameer replied, “How can I say such thing?” The Shaykh said, “Say what I have told you to say.” As soon as he did as he was told, it rained all around them yet not one drop of rain landed on the small patch of land where they were. One of the mureeds of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi brought an apple for the Shaykh. The Shaykh said, “Wait; do not eat this apple right now because it is busy in tasbeeh.” Those present heard clearly the recitation of the apple. Once, the Shaykh was in the city of Sarkhas. A few envoys of King Hussain came to see the Shaykh from Herat and they delivered a message from the king, which said, “I have a strong desire to meet with the friends of Allah.” The Shaykh did not make a habit of visiting Sultans, but on this occasion the Shaykh accepted the invitation and went to see the king, where a huge reception was waiting for him. The king spoke to Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi, saying, “Your type of spiritual prowess is hereditary, is it not?” The Shaykh replied, “No, and I have only come here in response to the command of my enthusiasm.” The King asked, “What is your Tareeqah?” Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi replied, “It is a saying of Khwajah Abd-ul-Khaliq Ghajdwani rahmatullah alayhi that ‘Khalwat dar anjuman.’” The King asked what this meant and the Shaykh replied, “It is to be with the creation physically and outwardly, but to be with the Haq subhana wa ta’ala spiritually and inwardly.” After a while, the King asked the Shaykh, “Some Masha’ikh have stated that Wilayah (sainthood) is more virtuous than Nabuwwah (Prophethood). What type of Wilayah are they referring to that is more virtuous than Prophethood?” The Shaykh replied, “They refer to the Wilayah of a Nabi, which is more virtuous than his own Nabuwwah.” The Shaykh also stated, “Although Salaah, fasting and extensive mujahidah (striving) and nawaafil worship is the way to reach Haq subhana wa ta’ala, according to us it is essential to negate one’s Self in the process, for that is the most virtuous achievement of the seeker.” One of the scholars of Bukhara came to Hadhrat Khwajah and asked, “What matter or action gives you the feeling of being in the presence of your Lord when you pray Salaah?” Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi replied, “Halal food that is consumed with care, understanding and thought.” The Shaykh stated, “The following has been stated by Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam: ‘My Ummah will never reach a consensus about a matter that is false.’ This is because there are people in the Ummah who are the Siddiqeen, and are known as Ummat-e-Mataabi’at.” He went on, “The Ummah falls into three categories. The first is ‘Ummat-e-Da’wat’, and this includes every person in the Ummah. The second is ‘Ummat-e-Ajabat’, meaning those that have Iman. And the third is ‘Ummat-e-Mataabi’at’, who are those who follow the ways of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam after they have been granted Iman.” The Shaykh stated, “Our Tareeqah is all Adab (etiquette). It is for this reason that one of the conditions for seeking the Path is Adab. One Adab is nisbat with Allah subhana wa ta’ala; one Adab is nisbat with Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam; and one Adab is nisbat with the Masha’ikh of the Tareeqah. The Adab of the nisbat that one has with Allah subhana wa ta’ala is that a person obeys the commands of Allah subhana wa ta’ala both internally and externally, and that his worship and all actions are for Allah alone. The Adab of the nisbat one has with Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam is that a person must always be obedient to Allah’s

Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam and to try his utmost to live his life upon the Sunnah in all aspects, considering Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam to be the link between Allah and His creation and the sole channel through which he can reach Allah. And finally, the Adab of the nisbat with the Mashai’kh is that it is compulsory for the seekers to have utmost respect and adab for their Shaykh, both in his presence and in his absence.” The Shaykh also stated, “In Qabdh (the state of spiritual constraint) one witnesses the quality of Jalaal (Awesome Power), and in Bast (the state of spiritual expansion) the quality of Jamaal (Beauty).” Once the Shaykh said, “All the Masha’ikh have two faces to their ‘mirror’; however there are seven faces to ours.” Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi explained this statement, saying, “The ‘mirror’ refers to the heart of the Arif (one possessed of direct spiritual insight), which is the link between the Rooh and the Nafs, and its two faces relate to the Rooh and the Nafs respectively. In the other Tareeqahs, both of these reflect onto the heart, and the heart thereby receives spiritual knowledge and blessing. In the Silsilah Aaliya Naqshbandia, knowledge falls onto the mirror of the heart from six directions or points, namely the Nafs, Qalb, Rooh, Sirr, Khafi and Akhfa. This is why it has been stated that the other silsilahs engage in the ‘exploration of the heart’, whereas the Silsilah Aaliya Naqshbandia engages in the ‘exploration of the internal orientation of the heart’; thus it is from those six lataa’if (points of spiritual reception) that spiritual knowledge enters the heart.” Thousands of karamat have been attributed to the blessed Shaykh, and if we were to put them in writing, we would end up with several very thick volumes. The biggest karamat of the Shaykh was that he gave life to hundreds of thousands of dead hearts with the dhikr of Allah, through bestowing such a mark (Naqsh)- on the hearts of the believers that, once stamped, is indelible (-band) and goes with them into the grave. To give life to a dead heart is more virtuous than bringing a dead person back to life. This is because if a dead person were to come alive, he could again occupy himself in the deceptions of the Dunya, whereas the heart that comes to life becomes nearer to Allah subhana wa ta’ala. It was a custom of the age to decorate clothes with beautiful patterns and prints. The Shaykh, however, imprinted the remembrance of the Haq onto the hearts in such a way that it could never be erased or tampered with. It is for this reason that the name of this Silsilah came to be known as Naqshbandia. It has been narrated that before the Shaykh passed away, he said, “When my last moment comes upon me, I shall teach the people how to die.” So when the Shaykh reached the last moments of his life, he raised his hands in du’a and supplicated for a lengthy time. No sooner had he finished the du’a and wiped his hands over his face, his soul went to meet his Lord. The Shaykh was seventy-three years old when he passed away on Monday the 3rd of Rabi-ul-Awwal 791 Hijri. He had given instruction for the people not to recite the kalimah or the Qur’an aloud in front of his funeral procession, since it could be disrespectful. The shrine of the Shaykh is at a place called Qasr-e-Arifan, and is a fountain of blessing for the seekers of the Haq. The Shaykh is Imam-ut-Tareeqah and it is from the nisbat of Hadhrat Shaykh rahmatullah alyahi that the Silsilah gets its name. The Shaykh reached the status of Ijtihaad in knowledge of Tareeqat. When the Shaykh was given khilafah in the Tareeqah by his Murshid, Hadhrat Ameer Kalal rahmatullah alayhi, he was already familiar with the Mujahidaat and acts of devotion of all

the various Tareeqahs. In solitude, the Shaykh went into Sajdah (prostration) and prayed to Allah subhana wa ta’ala, saying, “O Allah, the people of the Ummah have become weak. They have no strength, determination or ability to tolerate hardship; and the blessed time and era of the Prophet sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, that was so full of goodness and blessing, gets further away from us as each day passes by. Through Your Mercy and Blessings, please give me a Silsilah by which one can gain Your nearness quickly and with ease.” For fifteen consecutive days the Shaykh remained in Sajdah, weeping and pleading before his Lord, only leaving that position in order to pray fardh Salaah in congregation or to attend the call of nature. On the fifteenth day, from the oceans of the Mercy of Allah, the Shaykh received Ilham (inspiration) from Allah in these words: “O Muhammad Baha’uddin! We shall give you that Tareeqah which was that of the Companions of My Habeeb sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, namely Wuqoof-e-Qalbi (stopping the worldly thoughts of the heart) and adherence to the Sunnah of Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.” The Shaykh expressed his gratitude to Allah subhana wa ta’ala and then lifted his head from the ground. Subsequently this Tareeqah spread across the world in the way that daylight spreads over the land at sunrise. Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi used to say, “All the Tareeqahs are blessed, full of light, and all of them lead to Allah. However the Tareeqah that Allah subhana wa ta’ala has given me is full of ease in comparison, and one reaches Allah very quickly.” In Dhikr-e-Qalbi (remembrance of the heart) there is Jadhb-e-Rabbani (rapture in the Divine) and in Dhikr-e-Rabbani (remembrance of the Divine) there is Sulook (the Path towards Allah’s nearness), and it is for this reason that Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi stated, “Ma murad-a-neem, kamaa fadhliy-a-neem”, meaning “We are of those who are sought, and we are of those upon whom there is fadhal.” Mawlana Jaami rahmatullaha alayhi states, “Naqshbandia ajab qafila sa laaranand, ke barandaaz rahe panhaan baharam qaafila raa”, which translates as: “The Naqshbandia lead an extraordinary caravan, for they take their students to the Haram via a secret, hidden route.”

name: Hadhrat Ala’uddin Attaar Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was the son-in-law, first khalifah and successor of Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi. After his own father had passed away, he had embarked on a programme of formal education at one of the Schools in Bukhara. The Shaykh had not yet completed his studies when his immense desire for the Haq made him go and sit in the company of Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi. Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi gave the Shaykh a lot of love and attention, so much so that he used to have the Shaykh sit near him during gatherings. Thus, through the blessings of the attention of Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi, the Shaykh quickly acquired the stages of perfection. Such were the Shaykh’s qualities that towards the end of his life, Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi transferred his own mureeds to the Shaykh and said in respect of this, “Ala’ud-din has relieved me of a great burden.” After Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi had passed away, all his mureeds made bay’ah with the Shaykh. Even Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Parsa turned to the Shaykh and

sat in his company. Another quality of the Shaykh was that he was given a special Tareeqah called A’laaniya, and a detailed account of this has been related by Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi in his Maktoobaat. During the time of the Shaykh, there was a great dispute amongst the scholars regarding the ‘description’ of Allah; all the scholars agreed that they should make the Shaykh a judge between them. The Shaykh addressed those scholars that opposed his ruling on the matter, saying, “Come and sit in my company for three days, and each day perform wudhu before you come.” On the third day, they were so overcome that not only did they change their views, they also attached themselves to the Shaykh for the rest of their lives. The Shaykh used to say, “The purpose of devotion is to detach yourself from your body, in order to have an eternal link with Alam-e-Arwah (the Realm of the Souls) and Alam-e-Haqeeqat (the Realm of Divine Reality).” The Shaykh also stated, “One attains fayz from the shrines of the Masha’ikh in accordance with how much belief one has.” As to dealings with people, the Shaykh stated, “When in the company of the creation of Allah, outwardly it should seem that one is dealing with the people around one, but in reality a person’s heart should always be attentive towards Allah subhana wa ta’ala.” Regarding matters of Tasawwuf, the Shaykh said, “The technique of the Muraqabah of negation is better and more excellent than that of verification, for the former provides lasting peace of mind.” He also stated, “Progress is achieved through sitting in the company of the Men of Allah with steadfastness and regularity”, and “A person should keep telling his Shaykh about his problems, even if by letter.” In his last illness, the Shaykh would say to those who were close, “I have no desire left in my heart except that friends come to me, but do not find me.” Before the Shaykh left this world, he said with great emphasis, “Hold on firmly to the Sunnah of Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and stay clear of all traditions and customs that oppose it.” The Shaykh then recited the Kalimah Tawheed and passed away. Hadhrat Khwajah Parsa rahmatullah alayhi writes that when Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi was in Bukhara, one of the Darweshes of the Shaykh saw him in a dream. In the dream, he saw a majestic and heavenly place. This Darwesh was with Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi and as they approached, they noticed that the place belonged to Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi entered the building, and after a while, returned in a state of great happiness, saying, “I have been given a karamat; I have, with the permission of Allah, been allowed to intercede on behalf of every person that will be buried (within a radius of approximately three miles) in the vicinity of my shrine in all four directions.” He passed away after Isha prayers on the 18th of Rajab 802 AH. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is at a place called Chaghaniyan.

name: Hadhrat Ya’qoob Charkhi Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh is counted amongst the great Shaykhs of the Naqshbandi order. Although he obtained khilafah from Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi, he is considered to be one of the Khulafa of Hadhrat Khwajah Ala’ud-din Attar rahmatullah alayhi, because it was in his company that the Shaykh later completed his spiritual training. The Shaykh initially acquired the

formal knowledge of the Deen at Herat. After this, in a state of fervent love for his Lord, he set off to sit in the company of Hadhrat Baha’ud-din Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi. On his way, the Shaykh met a Majdhoob (one in a state of spiritual rapture), who addressed him, saying, “O Yaqub! Increase the speed of your steps, for the time has come for you to join the number of those who have been accepted.” After saying this, he drew some lines on the ground.” Mawlana thought to himself that if these lines were an odd number, then he would achieve his goal. On counting them, he discovered that there was indeed an odd number. Some time later, the Shaykh entered the company of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh relates this in his own words, saying, “I went into the presence of the Shaykh and expressed my desire to make bay’ah. Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi replied, ‘I am reliant on Allah, so it is not for me to decide. If I get any sign for this by tomorrow, then it shall be so.’” The Shaykh later recalled, “In terms of anxiety, that was the hardest night of my life. I was petrified that I would be rejected. In the morning, I prayed Fajr Salaah by Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi. After the prayer Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi turned to me and said, ‘Congratulations’, and I understood that I had been accepted. After this I received my spiritual education from the Shaykh. After some time in the company of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi, I was given permission to travel and Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi said, “Pass on whatever you have learnt from us to the men of Allah.” And then three times he said, “I place you in the safeguard of Allah.” The Shaykh further directed me to go and sit in the company of Hadhrat Khwajah Ala’ud-din rahmatullah alayhi. “From there I departed for a place called Kaysh. On arriving at Kaysh, I was informed that Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi had passed away. In a state of grief and sorrow, I left Kaysh and set off for Badakhshan. From there I intended to return to Charkh. It was then that I received a letter from Hadhrat Khwajah Ala’ud-din rahmatullah alayhi and, in accordance with the instructions of Hadhrat Baha’ud-din rahmatullah alayhi, I went into the company of Hadhrat Khwajah Ala’ud-din rahmatullah alayhi, who showed me great affection. I benefited from his company for many years; in fact I stayed with the Shaykh until he passed away.” The Shaykh states, “One day I saw Hadhrat Khwajah Baha’ud-din rahmatullah alayhi in a dream and I asked him, ‘By which of your actions in life should we remember you?’ The Shaykh replied, ‘Adherence to the Shari’ah.’ And he also said ‘Everything that I have attained is from acting upon the Qur’an and Ahadeeth, being steadfast upon devotion and by staying clear of innovation.” As instructed by Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi, the Shaykh had to pass on what he had learned from his company. So the Shaykh used to deliver speeches that were very beneficial to those that came to listen, and for those that were not present, the invitation towards the Deen was extended by way of literature. The Shaykh never considered his knowledge to be his own, but rather that all he was doing was passing on the teachings of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi, teachings that were full of great wisdom. The Shaykh was a great writer, and wrote a tafseer for the last two chapters of the Qur’an. He also published a magazine containing the life teachings of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh passed away on the 5th of Safar 861 AH. His shrine is located at a place called Halfatu near Hasar, Mawralnahar.

name: Hadhrat Abaydullah Ahraar Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi was born at a place called Baghistan in Tashkent, in the month of Ramadhan 806 AH. For forty days after his birth, the Shaykh did not drink his mother’s milk due to her being ritually impure following childbirth. As soon as this time had elapsed, and his mother made the customary ghusl, he began feeding on her milk. The grandfather of the Shaykh, Khwajah Shahab-ud-din rahmatullah alayhi was the Qutub of the age. On his deathbed, Shaykh Shahab-ud-din called for all his grandsons so that he could bid them farewell. At the time, Hadhrat Ubaydullah Ahrar was still a young child. When the child was presented before him, Shaykh Shahab-ud-din stood up in respect and then sat the child on his lap, saying, “I have been informed that this son of mine will be a great Shaykh of his time and he will be a reviver of the Shari’ah and Tareeqah.” Even as a boy, it was apparent that the Shaykh possessed qualities of goodness and piety. In his childhood, the Shaykh used to visit the various shrines of the Masha’ikh in the area and he would often visit all of them in one night alone. The Shaykh’s maternal uncle, Khwajah Ibrahim rahmatullah alayhi, was greatly interested in the Shaykh’s education, and at the age of 22 took him from Tashkent to Samarqand. However the Shaykh’s immense interest in the matters of the inner self was, at the time, a barrier to his completion of the outer knowledge. From the age of 22 to 29, the Shaykh spent his time travelling. On his travels, the Shaykh had opportunities to sit in the company of many Masha’ikh. In Samarqand, the Shaykh often used to sit in the company of Mawlana Nizam-ud-din, who was a Khaleefah of Hadhrat Ala’ud-din Attar rahmatullah alayhi. A day before their first meeting, Mawlana Nizam-ud-deen was in Muraqabah when he suddenly called out aloud, saying, “There has appeared a man from the east called Khwajah Ubaydullah, and he has taken all the lands!” One day, during his stay in Samarqand, after he had left the presence of Mawlana Nizam-ud-din, someone asked Mawlana Nizam-ud-din rahmatullah alayhi, “Who is this young man?” Mawlana Sahib replied, “That is Khwajah Ubaydullah; soon the sultans of the world will be his greatest admirers.” Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi relates: “After hearing of the virtues and qualities of Hadhrat Mawlana Charkhi rahmatullah alayhi from a tradesman, I set off for Balaghnoor to meet the Shaykh. On my journey, I fell ill for twenty days and during that time, some people spoke to me in negative terms about the Shaykh and I thought I ought to return. But then I thought that it would not be appropriate for me to return after such a long journey, and hence continued on my journey to see the Shaykh. During our meeting, Hadhrat Charkhi rahmatullah alayhi related to me the account of his meeting with Hadhrat Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi, and then put his hand forward, offering me the opportunity to make bay’ah with him. But I held back, disturbed by an odd looking mark that looked like leprosy on the Shaykh’s forehead. The Shaykh realised what was on my mind, withdrew his hand and then appeared before me in such a handsome and striking appearance that I was overcome and helpless. The Shaykh again put his hand forward, saying, “Hadhrat Baha’ud-din Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi held my hand and said, ‘Your hand is my hand; whoever takes your hand has indeed taken the hand of Khwajah Baha’ud-din rahmatullah alayhi.’ As soon as I heard this, I took his hand immediately. After this, the Shaykh educated me and finally said, ‘This is all that reached me from Hadhrat

Khwajah Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi.’ He also said, ‘A seeker should come to his Shaykh in the manner that Ubaydullah has come here.’ When I sought permission to leave for the first time, the Shaykh related to me some detailed teachings and ways of Hadhrat Khwajigan and said, ‘Pass on this information to those with potential.’ After taking leave of Hadhrat Khwajah Yaqub Charkhi rahmatullah alayhi, the Shaykh travelled to Herat where he stayed for one year, before returning to Tashkent at the age of 29. The Shaykh then became a permanent resident of Tashkent and chose agriculture as his profession. Allah subhana wa ta’ala blessed his work, and he became very wealthy, spending what he earned on the poor, needy and the dhakireen of Allah. In a dream, the Shaykh saw that the implementation of Shari’ah would be greatly increased through his help. The Shaykh formed the view that for the implementation of Shari’ah, it was essential for the Sultans of the land to be inclined towards it. It was for this reason that the Shaykh set off for Samarqand, which was at the time ruled by a man called Mirza Abdullah. When the Shaykh arrived in Samarqand, one of the ministers of Mirza Abdullah came to see him. The Shaykh told him that he wished to meet with the king. The minister gave him short shrift, saying, “Mirza cares nothing for your mission, so meeting him is out of the question.” The Shaykh replied, “If your Mirza does not care, then he will be replaced by one who does care.” After saying this, the Shaykh wrote his name on some paper and then erased it. After one week, the minister died and Sultan Abdullah was killed. The Shaykh used to say, “If I was to carry out the duties that are normal for a Peer, people would flock to me such that the rest of the Peers(Shaykhs) of this age would be left without any mureeds. But I have been given another mission, and that is to save the Muslims from the evil of the oppressors and to revive the Shari’ah. It is for this reason that I aim to communicate with the Sultans.” The Shaykh also stated, “Allah subhana wa ta’ala has given me so much power that if I was to write just one letter to the kings, they would leave their monarchies and come running to me barefooted; but I do not do anything without the permission of Allah subhana wa ta’ala.” Once the Shaykh was travelling with his companions through what was considered to be a dangerous part of the countryside. Evening was approaching and they were still a considerable distance from their destination. The Shaykh’s companions became anxious, and the Shaykh noticed this and said, “Do not worry. Insha’allah we shall reach our destination before sunset.” What followed was that the Sun remained at the same point in the sky, and no sooner had they entered the city than the sun went down and with it darkness fell. All the companions of the Shaykh were dumbfounded by what they had seen. One day, two seekers came to visit the Shaykh and when they reached the Khanqah they learned that the Shaykh had gone to visit the king. They were bemused and thought, ‘What kind of Shaykh can he be if he spends his time in the company of kings?’ By apparent coincidence, on the same day two thieves had escaped from a nearby prison and the police were searching for them. Because these two seekers were strangers to the town, people thought that they were the thieves and had them arrested. They were restrained and brought before the king. The king ordered for their hands to be severed. However Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi, who was also present at the time said, “They are not thieves; they are guests who have come to visit me.” The king then released them and the Shaykh took them with him to the Khanqah, and told them,

“My reason for going to see the king today was just so that I could save your hands from be cut off.” Once a scholar came to visit the Shaykh. When he reached the gates of the city, he saw a large amount of food stock being transported. He enquired and discovered that all this stock belonged to Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi, so he thought to himself, “How can Faqr (spiritual poverty) and such wealth coexist?” This thought that had occurred to his heart made him want to return without meeting the Shaykh, but then he thought, “I have travelled so far that I may as well see what I came for.” With this he made for the Khanqah. On reaching the Khanqah, the scholar fell into a slumber and saw a vision. He had a vision of the Day of Judgement and before him was a man to whom he owed some money. The man was demanding that the scholar pay his debt, otherwise he would see the scholar go to Hell. At the same time, he saw Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi coming before them both and paying the debt on his behalf. His relief was unimaginable. When the eyes of the scholar opened, he saw the Shaykh before him, smiling and saying, “The reason for my wealth is precisely so that I can help people like you.” There are innumerable such karamats attributed to the Shaykh, and not all of them can be put into words. But the Shaykh never relied on his karamats. In fact the Shaykh stated, “Steadfastness upon the Shari’ah is the biggest karamat”, and this point is made time and again in the blessed sayings of the Shaykh. The Shaykh used to say, “A person whose heart becomes cold to the Dunya and warm for the dhikr of Allah has truly benefited from life in this world.” He also stated, “The true Shaykh is he whose actions are all beneath the canopy of the pleasure of Allah and his Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. His manners, actions and qualities are steeped in the colour of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.” As for mureeds, he said, “The true mureed is he who has no personal desires. He should divert his attention from all worldly things, and hisentire focus should be on his Shaykh.” He also explained that “The person who comes to meet and acquire the company of the Faqeers should emanate immense sincerity so that he can obtain Mercy.” Regarding Salaah, the Shaykh used to say, “To pray Salaah at a place where actions and manners are not proper cannot be compared, in terms of blessing, to other places such as those that have been affected by the presence of the leaders and guides of Mankind. This is also why two rakats of prayer offered in the Haram is more virtuous than that offered in any other place.” He also advised the following about praiseworthy states: “A person should always strive to attain the state in which he has no desire save for Allah in his heart. If you can achieve this, then you have certainly succeeded, and after attaining this state it does not matter whether or not you have visions and karamats.” The Shaykh also used to say, “If lies are absent from the tongue, then this is Shari’ah; and if lies are distant from the heart, then this is Tareeqah; and if they leave both your tongue and heart, whether through your own effort or otherwise, this is Haqeeqah.” Other sayings of the Shaykh include: “To incline towards and perform only those acts of worship that are absolutely essential is the way of the (spiritually) weak. The way of the Hadhrat Khwajigan is that of complete devotion to worship”; and “When Allah subhana wa ta’ala gives a person the tawfeeq to do Tawbah, he should try his hardest never to spend even one moment

neglectful of Allah’s dhikr”; and also “Before a person goes to sleep at night, he should assess how he spent the day. If he has spent the day in acts and manners outside the Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, then he should repent and seek Allah’s forgiveness.” He also stated, “One of the Adaab (etiquettes) of the Path is that one should always be in a state of wudhu. To be in a state of wudhu at all times opens the gateways to sustenance.” The Shaykh passed away on the 29th of Rabi al-Awwal 895 AH. At the time of the death of the Shaykh, those present noticed a light emanate from between his eyebrows. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is at a place called Mahota Malayian. The descendants of the Shaykh had a beautiful building constructed over the shrine.

name: Hadhrat Muhammad Zaahid Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh belonged to a family that was famous for the number of Awliya that came from it. He was the grandson of Hadhrat Mawlana Ya’qub Charkhi rahmatullah alayhi, and it was from one of Hadhrat Yaqub Charkhi rahmatullah alayhi’s khaleefahs that the Shaykh first learnt the dhikr. After acquiring knowledge, he then followed the path of seclusion. Later, the Shaykh went into the company of a famous Shaykh of the Naqshbandi Silsilah called Hadhrat Khwajah Ubaydullah Ahrar rahmatullah alayhi. When the Shaykh heard of the popularity of Hadhrat Khwajah Ahrar rahmatullah alayhi, he decided to go and visit him. The Shaykh set off from Hisar for Samarqand, which was where Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi lived. When he arrived in Samarqand, he stopped at a place called Walnahar, so that he could wash and put on new clothes before going into the presence of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi. While he was doing this, Hadhrat Khwajah Ubaydullah rahmatullah alayhi had a kashf (spiritual insight) by which he realised that the Shaykh was a man of high spiritual status who had travelled far to meet him, so in the heat of the early afternoon, Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi mounted his camel to go and meet him. Since he was not aware of where Hadhrat Mawlana rahmatullah alayhi was staying, he let the camel take a course of its own and move as it willed. The camel went straight to the place where Hadhrat Mawlana Zahid rahmatullah was staying and halted outside. Hadhrat Khwajah Ubaydullah Ahrar dismounted his camel, and it was quickly brought to the Shaykh’s notice that Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi had come to visit him. On hearing this, the Shaykh ran to welcome Khwajah Ubaydullah Ahrar and kissed his feet. The Shaykh asked Hadhrat Khwajah Sahib to come inside the house, upon which he related his whole situation and requested to make bay’ah at the hand of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi. Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi accepted his bay’ah, and in that same sitting, gave the Shaykh so much spiritual attention that the Shaykh completed the stages of spiritual perfections. He was also given khilafah during that first meeting. Many of the old mureeds were astonished, for they had been sitting in the company of the Shaykh for many years and were, therefore, surprised that their Shaykh had given Hadhrat Muhammad Zahid rahmatullah alayhi khilafah after just one meeting. Khwajah Ubaydullah Ahrar dispelled their confusion by saying, “Muhammad Zahid came to me with a lamp that was in full

working order; all I had to do was light it.” This event was in fact a proof of the great spiritual powers of Hadhrat Khwajah Sahib and also the immense ability and talent of Hadhrat Mawlana rahmatullah alayhi. Following this meeting, the Shaykh became a great servant to the Silsilah Aaliyah Naqshbandia. The Shaykh passed away in the month of Rabi-ul-Awwal in the year 936 Hijri. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is at a place called Wahsh, near Hisar.

name: Hadhrat Darwesh Muhammad Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The blessed name of this Shaykh was Darwesh Muhammad. Even in his youth, the Shaykh had a saintly manner and often used to spend long periods in the wilderness. There is no doubt that he spent a full fifteen years of his life in intense worship, devotion and abstinence. One day, the Shaykh was so hungry that he turned his face towards the sky, where he saw Hadhrat Khidhr alayhi salaam approaching him, saying, “If it is patience and contentment that you desire, then go and sit in the company of Khwajah Muhammad Zahid rahmatullah alayhi.” So the Shaykh went into the company of Khwajah Muhammad Zahid rahmatullah alayhi, who was, as it happens, the maternal uncle of the Shaykh. He then acquired the stages of perfection from his Shaykh and became his successor after he passed away. The Shaykh’s excellence in terms of taqwa, piety, patience and tawakkul was well-known, and he always preferred anonymity, never seeking the attention of the public. In order that people should not discover his status, the Shaykh used to shy away from company, apart from the time he spent teaching children how to recite the Qur’an. Once a Turkish Shaykh passed through the area and said, “I smell the scent of a true man of Allah from this place.” He was addressing the son of the Shaykh and pointed in the direction of the Hadhrat Darwesh Muhammad rahmatullah alayhi as he spoke. Despite the Shaykh’s attempts to remain out of the public eye, it was only a matter of time before people became aware of his qualities. The following account is related by his son: “A great Shaykh of the age, called Hadhrat Noor-ud-deen rahmatullah alayhi, came to Amkinah and the Shaykh, dressed in old and worn clothes, went to meet him. When they met, Shaykh Noor-ud-deen got up and hugged my father and then they both sat in Muraqabah for a while. After my father left, Shaykh Noor-ud-deen addressed the assembly, saying, “The seekers of the Haq must be reaping great benefit from this Shaykh.” The people replied, “He is not a Shaykh; he just teaches children how to read the Qur’an.” Shaykh Noor-ud-deen was astonished by this reply and said, “Subhanallah! The people of this area are so dead and blind that they do not recognise such a great man of Allah and are not benefiting (spiritually) from his presence.” After this people from all around soon learnt of the Shaykh’s qualities, and began to visit the Shaykh in large numbers to obtain fayz. However the Shaykh did not enjoy his fame and was never at ease with so many people coming to meet him. Spiritually, the Shaykh was also a very powerful man of Allah. Once a Shaykh called Khwarizmi Kurdi rahmatullah alayhi, who was famous for his spiritual prowess, came to the city of the Shaykh. It was the habit of Hadhrat Shaykh Khwarizmi that he would overwhelm and take control of the personal spiritual connections of the Mashaa’ikh of every area that he visited. But

when he came to the city of the Shaykh, Hadhrat Darwesh Muhammad rahmatullah alayhi instead, with his perfections of spiritual power, overwhelmed and took control of the connection of Shaykh Khwarizmi before he even arrived, and emptied him of his spirituality. Then Hadhrat Darwesh Muhammad rahmatullah alayhi set out to meet Shaykh Khwarizmi. Shaykh Khwarizmi felt the loss of his spiritual capacities, and as the Shaykh approached him in the distance, he began to smell the fragrance of the connection that had gone missing. When the Shaykh came into his presence, Shaykh Khwarizmi realised that Hadhrat Darwesh Muhammad rahmatullah alayhi now was in possession of his connection. Shaykh Khwarizmi was humbled, and with great regret and humility said, “I had no idea that your status was so great”, and then in a state of anxiety he made to leave. At this, Hadhrat Shaykh Darwesh Muhammad rahmatullah alayhi took pity on him and returned his connection. But despite the spiritual power of the Shaykh, he still preferred to live in seclusion. The Shaykh’s adherence to the Shari’ah and his following of the Sunnah was exemplary, and his manner in worship was truly outstanding. Hadhrat Mawlana Darwesh rahmatullah alayhi passed away on the ninth of Muharram al-Haram 970 Hijri. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is in a small district called Isqarar, which is in the city of Sabz Mawralnah.

name: Hadhrat Muhammad Waaqif Akangi Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The name of the Shaykh was Khwajigi and he was a resident of a village in Bukhara called Akang. It is for this reason that the Shaykh is known as Akangi. The Shaykh acquired both outer and inner knowledge from his father Khwajah Darwesh Muhammad rahmatullah alayhi and it was from him that he attained khilafah. For thirty years, the Shaykh delivered the message to the people from his father’s seat. The Shaykh would give comprehensive teaching of the Naqshbandi Silsilah as well as teach people the dhikr of Allah. The scholars, Sufis and elite would all come to sit and benefit from the Shaykh’s company. Many great rulers of the time considered it an honour to visit the Shaykh. However this did not ever affect the Shaykh’s manner, for he was an extremely humble Faqeer of Allah. Despite being weak and frail, the Shaykh would bring food for visitors with own hands. Indeed, such was the Shaykh’s humility that he would often take it upon himself to look after the mounts of the guests, whether horses or mules. A sultan of Tawran had a dream. He relates: “I saw that Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam was present and that there was a man standing at the door with a staff in his hand. With utmost respect, this man was putting the requests of the people to Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and then delivering each and every reply of Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam to the one who had asked the question. I saw Allah’s Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam bestow upon me a sword, and that sword was then tied to the back of a saint. That Shaykh was none other than Hadhrat Mawlana Khwajigi Akangi rahmatullah alayhi.” After his dream, the Sultan became such a great follower of the Shaykh that he would come to sit in the company of the Shaykh every morning without fail.

On one occasion, an army of fifty thousand men tried to besiege the city of Samarqand. The ruler of Samarqand, a man named Baqi Muhammad Khan, went straight to the Shaykh and explained the situation, informing the Shaykh that he had an army of only fourteen thousand, which was no match for the invaders. The Shaykh said to him, “If you repent sincerely, from your heart, that you will never oppress Allah’s creation from this day forth, and that you will rule with justice, then victory will be yours.” At this, Baqi Khan did indeed repent sincerely, promising that he would not oppress anyone again. The Shaykh said, “Now go; fight the enemy and have no fear.” Baqi Khan left, and the Shaykh went into a Masjid and sat in Muraqabah. Some time later, the news arrived that Baqi Khan had been victorious. The teachings of the Shaykh were all in accordance with the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. The Shaykh did not attribute much importance to visions and miracles. Once, three seekers came to the Shaykh. Each one of them had questions in his heart, and they were all thinking that if this person were a true friend of Allah, then he would know what they wanted without them telling him. When they came into the presence of the Shaykh, he knew at once what they had come for and answered their thoughts and questions. Then the Shaykh addressed them, saying, “It is through obedience to Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam that one acquires perfections. The greatest miracle is for a person to live his life without performing any act that opposes the Shari’ah. Allah’s friends are not interested in the intentions that you have come with; if you wish to visit them, then do so purely for Allah’s sake, for otherwise you will not receive any benefit from their company.” Once, a darwesh was travelling with the Shaykh and a thorn got stuck in his foot. The Shaykh said to him, “My friend, a person can only truly appreciate the wealth of ownership of the flower if one feels the pain of its thorns.” What he meant by this is that the path of tasawwuf is not a bed of flowers. In fact it is often through mujahidaat (tests) and hardship that one attains the Qurb (nearness) of Allah subhana wa ta’ala. The Shaykh passed away at the age of ninety in the year 1008 AH. A few days earlier, the Shaykh had written a letter to his dearest khalifah Hadhrat Baqi Billah rahmatullah alayhi, which included two couplets that indicated his imminent departure from this world.

name: Hadhrat Baqi Billaah Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was born in Kabul in the year 971 Hijri. It was here that he spent the first years of his life, and where he was raised by his parents and nurtured by his father Qadhi Abd-us-Salam Khalji Samarqandi Qurayshi rahmatullah alayhi, who was himself a pious man of Allah. From childhood, the Shaykh possessed many saintly characteristics and would spend a great deal of time in solitude. The Shaykh learnt his formal Islamic knowledge from Maulana Muhammad Siddique Halwai who was a famous scholar of the age, and he had barely completed his studies when he set foot on the spiritual path of Allah. This led him to sit in the company of many Shaykhs of the time, and in some cases he even did Tawbah at their hand. One day, while the Shaykh was studying a book on Tasawwuf, he was suddenly overcome by a spiritual state in which he was given dhikr by Hadhrat Khwajah Baha’ud-deen Naqshband rahmatullah alayhi. After this experience, the Shaykh lost touch with his senses, and it seemed

as if he was constantly lost in his own thoughts in the manner of one overwhelmed with extreme worry or depression. The Shaykh’s mother was worried about her son’s condition and prayed to Allah, saying, “O Allah, I cannot bear to see my son in this condition. Please relieve him of his pain and grant him his goal or else take my life, for I do not have the strength to see my son in this state.” In later days, the Shaykh would say, “I am where I am today due to the supplication of my mother.” This restless desire led the Shaykh to visit many Masha’ikh in various places, such as Balkh, Badakhshan, Lahore and Kashmir. But it was finally in the company of Hadhrat Maulana Khwajigi Akangi rahmatullah alayhi that the Shaykh found the freedom of the soul for which he was searching. The Shaykh states: “I saw Hadhrat Maulana Khwajigi Akangi rahmatullah alayhi in a dream, and he addressed me, saying, ‘My son, my sight is set in your direction.’” At this, he went to Hadhrat Khwajah Akangi rahmatullah alayhi, and for three days and nights he was granted the sole company of the Shaykh and attained all the inner stages. Hadhrat Khwajigi Akangi rahmatullah alayhi said to him, “By the grace and blessings of Allah, you now possess all the spiritual blessings and stages that are required. Go from here to India, and through you this Silsilah will be revived in that country.” The Shaykh states, “I felt at the time that this task was beyond me and I was incapable of such a big task. I offered this as an excuse to my Shaykh, who then gave me the Hukm of making Istikhara.” The Shaykh relates: “After making Istikhara, I had a dream in which I saw a parrot sitting on the branch of a tree. The thought came to my mind that if this parrot flew down and sat on my hand, it would be a sign for me that my journey to India would be made easier. And that is exactly what happened; the parrot flew over to me and sat on my hand. I put some of my saliva in the beak of the parrot, and in return the parrot put some sugar in my mouth. I related this dream to my Shaykh, who replied, ‘The parrot is a bird of India; in India a man from amongst your companions will arise to light the world with his presence, and you too will benefit from him.’” This dream referred to Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi. So on the instruction of his Shaykh, the Shaykh travelled to Lahore and stayed there for one year. The scholars and pious men of Lahore developed great admiration and love for the Shaykh. After staying in Lahore, he left for Delhi and settled at Qila Ferozi, which was to be his home for the rest of his life. The Shaykh was a very humble, quiet man and was naturally reserved in his manner. It often happened that when a person came to him with a request to enter the Silsilah, the Shaykh would excuse himself from the responsibility. One example of that concerns a person of Khurasan, who used to stay at the blessed shrine of Hadhrat Khwajah Bakhtiyar Kaki rahmatullah alayhi. This person was in search of a true Shaykh and it was for this reason that he stayed at the shrine, hoping that one day he would get some spiritual guidance in this matter. When Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi came to Delhi, this person had a vision in which he saw Bakhtiyar Kaki rahmatullah alayhi saying to him, “A Shaykh of the Naqshbandi Tareeqah has recently arrived in this city; go and sit in his company.” In accordance with the instruction given to him, this person went into the company of the Shaykh and related his vision, to which the Shaykh replied, “You must be mistaken. I am not this worthy, so the Shaykh you have been instructed to meet must be someone else.” On hearing this, the person left. On returning to the shrine, the person had another dream, in which Hadhrat Bakhtiyar Kaki rahmatullah alayhi once again spoke to him, saying, “That was indeed the

Shaykh that I instructed you to meet.” The next day, this person again made his way to the Shaykh and related his dream. The Shaykh again humbly replied, “You are mistaken; go and search for this Shaykh and when you find him, come and tell me so that I too may visit him and obtain some blessings.” A similar experience was that of Hadhrat Khwajah Hisam-ud-deen rahmatullah alayhi who later became a great Khaleefah of the Shaykh. This man also set out in search for the Shaykh and received the same response as the man from Khurasan. In his despair, Hisam-ud-deen walked the streets of Agra and heard someone reciting a couplet of Hadhrat Sa’di rahmatullah alayhi, which made him understand the situation. He immediately went back to Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi and explained his insight into the matter. It was only then that the Shaykh accepted Hadhrat Hisam-ud-deen rahmatullah alayhi. There was a great amount of Jadhb (spiritual rapture) in the company of the Shaykh. When the Shaykh looked at someone, they would lose themselves. Once a person was coming to meet him, and as the Shaykh was coming out of the Masjid, he looked at this person. The person went straight into a state of Jadhb, lost control of his senses and set out for the desert - and nobody knows where he went after that. Some people became Majdhoob (in a state of permanent spiritual rapture) and Maghloob (overcome) just by looking at the blessed face of the Shaykh. It has been related that once a speaker was delivering a sermon from the pulpit when his gaze fell upon the Shaykh, and as soon as this happened, he lost sense of his faculties and fell off the pulpit. It has also been related that one night in Ramadhan, Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi sent a person with some Faloodah (a sweet dish) for the Shaykh. The Shaykh came out to receive the Faloodah and asked the courier his name. The man informed the Shaykh of his name, to which the Shaykh replied, “You are a khadim (servant-mureed) of my Ahmad; hence you are mine too.” When the man returned, he was overcome with Jadhb and Sakr (intoxication) and went screaming to Hadhrat Mujaddid rahmatullah alayhi. He told him about what happened, and said that wherever he looked, whether it was the earth, the skies, the trees or the stones, all he could see was light. The Shaykh was a very kind hearted and merciful man. One night, for instance, when the Shaykh had prayed the tahajjud prayer, he returned to his bed and found a cat sleeping there. Since he did not wish to disturb the cat, the Shaykh remained sitting in the cold till morning. The Shaykh had very little interest in the matters of the Dunya, and in his gatherings he never spoke about worldly matters. If a rich person arrived wanting to offer something to the poor, the Shaykh would not accept it either for himself or for his mureeds. The Shaykh always preferred to live in a state of tawakkul (trust in Allah) and contentment. He would never, for instance, ask for a new set of clothes when his clothes were worn. Despite being very weak and frail, the Shakyh was always busy in Allah’s dhikr and in abundant worship. When he felt weak, he would get up and perform wudhu and then return to Muraqabah. He would often spend the whole night like this. The Shaykh was extremely careful regarding food, taking particular care to make sure that it did not come from the wrong place. He would say, “If the food we eat is from a source that is not good and we do not take due care, a spiritual smoke from the food takes the form of a barrier that prevents fayz from reaching us.” All the actions of the Shaykh were characterised by extreme care.

There was never any singing or loud worship in the gatherings of the Shaykh, to the extent that once, when a Darwesh said “Allah!” out loud in the gathering, the Shaykh said, “If you wish to attend our gatherings, then please make sure that you abide by the adaab (etiquette) that is required.” The Shaykh used to say, “The Mashaa’ikh of the Silsilah Aaliya Naqshbandia have stated that if a person is keen to tread this path, then after making Tawbah, a person should spend all his time in Allah’s dhikr.” He also stated, “The dhikr of this Tareeqah develops Jadhb (rapture).” On another occasion he stated, “If a mureed loves a Shaykh of this Sisilah to the extent that they see him when they are not even in his presence, then that is what we call ‘Rabta’ (connection). And bear in mind that it is essential that you do not do anything that might make the Shaykh dislike you, for this could result in your exclusion from his murads.” He also stated, “This Tareeqah is that of Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique radhiallahu anhu, who had immense love and Ishq for Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and this was the means by which he obtained the fayz. It is for this reason that the most important type of nisbat with the Shaykh is that of love.” The Shaykh also stated, “Regular Muraqabah is a great wealth, for it makes the hearts fertile.” He also mentioned that, “One can never rely on ‘kashf qaboor’, and in ‘kashf sooria’ one can easily be mistaken and led astray”; and he stated, “The Awliya’allah are not free from mistakes. If, on a very rare occasion, you should see them make a mistake, then realise that this is a possibility.” Another saying of his is that, “Tawakkul is a great thing and is not adopted without reason. A person should never engage in earning a livelihood that has certain aspects to it which could lead to a form of shirk. Not to work for a living is disrespectful; one should always choose a suitable profession.” Innumerable karamats have been attributed to the Shaykh, but what greater karamat can there be than the fact that the Shaykh preached for only three to four years, and in that time his fayz reached all parts of the globe. Many Masha’ikh actually finished teaching their mureeds altogether, and came to sit in the company of the Shaykh in order to progress in the stages of Sulook. After the Shaykh reached the age of forty, he used to take a deep breath and say, “He has gone”, every time he was informed of someone’s death. Once the Shaykh said to his wife, “A significant event will happen when I reach the age of forty”; and one day he stated, “Someone has said that the Qutub of the age has passed away.” During the middle of Jumada ath-thani, the Shaykh fell ill; and from that same illness, with the words “Allah! Allah!” on his tongue, the Shaykh passed away on Saturday the 25th of Jumada al-akhir 1012 AH. Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’oon. The grave of the Shaykh is located at a place where the Shaykh had once performed wudhu and some dust from the ground had come onto his body. The Shaykh had stated, “The dust of this place will be my companion. This place is close to the point where the Prophet sallallahu alayhi wa sallam placed his feet.” The shrine of the Shaykh is in an outer district of Delhi towards the Ajmeri Gate, and in accordance with the Shaykh’s instruction, there is no dome on the blessed shrine. A high terrace or platform has been built, however, and the karamat of the Shaykh is such that despite the heat, the ground at this point does not feel hot against one’s feet. To conclude, how true was the following saying of the Shaykh: “Those people who are always attentive towards Allah do not need to have visions; and the visions of this dunya are of no benefit. The essence of the

matter is to follow the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. No kashf could ever compare to that.”

name: Hadhrat Sheikh Ahmad Farooqui Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The blessed name of this Darwesh of Islam was Ahmad. His titles include Badr ud-Deen (Illuminator of the Faith) and from his family name Farooqui he was called Abul-Barakaat (the father of blessings). He acquired the status of Khazeenat ur-Rahmah (the Treasure House of Mercy) and of Qayyoom az-Zamaan (the Pillar of the Age), and the title of Mujaddid Alf Thani (the Reviver of the Second Millenium); and he is also known as Imam-e-Rabbani (the Imam of Wise Guidance) and Mahboob-e-Samdaani (the Beloved of the Self-Sustaining). His madhhab was Hanafi and maslak was Naqshbandi. Hadhrat Shaykh's blessed family lineage goes back twenty-seven generations to his great ancestor Hadhrat Umar al-Farooq radhiallah anhu. In the Naqshbandi Silsilah, Hadhrat Shaykh's chain goes back twenty-four generations to Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. In the Qadiri silsilah, it is twenty-five generations and in the Chishti Silsilah, twenty-seven. However, Hadhrat Shaykh had natural inclination towards the Naqshbandi order and this remained his preferred maslak. It has been related that the blessed day of the Shaykh's arrival into this world was Thursday the fourteenth of Shawwal 971 Hijri, to which the corresponding date on the Gregorian calendar is the twenty-sixth of June 1564. His place of birth, also the place from where the Shaykh enlightened the world with his presence, was a town called Sarhand. At the time of his birth, some extraordinary events were recounted. His mother relates, "After the birth of my son Shaykh Ahmad, I fell unconscious whereupon I had a vision, and saw that my home was full of Awliya'allah who were all congratulating me on the birth of my son". TheShaykh's father Makhdoom Abdul-Ahad rahmatullah alayhi relates, "On the day of the birth of my son, I had a vision in which I saw Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam reciting first the Adhaan and then the Takbir in the ears of my son." In addition, the khalifah of Hadhrat Shaykh Abdul Quddoos Gungohi rahmatullah alayhi, namely Shaykh Abdul Aziz, was present in Sarhand on that day, and in a state of kashf he saw a huge gathering of angels. Shaykh Ahmad was bestowed by Allah subhana wa ta'ala with natural adherence to the Sunnah of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam right from his first days. He was born with the physical requirements of the Sunnah already fulfilled, and as an infant he was unlike other children. He would not cry, would always have a smile on his face and would never be seen naked. When Shah Kamal Kaythli rahmatullah alayhi saw the child, he said, "A huge number of practising scholars and kamil Shaykhs will obtain fayz from this child. The light of his guiding words and instructions will shine until the day of Qiyamah. He will rid the land of innovation and falsehood, and will revive the Sunnah of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam." After saying this, the Shaykh placed his tongue in the baby's mouth, and Hadhrat Shaykh Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi suckled on it. When the Shaykh first went to school, he memorised the Qur'an in a very short space of time. He then became a student of his father and acquired much knowledge very quickly. The Shaykh

could easily solve many complicated masaa'il. His childhood behaviour and pastimes, in fact, were more like those of a youth, and as soon as he finished his studies, the famous scholars of Akbarabad began to talk about the talent of this young man. Akbarabad at the time was the capital city from where the Moghul Emperor Akbar ruled his Empire. The Shaykh went to Akbarabad, and it wasn't long before many great scholars were considering it an honour to be his students and learn Ahadeeth and Tafseer from him. His popularity spread to the extent that a renowned scholar of the time called Abul Fayz Fayzi, who was in the process of writing a Tafseer of the Qur'an, came to the Shaykh requesting assistance regarding a particular point that he could not explain. At his request, Hadhrat Shaykh wrote one detailed and perfect page regarding that particular topic. The scholar was so astonished at the accuracy and knowledge of the Shaykh that he too became a firm believer in the Shaykh. However when Shaykh Ahmad learned that the beliefs of this scholar were not correct, he expressed his dislike for him. It has been related that during this period, Shaykh Sultan had a dream in which he saw Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, who said to him, "Your daughter is the most pious woman of this age; marry her to my son and representative Shaykh Ahmad. This will be extremely beneficial for both yourself and your daughter." He had this same dream on three occasions and each time he was shown the image of the Shaykh. So Shaykh Sultan set out in search for the Shaykh.
