By apparent coincidence, Hadhrat Shaykh happened to be in the area, and upon seeing and recognising the Shaykh, Shaykh Sultan took him home as a guest. Shaykh Sultan informed the Shaykh of his dream and the instruction of Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Hadhrat Shaykh gladly accepted the offer of marriage. Soon afterwards, Hadhrat Shaykh was married and returned to Sarhand with his bride. After marriage, the Shaykh remained in the service of his father and attained the fayz of inner perfections. When his father was getting close to his last days, he gave khilafat to the Shaykh in the Suhrawardi, Chishti and Qadiri Silsilahs, and in the presence of all his sons and companions he appointed the Shaykh as his successor. The Shaykh’s father had attained khilafat in the Suhrawardiyah silsilah from his ancestors, from Hadhrat Shah Kamal Kaythli rahmatullah alayhi in the Qadiriyah silsilah and from Shah Rukn-ud-deen, the son of Hadhrat Shaykh Abd-ul-Quddoos Gungohi, in the Chishtiyah silsilah. Soon after this, Hadhrat Shaykh himself fell very ill, and out of much anxiety his wife prayed two rakats nawaafil prayer and supplicated for his health. While supplicating, she fell into a slumber and heard a person saying, "Do not worry; we have many an important task for this man. Indeed, not even one in a thousand of these have yet been accomplished." And it wasn't long before the Shaykh regained his full health. Hadhrat Shaykh always had an intense desire to visit the Haramayn to perform tawaaf of the Ka'bah and to visit the shrine of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, but due to the health of his father he did not travel. After the demise of his father, the Shaykh made intention for Hajj and set out on the journey. The first stop on the way was Delhi. In Delhi, Mawlana Hasan Kashmiri praised a Shaykh of the Naqshbandi Silsilah who had recently arrived in the city. The name of this Shaykh was Khwajah Baqi Billah rahmatullah alayhi and because Shaykh Ahmad had always had a deep interest in the Naqshbandi silsilah, he was keen to meet him. After the meeting, Hadhrat Baqi Billah rahmatullah alayhi said to the Shaykh that he should stay with him for at least one month. After just two days, the Shaykh was overcome by the Tareeqah, and there followed events that can neither be expressed in words nor understood by the ear.

Hadhrat Shaykh acquired all the stages of the Naqshbandia order within two months and a few days. Hadhrat Khwajah Baqi Billah rahmatullah alayhi states, "Shaykh Ahmad is the meaning of my dream, the dream that caused my Shaykh Khwajah Akangi rahmatullah alayhi to send me to India, saying, 'There will emerge from your companions in India a very great person who will enlighten the world with his presence; and you too will benefit from him.' When I passed the town of Sarhand on my way to Delhi, I was informed through a vision that I was in the neighbourhood of this Qutub, and I was also shown an image of this person. I saw myself lighting a very big lamp, and all the people around me lit their lamps from mine; and when I approached Sarhand, I saw that the whole area and countryside around it was lit up with burning torches." There was no limit to the respect and trust that Shaykh Ahmad had for his Shaykh. One day Shaykh Baqi Billah called for him, and as soon as he heard that his Shaykh had called for him, his whole body began trembling uncontrollably out of fear and reverence. Regarding the love and service that he showed his Shaykh, Shaykh Ahmad writes, "Four persons were blessed with the opportunity to be in the service of Hadhrat Khwajah Sahib at all times, and I was one of them. Until then I had never believed that such love could exist after the time of Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and I am very grateful to Allah subhana wa ta'ala." Never had anyone seen nor heard of such a relationship between a mureed and his Shaykh. On one occasion, Hadhrat Khwajah Baqi Billah rahmatullah alayhi stated, "Mian Ahmad is one of the complete lovers and seekers." Another time he stated, "Under the skies, there is no one like him living today." He was also heard to say, "After the Sahaba and the blessed Tabi'een, there have only been a handful of people like him." Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi himself stated, "It seems that when Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi completed my training, he withdrew from teaching as a Shaykh and transferred his students to me." He also stated, "On the third occasion that I travelled from Sarhand to Delhi to see Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi, Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi said, 'My body has now become very weak indeed and it is evident that I will not live in this world for much longer.'" On returning to Sarhand, the Shaykh realised that this was the last meeting he would have with Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi. Shaykh Ahmad then travelled to Lahore, and it was in Lahore that he learnt that Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi had passed away. As soon as he heard the news, he set off from Lahore to Delhi. The companions of Hadhrat Khwajah rahmatullah alayhi saw his arrival as a great blessing, and the Shaykh attended all the gatherings that took place while he was there. The qualities and virtues of the Shaykh are so great that they are hard to explain. In his Maktoobaat (Collected Writings), volume three, letter 100, it is related that he was made from the dust that was left over after the faultless creation of Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. It has also been related that the Shaykh was given the status of Qayyoomiat. Regarding this, the Shaykh relates the following account: "One day after Zuhr Salaah, I was sitting in Muraqaba reciting the Qur'an by heart, which was my habit, and all of a sudden I saw that I was covered by a glowing robe. This robe of Qayyoomiat, enlightenment and obedience was a gift from Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, for I then saw Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam come before me, tie a turban on my head and congratulate me for the status of Qayoomiat.” The detail of this can be found in Maktoobaat, volume 2, 79-80. It is also the case that Allah

subhana wa ta'ala disclosed to him the secrets of the Mutashaabihaat and Muqatti'aat of the Qur'an. Further, it is related that Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam gave him the tidings that on the Day of Qiyamah, thousands of people would attain salvation through him. It has also been related that the Ka'bah came to the Shaykh. The Shaykh always had an intense desire to visit the Ka'bah, but due to various circumstances was never able to undertake the journey. This inability to travel had made him extremely restless with desire to see the Holy Lands. The Shaykh writes of a vision in which he saw all types of creation - humans, jinn and angels - facing in his direction and prostrating. The Shaykh then realised that he was sitting by the Ka'bah itself, and that the creation was actually prostrating towards it. He then had Ilham that, 'You have always had an intense desire to see the Ka'bah; today we have brought the Ka'bah to you for your Ziyarah'. The place where this happened was at the Khanqah of the Shaykh in Sarhand. During the time of Hadhrat Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi, the Mosque was expanded and the blessed earth where the Ka'bah appeared was raised a little higher than the rest of the Masjid, and this platform serves as a monument for many people who visit Sarhand to this day. Allah subhana wa ta'ala also bestowed the Shaykh with status of Fauq Razaa (Maktoobaat volume 3, number 7). On another occasion, while the Shaykh was in Muraqabah during a gathering, he had Ilham that, "You are forgiven, as well as all the people until the Day Judgement that have connection directly with yourself or your silsilah." Hadhrat Shaykh later stated, "The name of every man and woman that will enter my Silsilah till the Day of Qiyamah has been shown to me; if I want, I can name them all." It has also been related that the Shaykh was informed that any funeral that he attended would lead to the salvation of the deceased. The Shaykh also stated, "All my writings will come before Imam Mahdi and he will accept it all." On another occasion, the Shaykh stated, "The spiritual benefits that Allah subhana wa ta'ala has bestowed upon me will never be matched by any person until the appearance of Imam Mahdi rahmatullah alayhi." Allah subhana wa ta'ala bestowed the Shaykh with Tareeqah Jadeed; before this, the highest stage was 'wilayat-e-sughra' (the Lesser Nearness). Imam Mahdi himself will be connected with this Silsilah. It is a very noteworthy point that in his numerous visions and extensive knowledge through kashf, the Shaykh described in great detail the qualities of Allah subhana wa ta'ala, and at no point did his descriptions contradict the Shari'ah. The excellence of the Shaykh amongst the Awliya is like the excellence of the Ool-ul-Azm prophets amongst all Prophets. The Shaykh related the following vision: "I saw myself performing tawaaf around a place that I did not recognise. Then I saw myself joined by angels and Prophets; the place where we were is fauq ul-arsh (above the heavens)." In another vision, the Shaykh states, "Hadhrat Ali radhiallah anhu came to me and said, 'I have come to teach you 'Ilm-e-Samawaat' (the knowledge of the heavens)." The Shaykh stated, "When I look into the Ijtihad of Hanafi and Shafi'i fiqh, I find two parts Haq coming from Imam Abu Hanifah rahmatullah alayhi and one part Haq coming from Imam Shafi'i rahmatullah alayhi; and neither of them transgresses the boundaries of truth." The Shaykh stated, "With the eye of kashf, I saw that the Hanafi madhhab is a great river of light compared to all the other schools of fiqh, which are more akin to fountains or springs of light. The Shaykh states, "I had a dream in which Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam gave me a certificate, similar to the type of permission letter a Shaykh gives to his Khaleefah. Then it

was realised that this letter was incomplete, and a person came to me and retrieved the letter. He later returned with a complete certificate, inscribed with the stamp of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. The words 'You have been given the permission for shafa'at in the Akhirah' were written on the back of the messenger who brought the certificate.” We could quite easily celebrate many more karamats and visions of the Shaykh. The reality, however, is that the status of the Shaykh is much greater and higher than this. In fact, the Shaykh's greatest achievement was the way he invited people to the Haq and revived the Deen. The Shaykh stood up for Islam in an extremely torrid age. Many different forces were at work trying their best to cut the branches, in fact cut the roots of Islam. One thousand years had passed since the time of Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam and the second millennium of the Islamic era had just begun. Enemies were attacking Islam from all sides. From one direction, new customs and innovations were being introduced into Islam. From another direction, deviant scholars and Sufis were polluting the fundamental beliefs of Islam. From yet a third angle, the enemies of the Sahaba were busily inciting people against the Khulafa Rashideen, and were not afraid to criticise and talk ill of the companions of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. And fourthly, the Hindus and Christians of the age were working hard to end Islamic law and rule. The influence of all these groups was so strong that the Moghul Emperor of the time, Jalaluddin Akbar, became an enactor of Laws that were both culturally and essentially in opposition to Islamic belief. The great achievement of the Shaykh was that he stood up, against all the odds, and revived the Shari'ah and Sunnah of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam in an age and place where this seemed imossible. In an age when kufr, shirk, fisq, darkness, transgression and remorseless sin were prevalent, in an age when the masses were disillusioned and drifting away from Islam, the Shaykh raised once again the banner of Tawheed and Sunnah and rid the land of the darkness that was covering it. Allamah Suyooti rahmatullah alayhi narrates a Hadeeth of Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam in his book 'Majma'-al-jawaami'. This Hadeeth is a prophecy referring to the Mujaddid that would come one thousand years after the time of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam stated, "A man will come in my Ummah who will be known as 'Sila'. A huge number of people will enter Paradise through him." In the Maktoobaat, volume 2, letter 6, the Shaykh writes to his son Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi, saying, "I feel that the reason for which I was created has today been accomplished, and a request of one thousand years has been accepted. I am utterly grateful to Allah subhana wa ta'ala who made me the one to unite two oceans and made me the conciliator between two important groups." One proof of the Shaykh's steadfastness on the Haq is as follows. When the Emperor Jahangir came to the throne, his wife, who held Shiite beliefs, influenced him strongly. Hence many of the people around him, including some advisors, were Rafidhites. Without any fear or worry, the Shaykh wrote books and articles that refuted their beliefs. It wasn't long before these people became enemies of the Shaykh, and began to speak to the Emperor, telling him, 'This Shaykh is very dangerous. His beliefs are corrupt, and he is against you and will not bow down before you." On being told these rumours, the Emperor called for the Shaykh and commanded him to bow down before him. The Shaykh vehemently refused, saying, "Prostration is for the Lord of the Worlds alone. How can I bow down before a dependant creation such as yourself?" Upon

this, the Emperor commanded for the Shaykh to be executed - but this did not bother the Shaykh at all. However Jahangir changed his mind, and commanded that the Shaykh be imprisoned in Gwalior Fort for an unlimited period. The Shaykh's state of patience and gratitude was such that he never moved his lips in wishing ill upon his enemies, nor did he allow his offspring and those that served him to do so. Many thousands of prisoners in Gwalior Fort embraced Islam at the hand of the Shaykh, and a very many of these took bay'ah and attained high stages of wilayat from the company of the Shaykh. The Shaykh would say, "If the Emperor had not imprisoned me, so many thousands of people would have been deprived of the light of Islam." This imprisonment allowed him to fulfil the Sunnah of Yusuf alayhi salaam, for he endured the hardships of captivity with the utmost patience. The Shaykh wrote to his sons and friends from the prison, saying, "Although hardship is indeed distasteful, it is a blessing. Praise Allah and do not spend even a moment in neglect. Always be busy in one of three things; the first is recital of Qur'an, the second is Salaah, and the third, abundance of dhikrullah. Always be pleased with whatever state Allah has given you. Pray that Allah gathers us all in Paradise, and that our meeting each other in this Dunya is for the Akhirah itself." Despite all the hardship suffered by the Shaykh in prison, the Emperor noticed that he was unmoved from his original stance. In addition, the karamah of the Shaykh had come to the Emperor's notice in that thousands of thieves and bandits had attained guidance and become pious people through the company of the Shaykh. It was at this point that the Emperor began to feel real regret for his actions. At around this time, the Emperor Jahangir had a dream in which he saw Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam biting his blessed finger and saying, "O Jahangir, you have imprisoned a very great person!" After this dream, Jahangir sorely regretted his actions and demanded the immediate release of the Shaykh. The Shaykh was brought to the Emperor, who apologized and asked the Shaykh to forgive him. The Emperor now began to treat the Shaykh with the utmost respect and would serve him himself. Indeed, his love for the Shaykh increased so much that Jahangir would find the time that he was not in the company of the Shaykh unbearable. Shah Jahan (the emperor’s son) was also amongst the mureeds of the Shaykh, and other members of the ruling group, including scholars and ministers, continued to join the Silsilah Mujaddidia right up to and including the reign of Alamgir Aurangzeb. In that same land, in the midst of the ruling group that had been advocators of kufr, shirk, innovation and Shi'ism, the Awliya' and scholars of the Haq were now common place through the blessed presence of the Shaykh, so much so the Emperor ordered that at any given moment, there should be four practising scholars fully immersed in checking the laws of the state, to make sure that the Shari'ah was upheld. Through Jihad of the tongue and pen, Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi gradually rid Jahangir's court of all non-Islamic laws. The congregations in the Mosques began to increase, and Shari'ah law was gradually implemented over the land. It wasn't long before Jahangir, the Moghul Emperor of India, himself did Tawbah at the blessed hand of the Shaykh, became a mureed and whole heartedly worked hard to rid his life from sin. Once the mission of the Shaykh had been accomplished, he increasingly began to prefer solitude and seclusion. One day the Shaykh stated, "It seems that my time for departure is

near." He wrote to his sons, saying, "Yesterday, during the Muraqabah after the Morning Prayer, I noticed that the robe I would usually wear was not with me, and it was replaced by another." Later the Shaykh appointed Khwajah Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi as his successor, and instructed all his Khulafa’ and mureeds to make bay'ah at the hand of Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi. The responsibility of running of the Khanqah was also passed on. If any new people came to the Shaykh asking to be his mureeds, the Shaykh would send them to Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi. On the fifteenth night of Sha'ban, the Shaykh heard his wife saying, "Allah subhana wa ta'ala knows best the names that have been deleted from the list of those that are to live another year." On hearing this, Shaykh said, "Can anyone imagine the state of a person who can see his name being deleted from the list with his own eyes?" Some people related that during these days, they asked the Shaykh why he had isolated himself so much from creation. He replied that his time for leaving this world was very close and that he had reached the age of sixty three, exactly the age at which Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam had passed away, so he knew that he too would pass away very soon. The Shaykh stated, "O men of Allah! I have passed on to you everything that has been given to me by Allah and His Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. In the struggle to uphold the true Deen of Islam, I worked hard and relentlessly all my life. I was a victim of oppression and tolerated much hardship, but despite the harshest of harsh attempts by various forces to destroy the cause, I remained steadfast and never allowed myself to be complacent. Now I am to part from you, and I leave you in the hands of the Lord of the Worlds. Our next meeting will be under the banner of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam on the Day of Qiyamah." On hearing this, those present could not hold themselves back and began to weep uncontrollably, and all began to say, "O Imam ul-Auliya! There is no doubt whatsoever that you have striven relentlessly in the struggle to uphold the Shari'ah, and to revive the Deen of Islam. And Insha'allah we will testify to this fact on the Day of Judgement." After this the Shaykh made du'a and then proceeded from the Khanqah. After six to seven months of solitude, the Shaykh went for the last time to the blessed shrines that were the resting places of his dear father and his respected grandfather Hadhrat Imam Rafee'udeen rahmatullah alayhi. After this, the Shaykh fell ill and did not recover. On the 13th of Safar this illness was added to by a high fever. Despite being so ill, the Shaykh continued to pray Salaah in congregation and did not slacken in his habit of dhikr and Muraqabah. The illness got worse and at the time of Chaasht on Tuesday the 28th of Safar 1034 AH, the 10th of December 1624 AD, the Shaykh left this Dunya to meet his Lord. A summary of the advice and pearls of guidance that the Shaykh left with his sons, mureeds and Khulafa' is as follows: "Remain steadfast upon Shari'ah and Tareeqah. Stay away from the company of those Mashaa'ikh whose lives contain practices that are in opposition to the Shari'ah. Miracles and dancing have no place in worship. Do dhikr and Muraqabah in abundance. Always be busy in the remembrance of Allah subhana wa ta'ala. It is impossible to progress in terms of inner character and to be steadfast upon the Shari'ah if one is not firmly adhering to the Sunnahs of Allah's Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. If there is a person showing miracles or one who seems to do the impossible, but his actions in general life are in opposition to the Shari'ah, then these are not miracles but merely a deception." The Shaykh informed them

that if they were to act upon his advice, it would be a way of achieving salvation in the Hereafter and a key to the progress in one's desire to possess inner knowledge. The complexion of the Shaykh was a light-brown wheat colour. He had a wide forehead that always possessed a radiant noor. The Shaykh had thin, curved eyebrows and his teeth were all in proportion. He had a broad and dense beard and was tall and delicate in build. Many scholars, pious men and fuqara saw the Shaykh in their dreams and in that state were given dhikr and were guided. Later they would seek the company of the Shaykh, and tread the path of Sulook. The Shaykh's dress code was like that of the Sahaba radhiallah anhum. He wore a sizeable Amaamah with a miswak tucked into it. The end of the Amaamah would hang between his shoulder blades, and the neck of his shirt parted over both shoulders. The Shaykh’s lower garment would always hang above his ankles, and he would walk with a staff. Thus the Shaykh was fully immersed in the Sunnah of Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. The blessed shrine of the Shaykh is at Sarhand in India, and is a fountain of blessings for both common and distinctive people alike. Regarding the blessed shrine, Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi stated, "Because of the exceptional adherence to the Sunnah and obedience to Allah's Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, our Hadhrat was given the glad tiding that the shrine that contains his grave and its courtyard are part of Riyadh-ul-Jannah.” The notable karamaat of the Shaykh are his sons, his five thousand Khulafaa akram and his letters, known as the Maktoobaat. These letters will continue to be a source of guidance for seekers of truth all over the world until the Day of Qiyamah.

name: Hadhrat Muhammad Ma’soom Farooqui Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh was the khaleefah and third son of Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi. He was born on the 10th of Shawwaal 1002 Hijri. The Shaykh's father stated, "The birth of this son was very blessed for us, since it was soon afterwards that I had the honour of meeting Hadhrat Khwajah Baqi Billah rahmatullah alayhi for the first time.” The Shaykh was admitted to a Dar-ul-Uloom, and after memorising the Qur'an, he set about acquiring the knowledge of other Islamic Sciences. The tawajjuh (attention) of Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi was upon the Shaykh from his childhood. Once he travelled with his father to Delhi. One day, close to midday, he fell asleep on his father's bed. Shortly afterwards, Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi arrived. A servant of the Khanqah wished to wake him, but Hadhrat told him not to and instead came back outside saying, "A friend of Allah is resting, and I am worried about disturbing him." He then sat down until the Shaykh woke up by himself. At the age of eleven, the Shaykh acquired the Tareeqah from his father. When the Shaykh was fourteen, he related, " In a dream, I have seen a light by which the whole world is illuminated shining out from my body." Upon hearing this dream, Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi said to him, "You are the Qutb of this age."

In terms of strict adherence to the Sunnah and having a high degree of Taqwah, the Shaykh was just like his father. He acquired the spiritual station called Wilayat-e-Muhammadi sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. The emperor Aurangzeb Alamgeer became a mureed and then a khaleefah of the Shaykh, and thus the empire, centred at Delhi, was run under the instruction of the Shaykh. The Silsilah spread like never before under the guidance of the Shaykh. It is related that he had approximately nine hundred thousand mureeds, of whom seven thousand were Khaleefahs. The Shaykh's father gave him the news that he had been given the status of Qayyoomiat. There are many karamaat attributed to the Shaykh. He stated, “Once, I was sitting in the gathering of dhikr after Fajr when I saw Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam come to me and hug me, saying, 'Allah subhana wa ta'ala has given you the title of Urwat-ul-Wusqa. Be grateful for this great blessing.'” The Shaykh went for Hajj and related, "During the days of Tashreeq, we came to the city from Mina. Upon completing Tawaaf, we saw an angel handing me a stamped letter which said that the acts of Hajj had been accepted." The Shaykh also stated, “The main goal of life is to seek the Ma'rifat (knowledge) of Allah, and Ma'rifat is of two kinds. Many great scholars have mentioned the first type, and the second type is the Ma'rifat which is in the hands of the Soofia Karaam. The first type is within the sphere of knowledge, whilst the second is within the sphere of Haal (spiritual states). The first type is not something that is always just 'done', while the second type can only be 'done'. The first type is obtained through completion of Hasooli 'Ilm (outer knowledge), whilst the second is the completion of Ilm-e-Hadhoori (knowledge of the presence of Allah).” The Shaykh stated that the Silsilah Naqshbandiah is the Tareeqah of the Sahabah and that it contains Istafaad-ul-Nakaasi (reflected benefits), meaning that the company of the Shaykh with all Adaab (respect) is essential, and the wazaa'if and adhkaar (lessons and types of dhikr) come after this in terms of importance. It is a condition of this Silsilah that the Sunnah be followed in a superlative manner, and that one be distant from innovations. In this Tareeqah, the more a mureed tries to keep the link with his Shaykh, the greater the Fuyooz (blessings) and barakaat. The things that help to create this link are: to have love for the Shaykh in the heart, as well as through outward actions; to serve the Shaykh and have utmost Adab (respect) for him, since a disrespectful person can never reach Allah. About two to three days before his death, the Shaykh wrote to pious men from near and far, saying, "The time for my departure is now here. Pray for me that it passes in a good manner." On the Friday, just one day before he passed away, the Shaykh came to the Mosque and, as was his habit, he prayed Fajr and sat in Muraqabah dhikr until Ishraaq. At the time of his death, the Shaykh’s tongue was seen to be moving quickly. His sons listened closely and heard that he was reciting Surah Yaseen. On the afternoon of the 9th of Rabi-ul-Awwal in the year 1079 Hijri, the Shaykh passed away. His tomb is in Sarhand, and is a blessed sight for the world.

name: Hadhrat Sayfuddeen Rahmatullah Alayh
biography: The Shaykh was the fifth son of Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi, and was born at Sarhand in the year 1049 Hijri. He acquired all the stages of the Mujaddidi silsilah from his father while he was still in his youth. The emperor at the time was Aurangzeb Alamgeer, and he put forward a request to Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi to send him one of the Shaykh's Khulafaa so that he could be guided and gain some spiritual attention. In answer to this request, the Shaykh sent Hadhrat Khwajah Sayf-ud-deen rahmatullah alayhi to Delhi, where he was greeted with much respect and reverence on entering the city. When the Shaykh reached the doors of the fort, he saw engraved pictures of elephants. At this, he said, "I shall only enter the fort when these pictures have been broken." They were then torn down and the Shaykh entered the fort. In a similar manner, the Shaykh cleansed the fort of everyting that conflicted with the Shari'ah. The emperor was very happy with this characteristic of the Shaykh, through whose blessings the entire household of the emperor and many of his ministers entered the Mujaddidi silsilah. After his stay in Delhi, the Shaykh returned to Sarhand. He began to fulfil his rights and responsibility towards the silsilah after his father passed away. The Khanqah of the Shaykh was so busy that it was constantly full of visiting mureeds and people thirsty for Allah's dhikr. Many karamaat (miracles) are attributed to the Shaykh. Once, a mureed of the Shaykh was on a journey from Kabul to Iraq. This mureed met a rafizi along his way, who was blasphemous and uttered appalling words about Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique and Hadhrat Umar radhiallah anhuma. The mureed lost his temper and killed the rafizi, and when he had calmed down, he began to worry that his people might come searching for him and take their revenge. He was just thinking about what to do when a veiled person on horseback appeared before him and said, "Do not worry, for I have changed his body to that of a donkey." The mureed looked across at the body and saw that it indeed had changed to a donkey. The mureed asked the veiled person if he could see who he was. The person removed his veil and the mureed saw that it was his Shaykh Hadhrat Sayf-ud-deen rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh used to say, "Here we have no need for performing strange miracles that oppose nature, nor do we find any need to add things to the Deen. The important things are the company of the Shaykh, the gatherings of Dhikr and the following of the Sunnah.” The Shaykh passed away at the age of 47. During the funeral procession, the Shaykh's body floated into the air. Everyone wanted to carry it on their shoulders but this was not possible. In fact, it stopped by itself when it reached the grave. The shrine of the Shaykh is in Sarhand.
