name: Hadhrat Noor Muhammad Badyooni Rahmatullah Alayh
biography: The Shaykh was accomplished in the formal knowledge of Fiqh, and he acquired all the stages of Sulook from Hadhrat Shaykh Sayfudeen, who was the son and khalifah of Hadhrat Khwajah Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi. He was so absorbed in Allah's dhikr that for fifteen years the Shaykh was not aware of the world other than at times of Prayer. He used to do so much dhikr that his back became hunched from sitting constantly in Muraqabah. The Shaykh was very careful in following the Sunnah. He was particularly careful about earning a halaal livelihood and also kept his distance from people continually obsessed with worldly matters. His visions and inner illuminations were exceptional; they were so clear that it was as if he were seeing them with his eyes. One day a Mureed of the Shaykh was coming to sit in his company, and on his way, his gaze fell upon a non-mahram woman. As soon as he arrived in the company of the Shaykh, the Shaykh said to him, "You have committed the sin of Zina". The Shaykh used to be able to tell people who sat in his company what they had done before they came to see him; he would know whether they had done dhikr nafi athbaat (Laa ilaha illallah) and whether the had recited Darood Shareef. Once a woman came to the Shaykh and said, "A jinn has kidnapped my daughter, and I have tried performing many amals to get her back but have failed. Please can you help me in this matter." On hearing what the woman had to say, the Shaykh went into muraqabah for a long while, after which he said to the woman, "Your daughter will come back at such and such a time." At exactly that given time, the woman's daughter re-appeared. On being asked, the girl said, "I was sitting in the desert and I saw a saintly man arrive. He took hold of my hand and brought me here." The Shaykh passed away on the 11th of Dhi Qa'dah in the year 1125 Hijri. His blessed shrine is in Dehli, a short distance from that of Hadhrat Nizaam-ud-deen Awliya rahmatullah alayhi.

name: Hadhrat Mirza Mazhar Jaane Jaanan Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Hadhrat Mirza Mazhar Jaan-e-Jaanan rahmatullah alayhi was born on the morning of Friday the 11th of Ramadhan in the year 1111 Hijri. This was during the reign of the Moghul Emperor Aurangzeb, and the Shaykh’s father held a very high post in the Emperor's court. The name Jaan-e-Jaanan was given to the Shaykh by Emperor Aurangzeb, who himself was a very pious-hearted man. The Shaykh's family lineage links back to Hadhrat Ali karramallah wajhu. He is one of the most revered khulafaa of Hadhrat Sayyad Noor Muhammad Badayooni rahmatullah alayhi. Hadhrat Muhaddith Shah Waliullah Dehlawi rahmatullah alayhi tells of the incomparable excellence of the Shaykh. The Shaykh himself said, "When I was nine years old, I saw Hadhrat Ibraheem Khaleelullah alayhi salaam in my dream, and he showed me much respect." The Shaykh also said, "Whenever I mention and remember Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddique radhiallah anhu, his image comes before me." He also stated, "I have seen Abu Bakr Siddique radhiallah anhu many times, and have always found him to be very merciful about my state." He also said, "On one occasion,

I saw a very bright light like that of the Sun, from which came forth the blessed being of Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi. I mentioned this to my father, who said to me, 'Insha'allah you will obtain Fayz (spiritual blessing) from the Tareeqah of that great Shaykh.’" The Shaykh's father took great care in the education of his son, and he reached a very high standard in every field. Apart from the knowledge of Qiraa’ah, Fiqh and Hadeeth, the Shaykh also mastered other fields of Islamic knowledge. After acquiring Nisbat with Hadhrat Sayyad Noor Muhammad Badayooni rahmatullah alayhi, the Shaykh was so overwhelmed with love for his Shaykh that when he looked in the mirror, he would see the image of his Shaykh rather than his own. This love and aqeedah for his Shaykh continued to increase all the time, and it was due to this immense love that he frequently used to visit the blessed grave of his Shaykh for six years after he had passed away. The Shaykh stated, “One day I asked my Shaykh if I could have permission in the Qaadiri Silsilah. My Shaykh replied, ‘Come, let us put your request to join this Silsilah to Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.’ At this, my Shaykh put his tawajjuh towards Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam and also instructed me to do the same. I then saw Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam accompanied by all his Sahaba and the Awliyaa Azzaam radhiallah anhum ajmaeen. They were all present in the blessed company of Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and Hadhrat Ghaws Abdul Qaadir Jilaani rahmatullah alayhi was also there. My Hadhrat Shaykh approached Allah's Rasool sallallahu alayhi wa sallam and said, ‘Mirza Jaan-e-Jaanan is hopeful of being accepted in the Silsilah Qaadiriyyah.’ To this Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam replied, ‘You must see Sayyad Abdul Qaadir rahmatullah alayhi about this matter.’ Then my Shaykh approached Abdul Qaadir Jilaani rahmatullah alayhi and put the same request. The request was accepted and I was given permission in the Qaadiri silsilah; I was also granted permission in the Suhrawardi and Chishti orders.” On another occasion, the Shaykh stated, "I have rectified my actions to accord with Ahadeeth and Fiqh. If you see me do anything that opposes the Shari'ah, then please inform me." He also stated, "Everything that I have ever obtained is due to the overwhelming love that I have for my great Shaykh. The actions of a man hold no weight, nor can they make him close to Allah subahana wa ta'ala unless they are accompanied by love for those who are themselves loved and accepted by Allah." The Shaykh also stated, "To have love for the Ahl-e-Bayt, and revering and respecting the blessed Sahabah radhiallahu anhum is essential; and that is the straight path." Once, a disrespectful rafizi uttered some insulting words about Hadhrat Umar al-Farooq radhiallah anhu, and the Shaykh was so angered by this that he immediately took out a dagger. The rafizi was frightened and said, "For the sake of Imam Hussain radhiallah anhu, let me live!" Upon hearing the name of Imam Hussain radhiallah anhu, the Shaykh's temper was calmed and he let the man go. The Shaykh stated, "In this Tareeqah, Peers, mureeds, bay'ah, shajarah and the like are not the only things. In fact, to act upon the teachings of your Shaykh, to do the dhikr of the heart and to keep the company of the Shaykh are vitally important." The Shaykh also said, "A person should do dhikr in abundance, for without abundant dhikr, the heart does not open." He also stated, “You should spend your spare moments in dhikr and worship, for this keeps the mind clear of impure thoughts."

One day, while commenting on the favours of Allah subhana wa ta'ala, the Shaykh said, "There is no desire left in the heart of this faqeer except for one, which is that Allah subhana wa ta'ala has given a very great status to martyrdom, and many of His beloved servants have had the privilage of being martyred.” Allah subhana wa ta'a'a accepted this du'a, and on the night of Ashoorah, the Shaykh was martyred by a rafizi. The shrine of the Shaykh is in Dehli.

name: Hadhrat Abdullah Shah Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The Shaykh, who was a descendant of Hadhrat Ali karramallah wajhu, was born at a place called Bataala in Punjab, in the year 1158 Hijri. Prior to the birth of the Shaykh, Hadhrat Ali radhiallah anhu appeared to his father in a dream and told him to name his son Ali, and so his father named him when he was born. It took only one month for the Shaykh to memorise the Qur'an by heart. In his youth, the Shaykh sat in the company of various Shaykhs but did not find the peace of heart that he sought, until finally he came into the overwhelming company of Hadhrat Mirza Mazhar Jaan-e-Jaanan rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh requested that Hadhrat Mirza Mazhar Jaan-e-Jaanan rahmatullah alayhi accept him in the silsilah, and it was then that he made bay'ah at the hand of his Shaykh. He remained in the company of his Shaykh for fifteen years, after which he was given permission by his Shaykh and made a khaleefah. It was then that he started the work of spreading the Naqshbandi Tariqah, and the fayz of the Shaykh spread at a tremendous rate, possibly more so than during the life of any other shaykh. The Shaykh had Khulafaa in many lands including India, Kabul, Balkh, Bukhara, Arabia and Turkey. Hadhrat Shah Sahib would say, "Our fayz has reached many far-off lands; our gatherings take place in Makkah Mu'azzama and Madeenah Munawwarah, and also take place in Baghdad Shareef, Turkey and the West.” Hadhrat Maulana Khalid Roomi rahmatullah alayh was sent by Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam from Madeenah to come into the company of the Shaykh in Dehli. When he arrived, he was given Khilafah and permission before he returned to his homeland Kurdistan. There are countless karamaat attributed to the Shaykh, the biggest of which was that he filled the hearts of the seekers of Allah with fayz and blessings. Once, a person was travelling to Dehli in order to meet the Shaykh and take bay'ah, when he lost his way and ended up in a deserted area. He had no idea which way to go, when suddenly a saintly man appeared and showed him the right direction. The person asked his guide, “Who are you?" The guide replied, "I am the person who you are travelling to meet and with whom you intend to make bay'ah.” The Shaykh stated, “I once saw myself sitting down, and a pious man of Allah came and sat by my side. I asked him, ‘Who are you?’ and he replied, ‘Baha'uddeen Naqshband’”. The Shaykh further relates that he was once visited by Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi, who said to him, "You are my Khaleefah". The Shaykh mentions that it was his habit to recite tasbeeh, do dhikr and then send its reward to the Soul of Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. He did this every night before going to sleep. One night, the Shaykh did not do this and he saw Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam in his dream, who reminded him about his ommision.

Once, the son of a Brahman came to the blessed gathering of the Shaykh. When the blessed gaze of the Shakyh fell upon this man, he began to recite the kalimah shahadah and became a Muslim. The Shaykh taught that the night of Qadr is a very blessed night indeed, a night during which prayers and worship are accepted. The Shaykh said, "Once I was sitting in I'tikaaf in the Jaami'ah Masjid. I would sleep a little while during the night, and one night a person came. He woke me and said, ‘Awake and supplicate for the Ummah of the Messenger sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.’ I got up and saw that all the spiritual lights were fully illuminated. On seeing this, I realised that this was the Noor of Laylat-ul-Qadr." The Shaykh also stated, "Once I was sitting in Muraqabah, and I saw that Hadhrat Baba Fareed-ud-deen Shakr Ganj rahmatullah alayhi had come to my house. The whole house was illuminated by his Noor and he said to me, ‘Come, let me give you the knowledge of dhikr.’ I replied, ‘I thank you for asking me, but the dhikr that I have learnt from my Shaykh is sufficient for me.’” The Shaykh also used to say that in the Naqshbandi Tareeqah there is less mujahida than in other Silsilahs. In this Tareeqah, success depends totally on the sincerity you have in regard to your Shaykh. The Shaykh passed away on the 22nd of Safar 1240 Hijri. He was buried close to his Shaykh, Hadhrat Mirza Mazhar Jaane Jaanan rahmatullah alayhi, at Khanqah Mazhariyah.

name: Hadhrat Abu Sa’eed Ahmad Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Hadhrat Shah Abu Sa'eed rahmatullah alayhi was born at a place called Raampur on the 2nd of Dhil Qa'adah 1196 Hijri. The Shaykh was a descendant of Imam-e-Rabbani Mujaddid Alf Thani rahmatullah alayhi from the line of his son Hadhrat Khwaja Muhammad Ma'soom rahmatullah alayhi. After memorising the Qur'aan and completing his studies, he made bay'ah at the hand of Hadhrat Shah Dargaahi rahmatullah alayhi, who was a Shaykh from the Mujaddidia Zubayria silsilah. The Shaykh was of noble character from a very young age. The Shaykh states, “In my early days, I once went to Lucknow. When going to the local Mosque to pray, I used to come across a Majdhoob person sitting naked in the street. But whenever he saw me, he would quickly cover himself. Somebody asked him the reason for this. The man replied, "There will come a time when this person (refering to Shaykh Abu Sa'eed rahmatullah alayhi) will attain such a great status that people will be overwhelmed and amazed." Hadhrat Shah Dargaahi rahmatullah alayhi paid a lot of attention to the Shaykh, and he was given Khilafah and Ijaazah after a very short period of time. The Shaykh then also had Nisbat with Hadhrat Ghulam Ali Shah Sahib rahmatullah alayhi. When the Shaykh came into the service of Shah Sahib rahmatullah alayhi, he was shown a great deal of respect and regard. Hadhrat Ghulam Ali Shah Sahib rahmatullah alayhi moved from his place and motioned for him to sit where he was sitting, and said, "Your place is here." Abu Sa'eed rahmatullah alayhi replied, "I have come into your service to gain benefit from your company and to obtain

blessings through serving you and picking up your shoes”. Hadhrat Shah Sahib rahmatullah alayhi accepted him, and the Shaykh remained in the company of Hadhrat Shah Sahib rahmatullah alayhi for fifteen years. After Hadhrat Shah Sahib passed away, the Shaykh was left in charge of the Khanqah, where he continued to give Fayz to the seekers of truth. There are many Karamaat attributed to the Shaykh. Once, when the Shaykh was absent, an argument took place in the Khanqah and some people made a lot of noise and were disrespectful. One person relates, "I had a dream in which I saw Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam enter the Khanqah. The Prophet in his anger mentioned a few names and said that they should be thrown out of the Khanqah. Extremely fearful that my name would be the next to be mentioned, I woke up." He immediately went into the company of Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed rahmatullah alayhi. He found the Shaykh busy performing wudhu for Tahajjud prayer, so he remained silent. When the Shaykh saw him, he reassured him by saying, "Why are you worried? Your name was not mentioned." Afterwards the Shaykh removed from the Khanqah all those whose names had been mentioned in the person’s dream. After returning from the journey to the Haramayn Shareefayn, the Shaykh fell very ill. On the day of Eid the pangs of death started, and he asked a Hafiz to recite Surah Yaseen. When the Hafiz had recited it three times, the Shaykh said, "Stop now, for there is no more time." The Shaykh passed away on the day of Eid-ul Fitr in the year 1250 Hijri. He was buried close to the shrine of Hadhrat Shah Ghulam Ali Sahib rahmatullah alayhi.

name: Hadhrat Ahmad Sa’eed Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Hadhrat Shah Ahmad Sa'eed was the khaleefah and also the son of Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed rahmatullah alayhi. He was born at Raampur in the year 1217 Hijri. When the Shaykh was only ten years old, he used to sit in the company of Hadhrat Shah Ghulam Ali Sahib, and Hadhrat Shah Ghulam Sahib showed great affection for him and gave him much attention. If he noticed him in a gathering, he would motion for him to come and sit close. Once, the Shaykh was sitting in front of Hadhrat Shaykh Ghulam Sahib when the latter said, "Hadhrat Imam-e-Rabbaani Mujaddid Alf Thani has written “Imam Mahdi will get Nisbat (link) with a Shaykh who will be one of my descendants.”” Hadhrat Shah Ghulam Sahib continued, saying, "To me, it seems that this Shaykh will come from the offspring of this boy." When the Shaykh's father went to perform Hajj, he appointed the Shaykh in his place, and Hadhrat Shah Ahmad Sahib became busy in the work of spreading the Shari'ah and Tareeqah. He would hold three gatherings every day, after the morning prayer, after Dhuhr and after Maghrib. The Shaykh used to say, "The Mureed is like a suckling baby. He is unaware of what profits or harms him. If a baby stops drinking milk before it is time, then this harms his growth. In the same way, if a mureed ceases to strive on the path of sulook before he has any capacity, he becomes defective and useless." The Shaykh also said, “The seekers of Allah should make sure that they do not spend even a moment away from Allah's dhikr, so that their relationship with Allah becomes total, to the extent

that their hearts have no desires or ambitions other than Allah. They should remain steadfast upon their daily wazaaif." The Shaykh had endless Kashf and karamaat. He relates that, "Once I saw myself with Rasoolullah salallahu alayhi wasallam, and we were both eating together from the same dish." On an another occasion, he said, "Once Hadhrat Mujaddid Alf Thani came to me (in a vision) with some food , saying, ‘Rasoolullah salallahu alayhi wasallam has sent this especially for you.’" At a time when war was blighting the land, he performed Hijrah from Dehli towards the Haramayn Shareefayn, and he left Hadhrat Dawst Muhammad in charge of the Khanqah. In the month of Safar in the year 1270 Hijri, the Shaykh arrived in Makkah Mu'azzamah. He stayed there for four months before leaving for Madeenah Munawwarah. The Shaykh said, "I resolved to make Madeenah Munawwarah my place of residence, for that is the wish of Allàh's Messenger salallahu alayhi wasallam." Many people of the Haramayn Shareefayn entered the Silsilah through the Shaykh. After living for 2 years in Madeenah, he passed away on the 2nd of Rabi-ul-Awwal in the year 1277 Hijri. The Shaykh is buried in the Baqee' graveyard, close to the grave of Hadhrat Uthmaan radhiallah anhu.

name: Hadhrat Daust Muhammad Qandhaari Rahmatullah Alayh
biography: Hadhrat Haaji Dawst Muhammad Saahib was a great and perfect Khaleefah of Hadhrat Shah Ahmad Sa'eed. From his early days as a student, the Shaykh had a keen desire to meet the friends of Allah, so whenever he heard someone being praised, he would go out to meet them in person. After acquiring formal religious knowledge, the Shaykh departed on a journey to find the friends of Allah. He sat in numerous gatherings and in the company of many Shaykhs, but wherever he went, he never felt at peace. On his journey to the Haramayn Shareefayn, the Shaykh stopped in Bombay and sat in the company of Hadhrat Shah Abu Sa'eed rahmatullah alayhi, and he also made bay'ah at his hand. Hadhart Shah Abu Sa'eed directed the Shaykh to go to Dehli and sit in the company of Hadhrat Shah Ahmad Sa'eed rahmatullah alayhi. The Shaykh went to Dehli, where he made bay'ah and stayed for a while. He acquired all the stages of Sulook during this time. His love and Ishq for his Shaykh was so immense that words cannot describe it. He often used to weep and cry while holding his Shaykh’s shoes to his face. He was a humble man and would clean the toilets with his own hands. His Shaykh used to make mention of the perfection of his state. He once said, "I have seen myself in a dream applying perfume to you from my bottle of Itr (perfume)." His Shaykh gave him permission in all of the four Silsilahs, and the Silsilah achieved untold popularity and publicity through the Shaykh. There are no limits to the Kashf and Karamaats attributed to the Shaykh, and he left behind hundreds of Khaleefahs and hundreds of thousands of Mureeds.

name: Hadhrat Muhammad Usman Damaani Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Hadhrat Shaykh was born on a Saturday evening, just after Maghrib, at Kalaachi in an area called Loni, in the district of Dera Isma'eel Khan. After acquiring the knowledge of the Deen, the love for the friends of Allah found its way into the heart of the Shaykh. It was this love that led him to search for a Shaykh, and he found a true man called Hadhrat Shaykh Dawst Muhammad Qandhari rahmatullah alayhi. He sat in the company of this Shaykh, and made bay'ah at his hand. After making bay'ah, he spent the rest of his life in the service of his Shaykh. He had unlimited and immense love for his Shaykh. He would always have his mind on serving his Shaykh, and this was all that worried him. He was invariably busy in doing the work of the Khanqah. When Hadhrat Shaykh Dawst Muhammad was in his last days, he called for the Shaykh and appointed him as his Khaleefah. Three years later, the Shaykh set off on the journey to perform Hajj at the House of Allah. After performing the Hajj, the Shaykh came to Madinah Munawwarah. On reaching the blessed city, the Shaykh was so overcome with the love for Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, that everywhere he looked all he could see was visions of the blessed Habeeb sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. During his stay, the Shaykh stopped eating and drinking, and he kept this up for eleven days, after which he departed on his return journey. The Shaykh travelled to many places for the purpose of Tableegh (propagating Islam). People from many different cities took bay'ah at his hand, people from far off lands such as Khurasaan and also places such as Daamaan. Hadhrat Shaykh used to emphasise strongly the importance of following the Sunnah and Shari'ah, and he liked very much those who were steadfast in following the Shari'ah and Sunnah. The Shaykh used to give advice people who visited the Khanqah and stayed there for a while. He would tell them to be steadfast in offering Tahajjud prayer and in doing the abundant dhikr of Allah, and also taught them the manners regarding their stay at the Khanqah. The Shaykh would often say, “My friends, as long as Allah gives you life, keep on doing His dhikr, for it is only with Allah's dhikr that the heart can be cleaned and purified.” The Shaykh was such a humble man that even though he was a learned scholar who acted upon his knowledge, he never issued a single fatwa. He would say, "I am a Darwesh, and the issuing of fatwas is a job for the Muftis." The Shaykh had his own library of books, containing a collection so great that no other library in the Punjab or India could compare with it. The Shaykh used to say, "My friends, the time you spend in this temporary life is very precious. Do not waste this time in neglect. Keep yourselves busy in Allah's dhikr at all times. Be aware! Let not even a moment be spent in neglect, for if it is, then you will regret it in the Hereafter, and it will also result in nothing but disappointment, and despair will come your way." The Shaykh also used to say, “This World is a stop on a journey; the true homeland is the Aakhirah."

The Shaykh also stated, "Do not grieve over anything except the Deen. You should not be deficient in fulfilling the obligations of the Deen, no matter how many hardships you may have to suffer." On the 19th of Rajab, the Shaykh fell very ill, and left this finite world a month later, just after sunrise on Tuesday the 22nd of Sha'baan 1314 AH. At the time of his death, the whole body of the Shaykh was doing dhikr. With his last breath, the Shaykh uttered the Kalimah Tayyibah (Laa ilaha illallahu Muhammad-ur-Rasoolullah). Before his death, the Shaykh said, “Look at my state. Where has my active body gone? What has happened to my cheerful talk? Where has my strength gone? Be aware, be aware! Take a lesson from this state of mine." Subhanallah, these were the last words of that great friend of Allah, who described the reality of this Dunya whilst he was leaving it.

name: Hadhrat Siraajuddeen Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Hadhrat Siraaj-ud-deen Sahib rahmatullah alayhi was born at Moosa Zai Shareef in the district of Dera Ismaeel Khan, in the year 1297 Hijri. Hadhrat Shaykh was educated by the best Islamic teachers of his time, and he learnt the knowledge of Tasawwuf from his father, Hadhrat Khwaja Muhammad Uthman Sahib rahmatullah alayhi. Once the Shaykh had completed his studies of both Zahiri (outer) and Baatini (inner) knowledge, his father performed the ceremony of Dastaar Bandi (spiritual graduation). After the Fajr prayer, a gathering of Dhikr Khatm-e-Khwaajigaan Naqshbandiah Mujaddidiah was held at the blessed shrine of Hadhrat Dawst Muhammad Qandhari rahmatullah alayhi. Afterwards, everyone who was there read the Qur'an individually. In total, three readings of the Qur'an were completed. After the Khatam, Hadhrat Khwaja Uthman Daamaani rahmatullah alayhi directed his attention towards the shrine of Hadhrat Dawst Muhammad Qandhari rahmatullah alayhi and supplicated to Allah for a long time. The effect of the Du'a was such that some of the people present fell into a state of Jadhb (rapture). Like his father, the Shaykh made unquantifiable efforts in the work of spreading the Deen. With rations of food and drink loaded onto camels for their journeys, he would travel from place to place with his Jama'at and propagate Islam. At times during these travels, people would invite the Shaykh to their homes for meals and so on. the Shaykh would reply, "My friends, Allah has provided this faqeer with all that he needs. I invite you towards Allah's dhikr. Come to me - you may eat, drink and then also do the dhikr of Allah in abundance!" Wave upon wave of people came into the service of the Shaykh and took Bay'ah. The flood of people who busied themselves in Allah's dhikr was so great that the Khanqah was always overflowing with dhaakireen. The Shaykh's fame became so widespread that he was well known in the streets of big cities and towns as well as those of small villages. By sitting in his company, people’s hearts were filled with Allah's Noor. Many thieves and bandits repented from their sins and busied themselves in Allah's dhikr. The Fayz from the Shaykh was

so powerful that people would rise in spiritual status just through coming under his blessed gaze. If ever a cry came from the Shaykh's mouth, many of those present would lose themselves in ecstasy, and they would remain in a state of Jadhb and unconsciousness for hours on end. A yearning desire to visit the Rawdah of the Beloved of the Lord of the Worlds salallahu alayhi wasallam resided in the heart of the Shaykh. So, accompanied by a few friends, the Shaykh undertook the journey to the House of Allah for Hajj. The blessings and events that occurred during that journey are so phenomenal that they cannot be described in words. The Shaykh lost all self-consciousness as soon as he set foot in Madinah Munawwarah. On one day during the stay in Madinah, the Shaykh performed an act the significance of which only he was aware of. He performed Ghusl, then changed from his clothes into a new Arab garment. With the sleeve of the right arm left hanging, the Shaykh lit a candle and held it in his hand. In this manner, he entered the blessed Rawdah and wept for a long time as he made supplication. With utmost respect, reverence and humility, the Shaykh then returned to his residence, changed back into his own clothes and returned the Arab dress to those who served him. On the last day of the stay, with tears flowing from his eyes, the Shaykh placed the dust from the blessed Rawdah into his eyes as surmah and made his farewell salaam before leaving Madinah to begin the journey home. The Shaykh passed away on Friday the 26th of Rabi al-Awwal 1333 AH. The enlightened grave of the Shaykh is in Moosa Zai, Dera Ismaeel Khan. May Allah shower hundreds and thousands of mercies upon his blessed grave. The following is a saying of the Shaykh: "To rid our hearts from the incitements of Shaytaan, we should remain busy in the dhikr of the heart. Make your body attentive towards your hearts and make your hearts attentive towards Allah. The true benefit of dhikr is only obtained through having sincerity and love for your Shaykh." The Shaykh also said, "Tasawwuf contains countless aspects that are thinner than the thickness of a hair. A person should never think that any ordinary person could become a Qalandar (true sufi) just by wearing the attire of Tasawwuf." Hadhrat Shaykh stated, "He who is busy (in Allah's dhikr) is accepted; and the one who is oblivious is far from acceptance." Hadhrat Shaykh also stated, "After thirty years, I have learnt that one moment that is spent in Allah's remembrance is better than having a kingdom like that of Sulaymaan alayhi salaam." Hadhrat Shaykh also used to say, "The key to Tasawwuf is steadfastness upon the Shari'ah of Mustafa salallahu alayhi wasallam." On another occasion, Hadhrat Shaykh stated, "When a person is alone and does Muraqaba dhikr in the morning and evening, he should cry to his Lord for forgiveness with humility, and should remain anxious and concerned over his deeds. This is because Rasoolullah salallahu alayhi wasallam would always be concerned and sorrowful." The Shaykh also stated, "The true purpose of becoming a Mureed is to seek the Path. It is waajib to seek the Path and this is evident from the Qur'an revealed by Allah ta'ala. O Muslims, adopt complete Taqwah and fear Allah! It is clear from the verses of the Qur'an that it is essential to adopt Taqwah."

name: Hadhrat Fazal Ali Shah Qureshi Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
The ancestors of Hadhrat Ghareeb Nawaz Khwaja Fazal Ali Qurayshi rahmatullah alayhi migrated with the Abbasi Yalghar from Arabia to Sindh, and then from there they moved on to settle in the district of Mianwali. Their settlement became famous as Da'ood Kheyl. Due to being of Abbasi and of Hashimi descent, the Shaykh's family was called Qurayshi by the people. The Shaykh was born at Da'ood Kheyl in the year 1270 Hijri. He spent the early years of his life in Kala Baagh, where he received education up to Sharh Waqaya and Sharh Jaami (key commentaries in Islamic law). Among his teachers were Hadhrat Maulana Qamar-ud-din Sahib and Maulana Ahmad Ali Sahib Saharanpuri, with whom he studied the books and Hadeeth. From an early age, the Shaykh had a fond desire to raise a parrot and train it to say good things. But a voice from the unseen said to him, "Teaching a parrot will not be of as much benefit as teaching the creation of Allah (Man). The heart is Allah’s parrot that should be brought towards His dhikr." Thus a desire to find a Kaamil Shaykh was born in his heart. The Shaykh was still in his youth when he came into the service and company of Hadhrat Khwaja Muhammad Uthman Damaani rahmatullah alayhi. Hadhrat Uthmaan Damaani rahmatullah alayhi sent the Shaykh to his first Khaleefah, Hadhrat Sayyid La'al Shah Sahib rahmatullah alayhi, at whose hand the Shaykh took Bay'ah for the first time. His path of Sulook, however, was not yet finished when Hadhrat La'al Shah Sahib rahmatullah alayhi passed away. The Shaykh then went into the presence and service of Hadhrat Khwaja Siraaj-ud-din rahmatullah alayhi in Moosa Zai Shareef. Hadhrat Siraj-ud-din rahmatullah alayhi taught the Shaykh dhikr from the beginning, and took him through all the Asbaaq (stages). On the occasion of Hadhrat Khwaja Siraajuddin having to go to Delhi for medical treatment, he sent for the Shaykh by letter. It was then that the Shaykh was given Khilafah, near the area of Chitley, a place blessed with the shrines of Hadhrat Mirza Mazhar Jaane Jaanan rahmatullah alayhi, Hadhrat Shah Ghulam Ali rahmatullah alayhi and Hadhrat Shah Abu Sa'eed rahmatullah alayhi. After returning from this blessed journey, the Shaykh returned to live in Miskeenpur Shareef, and the creation of Allah began entering the Silsilah in large numbers. The Shaykh's Mureeds were characterised by great love and enthusiasm, and ignorant people began to spread rumours that the tapping of the tasbeeh by the Shaykh was some form of magic. But gradually, the same people who had harboured ill thoughts began taking Bay'ah at the Shaykh's hand, and soon the whole area was alight with the Haq of Allah's dhikr. It was not long before the effects of this spread across India and then rapidly to all corners of the Islamic world. Whilst ploughing the fields, Hadhrat Shaykh would do the dhikr of Ism-e-Dhaat (the name 'Allah') and do so with a tasbeeh in his hands. Often the number of times this dhikr was repeated would reach eighty thousand. He used to travel 250 miles by foot to sit in the service of his Shaykh, and on many occasions he would travel contentedly for a month or so on the provision of just 2 to 4 kilograms of food. On one occasion, he had only a few coins on his person, and on this journey the Shaykh

survived on a supply of carrots and chickpeas. But this hardship never limited the delight, happiness and joy that he felt upon seeing his Shaykh when he arrived at his destination. When the Shaykh tapped the beads on his tasbeeh, people would ask him, out of curiosity and sometimes with sarcasm, "What are you doing?" Hadhrat Shaykh would reply, "I am playing. I am an entertainer, so come to me and I shall show you how, then you too can play this game.” The Shaykh was granted many visions and Karaamaat (miracles) but his greatest karaamat was his steadfastness upon the Sunnah of Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wasallam. Once, the Shaykh was travelling by train and a fellow passenger on the train, who was a drunkard, a drug addict and a fornicator who neglected Salaah, happened to sit in his company. Before the journey was over, this person had become a Dhaakir and was drowned in the remembrance of Allah and Ism-e-Dhaat. The Shaykh often mentioned this story and would say, "This is how the dhikr of Allah purifies a person." Once the Shaykh was riding on a horse. As the horse was walking along, his hoof knocked against someone who was lying on the ground. At this, the Shaykh stopped, dismounted and said to the person, "Please forgive me; I am sorry that my horse has hurt you." The person replied, "No, I should be grateful to you, because when the hoof of your horse touched me, my heart began to busy itself in Allah's dhikr. I regard myself as very fortunate indeed." The Shaykh once said, "It was my habit to go out and look for firewood for cooking langar (food) for the people who came for dhikr. One day, I came across a small twig and, seeing that it was too small, I did not pick it up. Allah ta'ala gave that twig the strength to speak, and it spoke saying, ‘Allah ta'ala says that He will reward a person for his every good deed, even if it is equivalent to that of a particle. But you have not even considered me equal to a particle.’ Upon hearing the twig, I felt very embarrassed and picked it up with the rest.” On an another occasion, the Shaykh said, "I was once collecting date stones for the Khatam. I left one date stone because it was not smooth and stuck out from the rest. The date stone addressed me and said, 'O beautiful one! If I am unsightly, then it is my Creator who has made me like this, and yet you find faults in me. If you have the power, then why not make me beautiful as you would like me to be.’” The Shaykh then said, "Upon hearing the words of the date stone, I began to cry. I kissed it and placed it with the rest, and whenever I came across it during a Khatam, I would kiss it again." One day a large number of people learnt dhikr from the Shaykh and repented from their sins. At night on the same day, Shaytaan appeared in his dream and said to him, "Why do you have so much enmity for me that you have stolen people from me who have been my mureeds for many years?" The Shaykh replied, " Insha'Allah I shall rescue many more people from your lure." The Shaykh said, "One day I was reciting the Qur'an, and my hands were placed on my foot. A heard a voice from the Lord saying, ‘When you are reciting the Qur'an, do not place your hands on such a place.’ Ever since that day, whenever I am going to recite the Qur'an, I first cover my feet with a cloth." One afternoon, the Shaykh had a dream in which he heard the recitation: "Man yuti ishaykh faqad ataa arRasool wa man yuti arRasoola faqad ataa' Allah." (He who followed his Shaykh has followed the Rasool Salallahu alayhi wasallam and he who followed the Rasool Salallahu alayhi wasallam has obeyed Allah).

When the Shaykh used to do dhikr in a gathering on hard land that needed ploughing, many large and hard stones would just crumble and become fine earth. Hadhrat Shaykh would smile and say, "Allah has saved this old man from ploughing the fields and has made my work easy for me!" The following is a saying of the Shaykh: "Four things elevate a person: First, abundance of dhikr; Second, aherence to the Sunnah; Thirdly, refraining from sins; and fourthly, connection with his Shaykh." He also said, “When I first decided to look for a Shaykh, I had a dream for 15 nights consecutively in which I saw a man who was not following the Shari'ah. I realised that this was Shaytaan. So beware! If you wish to find a Shaykh, then make sure that he is a person of the Shari'ah, for if he is not then he can be worse for you than Shaytaan." Hadhrat Shaykh said, "The friends of Allah put great emphasis on doing the dhikr of Allah because the benefits of it are everlasting and permanent." Hadhrat Shaykh also stated, "If you wish to understand the Qur'an, then adopt Taqwa." His last journey to Delhi was one of Tableegh, and during the trip, Hadhrat Shaykh fell very ill and was escorted back to Miskeenpur Shareef. On Thursday, which was the last night before the month of Ramadhan 1354 Hijri (28th November 1935) at the age of 84, Hadhrat Shaykh left this finite world for that which lasts forever. Hadhrat Shaykh's shrine is situated in Miskeenpur Shareef, which is in the district of Muzaffargarh. The Khulafa of the Shaykh numbered 66, and the light of Allah's dhikr continues to spread across the world due to the efforts of these pious people. There is a yearly gathering in Miskeenpur Shareef to commemorate the Shaykh. Thousands of people attend this gathering and obtain spiritual Fayz.

name: Hadhrat Sheikh Ali Murtaza Rahmatullah Alayh
biography:
Hadhrat Shaykh's homeland was Gadai, Dera Ghazi Khan, and he was born in the year 1907 AD. Hadhrat Sahib's father, Hadhrat Maulana Allama Muhammad Hussain Sahib nawwarAllahu marqadah, was a great Darwesh and Aalim who studied Ahadeeth in Bhopal under Shaykh Bin Muhsin Yamani (1245 - 1329 Hijri). Hadhrat Sahib therefore learnt and became qualified in Ahadeeth from being taught by his father, who studied at various places including Bhopal and Hyderabad Dakkan. After a certain time, his father adopted poverty and a simple way of life, and returned to live in Gadai, which was his fatherland. Here he continued to teach, without any charge, until his last breath. He also used to work as a shepherd, herding goats, and he had three sons who were all people of knowledge, one of whom was our blessed Shaykh. His grandfathers and great grandfathers were also all pious people. Hadhrat Sahib was an exceptional scholar, and acquired formal knowledge of the Islamic Sciences from his father. He mastered Tafseer, Ahadeeth, Fiqh, Mantaq and Philosophy, as well as completing Hifz of the Qur’an. He learnt Tajweed and Qiraa'at from Qari Abdul 'Aleem in Saharanpur. Among his teachers were Hadhrat Mawlana Khaleel Ahmad Sahib Saharanpuri, Mawlana Thaabit Ali Sahib, Mawlana Abd-ul-Lateef Sahib, Mawlana Waahid Bakhsh Sahib, and

Mawlana Muhammad Siddeeq Sahib. In addition to this, he also received lessons on Hadeeth from Hadhrat Mawlana Muhammad Yahya Sahib, who was the father of his class-fellow Hadhrat Shaykh-ul-Hadeeth Sahib nawwarAllahu Marqadah. Hadhrat Shaykh memorised the Qur'an in seven months. Until his last breath, he never got mixed up whilst reciting similar verses from fifteen chapters of the Holy Qur'an. During his last year of acquiring formal knowledge, Hadhrat Shaykh felt an intense need to acquire Batini knowledge (inner knowledge). He attached himself to Qibla-e-Aaalam, Qutb-ul-Irshad, Hadhrat Mawlana Fadhal Ali Sahib Qurayshi nawwarAllahu Marqadah, who was a Saint of the Naqshbandi order. Hadhrat Sahib's love for his Shaykh was very great indeed. Every other week he would travel by foot from Gadai to Miskeenpur Shareef. On his journey, he would cross the River Sindh and would then reach Miskeenpur to be in the presence of the Shaykh by noon on the following day. It was the Hukm of Hadhrat Shaykh that he was not to get involved in any kind of chit chat or worldly discussion on these journeys. This was a time of great poverty for Hadhrat Shaykh. He would invariably have only one coin with which to pay the fare for the boat to cross the river. After staying for two days, he would return home. This remained his habit year after year. He received permission in all the Silsilahs from His Shaykh, but the dominant silsilah was Naqshbandiah. When Hadhrat Shaykh was in his last stages of acquiring the Zahiri and Baatini Knowledge, his father passed away. Hadhrat Shaykh had to take a loan in order to prepare his father's burial. Poverty did not affect or shake the steadfastness of Hadhrat Shaykh. He always worked, sewing clothes and working in a library containing religious books. He continued to deliver lessons on Deen free of charge, and the gatherings of Allah's dhikr and shukr were always held. Gatherings of Muraqabah Dhikr would take place daily, after morning Salaah for one hour, and after Maghrib Salaah for twenty minutes, both of which would end with Du'a. On Friday night (Thursday evening), Hadhrat would give a talk after the gathering for Muraqabah Dhikr. Hadhrat Shaykh went for Hajj on fourteen occasions, the first of which was completed in 1357 AH. On this occasion, it happened that Hadhrat Shaykh had only seventy rupees with him. An event occurred on this first Hajj when Hadhrat Shaykh was at the blessed shrine of Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam conveying his farewell salaam. At that moment, a voice came from the blessed shrine saying, “'Awdan, 'Awdan” (‘Return, return.’) This was good news and an invitation for Hadhrat Shaykh to come again. And so it came to pass, for Hadhrat Shaykh returned for Hajj the following year. Hadhrat Shaykh performed their last Umrah in Ramadhan al-Mubarak 1402 AH and their last Hajj was also performed in the same year. Hadhrat Shaykh had a very great status indeed. Despite his station, he would not show anything. Once, during a visit to the blessed shrine of Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, a voice replied to him from the shrine. On another occasion, Hadhrat Shaykh did not have enough money to cover the cost of staying in Madeenah Munawwarah, and he had been without food for a few days. Then, in a dream, Hadhrat Shaykh did Ziyaarah of Rasoolullah sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, who said to him, “Whose guest are you?”. He replied, “I am your guest, O Messenger of Allah”. Rasoolullah sallallahu alayhi wa sallam then placed something in his hand. When Hadhrat Shaykh awoke, he opened his hand to find a Riyaal in it.

During his last days, Hadhrat Shaykh began to say things that made it clear he was close to separating from this world. A close friend had a dream in which he saw that two of the minarets of the Haram in Makkah had fallen down. Hadhrat Shaykh explained the dream, saying that soon an irreplaceable Friend of Allah would pass away. And this is exactly what happened. On Saturday the 25th of Shawwal 1408AH, he parted from thousands of loving followers. At the time of his death, there was a smile on his face and the index finger of his right hand was pointing straight ahead. It was the wish of Hadhrat Shaykh that he be buried at the place where the people took off their shoes for prayer. His Kafan was his Ihraam cloths of many years. In his last sermon, on the night of Friday 24th Shawwal, Hadhrat Shaykh said, “He who has purified his Nafs is the successful one. An important reason behind Allah sending the Prophets is purification and the rectification of Manners. For the purification of the Nafs, three things are undertaken and one thing is abandoned. The things that are undertaken are the Dhikr of Allah, the following of the Sunnah and the acquisition of the company of a Shaykh; and the thing that is to be abandoned is Sin. The following of the Sunnah is Noor, and without light it is impossible to walk in the path. Without the Sunnah, Tareeqah becomes deception. Everything that a person needs becomes easy with love for your Shaykh.” There are fifty-nine Khaleefahs of Hadhrat Shaykh nawwarAllahu Marqadah, and they are spreading the blessings of Hadhrat Sahib throughout the world.

name:
Rahbarey Tareeqat, Muhiyyusunnah, Hadhrat Sheikh Asif Hussain Farooqui Naqshbandi
Mujaddidi Daamat Barakaatuhum
biography: The first point to note is that Hadhrat Shaykh’s family lineage contains many famous and influential figures from the history of Islam. The most important of these was the second of the Khulafaa Al-Raashideen, Umar Bin Khattaab RadhiAllahu Anh, known as ‘Al-Farooq’ due to his outstanding ability to distinguish right from wrong and truth from falsehood. From this title derives the family name. Of his other ancestors, Shaykh Ahmad Sarhindi Farooqui Rahmatullah Alayhi is the most prominent, known by the title of Al-Mujaddid Alf-Thani — the Renewer of the Millennium — for the profound reinvigoration which his teachings gave to the Ummah one thousand years after the time of our Prophet Sallallahu Alayhi Wa Sallam. Another great exponent of Islam, Baba Farid Shakur Ganj Rahmatullah Alayhi, is also a direct ancestor of Hadhrat Shaykh. In terms of the history of his own life, however, Hadhrat Shaykh was raised near Dera Ghazi Khan in Pakistan, and he had the great benefit of being brought up in a family of pious, practising Muslims. One incident from his childhood indicated, with hindsight, the path that Hadhrat Shaykh was later to tread. He was some nine years old at the time, and while walking near his home one day, he came upon an assembly of people gathered around a renowned Naqshbandi Shaykh. The Shaykh, who was known to be particular about whom he would accept as a pupil, suddenly summoned the surprised young boy from where he was standing at the edge of the gathering, took his hand, and asked him to repeat the Oath of Allegiance to him — the Bay’ah. Hadhrat Shaykh never met him again and put the incident to the back of his mind. Hadhrat Shaykh’s outlook towards ‘Pirs’ and people claiming to be Sufis was generally not favourable in his youth, for his intelligence and education helped him to realise that most of these were simply making a living out of the hopes and fears of people with a limited knowledge of the Deen. But from an early age, he had realised that there was more to life than success in worldly matters, and his love for Islam, together with his awareness from the knowledge of Qur’an of the excellence of the people of Taqwah (fear of Allah), gave him a strong desire to meet and learn from someone with the true characteristics of a Muslim — someone truly orientated towards Allah and His Prophet SalAllahu Alayhi Wa Sallam. Hadhrat Shaykh had for many years been interested in poetry, and at about this time he began composing verses in celebration of the Prophet SalAllahu Alayhi Wa Sallam. It was not long before a strong desire awakened in him to perform Umrah and pay his respects at Masjid Al-Nabawi. He was not yet thirty years old when he set out on this pilgrimage, the first stage of a four-month period that changed his life completely. Hadhrat Shaykh’s first experience of Madinah came late one evening after arriving by bus from Makkah, his Umrah completed. He went straight to Masjid Al-Nabawi, where the people were leaving the mosque after Isha Salah. The building was a fraction of its present size, and the authorities were preparing to close it for the night, as they still do except during Ramadan. Since it was his first visit, Hadhrat Shaykh was unaware of this, and he walked in unnoticed by the guards and went straight to the Tomb of the Prophet Sallallahu Alayhi Wa Sallam to present himself and give Salaam. For a full half an hour, he stood undisturbed in that blessed place, silently contemplating the greatness of the company that he had the opportunity to keep. Some days later, again while sitting in the immediate vicinity of the Rawdha Mubarak (the Blessed Tomb), he was approached by a tall African man, strikingly dressed in white, with a turban on his head. Hadhrat Shaykh was surprised to see a chapati being held out to him, with the man urging him to eat. “Though I was hungry,” recalls Hadhrat Shaykh, “I was worried that it might be contrary to the etiquette of that great place to accept the offer, so I declined.” The stranger persisted with the offer and was again declined, upon which a second person walked up, resplendent in the clothing of the Sunnah, whose Surma-shaded eyes were brimming with tears beneath his beautiful green turban. He addressed Hadhrat Shaykh in Siraiki, which is a dialect spoken only in the area around Multan in Pakistan: “My son,” he said, “never refuse the provision of Allah Ta’ala.” With that, he took the bread from the African, tore it in two, handed one half to Hadhrat Shaykh and, with the other half in his own hand, departed as suddenly as he had come. Hadhrat Shaykh was amazed and resolved always to be ready to avail himself of true spiritual sustenance. He prayed for the opportunity to be offered it by such sincere servants of Allah Ta’ala. Some days later, he met the African man again, who seemed to recognise this desire in him, and advised Hadhrat Shaykh to go back to his homeland and travel to a place called Gadai. Hadhrat Shaykh had planned to visit his family after the Umrah trip in any case, and his father had heard of Gadai since it was not far from Dera Ghazi Khan, though he knew nothing about the place that would merit a visit. Hadhrat Shaykh, too, did not know what he might find there, but he had made up his mind to follow the advice that he had received, and so he set out one morning on his quest. Someone he spoke to along the way told him of a Shaykh in the village who could always be found in his Khanqah, sitting with his head bowed in the remembrance of Allah. At around the time of Salat Al-Asr, Hadhrat Shaykh arrived at the Khanqah. He described the sight that met his eyes as he entered the dusky interior thus: “The Mureeds were seated in a circle around their Shaykh. All were dressed in white, with turbans on their heads, and their full-bearded faces were lowered in contemplation; the peace and respect radiating out from the group was overwhelming. Hadhrat Shaykh himself had a white Chaadar (winding sheet) wrapped around him, and the serenity that shone out from his face seemed to light up my heart, and I knew that I had found what I had been looking for. As I took in this captivating sight, Hadhrat Shaykh looked up at me, smiled and stood up, greeting me as if he knew me, despite the incongruity of my Western clothes and clean-shaven face in such company.” The two then sat down together, and the Shaykh enquired as to what assistance he could offer. When Hadhrat Shaykh explained about his search for the way to acquire the Pleasure of Allah Ta’ala and live his life in His remembrance and service, his host was delighted and said: “For seventy years this Faqeer has sat and waited for someone to come to me with an intention as pure and sincere as this! My son, I will guide you towards your goal, and soon, InshaAllah, you yourself will be a guide on this path.” That Shaykh was none other than Qutb Al-Irshad, Arif-Billah Hadhrat Shaykh Ali Murtaza Sahib Rahmatullah Alayhi. He himself had received Khilafah (permission) to continue the work of the Shaykhs of Silsilah Naqshbandia Mujaddidia from the renowned and highly influential Shaykh Fazal Ali Qurayshi Rahmatullah Alayh, and was his last surviving Khalifah. Shaykh Ali Murtaza Sahib had himself received full permission to teach from the streams of the four Silsilahs (Qaadriya, Chisthiya, Suhurwardia, Naqshbandia). Although highly qualified in the sciences of Islamic scholarship and a Hafidh of Qur’an, Shaykh Ali Murtaza Sahib Rahmatullah Alayhi used to say that the role of the ‘Ulamaa (scholars) is like that of people who make sweets, meaning all the many rulings and definitions of the Shari’ah, whilst the role of the Sufis is to instil in people the taste for those sweets, and that it was the latter role for which he had been chosen. He was meticulous in his observance of the Sunnah, a striking feature of the Mashaykh of Silsilah Naqshbandia Mujaddidia, and his personal humility combined in a marvellous way with the authority of his evident piety and Taqwa, so that he invariably had a lasting impact on those who met him. As a result, he had thousands of Mureeds who benefited from his guidance. Hadhrat Shaykh spent the next three months in the company of his Shaykh, receiving close attention and intensive instruction in all matters relating to the Deen, and when the time came for him to return to England, he was given permission to teach and invite people towards the Dhikr of Allah Ta’ala. Hadhrat Shaykh met with Shaykh Ali Murtaza Sahib Rahmatullah Alayhi every year after this, usually when his Shaykh went to the Haramain (the two Holy Places of Makkah and Madinah), which, by the Grace of Allah Ta’ala, he visited every year to perform either Hajj or Umrah. They also communicated constantly by letter, and within a very short time, Shaykh Ali Murtaza Sahib bestowed Hadhrat Shaykh with Khilafah (permission to give Bay’ah and guidance to Seekers) in all four of the Silsilahs of the Tariqah Naqshbandia Mujaddidia, having taken him through all the lessons and stages of the Silsilah. His other Mureeds were surprised at the speed with which Hadhrat Shaykh had traversed this path — which most do not achieve in a lifetime — and asked Shaykh Ali Murtaza Sahib why he gave Hadhrat Shaykh such close attention. “Farooqui Sahib has killed his Nafs”, was the simple reply. His friends and family recognised this as well, for Hadhrat Shaykh had lost all normal inclinations to frivolity and the attractions of the world, and had become immersed in the ways of the Sunnah and in steadfast devotion. An indication of the effect that this change had on those close to him is that his best friend, with whom he had previously spent time in worldly amusements, became one of his first Mureeds; and his family were also quick to take advantage of the auspicious change that they could see taking place in Hadhrat Shaykh. The Sunnah of earning Halal provisions for one’s dependants was not neglected, however, and despite his commitment to his hundreds of Mureeds worldwide, he continued to oversee his business. In 1994, the current premises of Khanqah Naqshbandia Mujaddidia were acquired to accommodate the ever-expanding numbers attending Jumu’ah and the assemblies of Dhikrullah. Hadhrat Shaykh’s emphasis on the importance of dressing according to the Sunnah is a central element of his teaching, though, of course, the necessity of combining this with the Sunnah of good manners and character, as well as Taqwah, sincerity and love in worship, is also continuously stressed. Hadhrat Shaykh’s own example shows that through incorporating the Sunnah into every area of one’s life, and by combining this with abundant Dhikrullah and the company of the Friends of Allah, a person can be graced with Allah’s Pleasure and nearness. Hadhrat Shaykh explains that the mark of a true Sufi is one whose daily life and worldly dealings are comprehensively imbued with the Shariah and Sunnah, for nearness to Allah Ta’ala is impossible to acquire by any other means. In both word and deed, he makes clear that at every step in life, the Sunnah provides opportunities to turn everyday activities into acts of worship and remembrance. The essential and indisputable Truth of this message can be gauged by the fact that his Mureeds have come from a wide range of the groups and sects that divide the Muslims today. Until this day, Hadhrat Shaykh holds Majaalis-e-Dhikr every morning and evening, Alhamdulillah, and has many Mureeds worldwide. The gatherings are streamed via the Dhikr website — sufi.org.uk. Daamat Barakaatuhum — may Allah Ta’ala ever prolong and increase the blessings that He delivers through Hadhrat Shaykh!
